## 3. Catarina's Success

I am part of a volunteering project which intends to help teenagers from academically disadvantaged backgrounds get support through their academic experience. For 2 years, my mentee was a 15-year old Portuguese girl who had fallen a few academic years behind and now is enrolled on a vocational bridging course designed to enable progression to sixth form. She has just passed the course, which means she can now progress to sixth form/college!  
I think this is the experience I want to share.

## 4. The administration's failure to provide adequate service to citizens.

Well, the other day I went to submit the paperwork to get married in a civil ceremony at the Madrid Civil Registry. They don't have an appointment available until November, even though my ceremony is in August. It would make sense to get married a few days earlier to avoid problems with my employer and the 15 days of honeymoon they're supposed to give me. Not only are they slow, but they also close the Civil Registry in August. August is when most people get married, so what's the point? Clearly, the administration isn't working to meet the needs of the citizens. A worse relationship with the administration means a worse democracy.

<u>Original title (es)</u> : El NO servicio al ciudadano de la administración

<u>Original content (es)</u> :

No solo es que van lentos, sino que además cierran en Agosto la Admnistración. En agosto es cuando más se casa la gente, ¿qué sentido tiene eso? Ahí la administración no está trabajando de cara a la necesidad del ciudadano, evidentemente. Peor relación con la administración, peor democracia.

## 6. Return from Ukraine

For the past three years, I have lived in Ukraine with my wife, both of us working for humanitarian organizations. We moved there after the Russian invasion began in 2022, and a few months ago we returned to Spain. Upon returning to the EU, I clearly felt a widespread lack of understanding and concern for the issue of Ukraine, the reality and consequences of the war, Europe's role and responsibility in this war, and the lives of the hundreds of thousands of Ukrainian refugees in Europe. Aside from a few exceptions and specific contexts, I find it difficult to understand—and partly accept—this low level of engagement, information, and activity, even indirect or merely emotional, among so many people in the place where I live. I also find the response and determination of most European institutions in seeking a solution utterly inadequate.

<u>Original title (it)</u> : Ritorno dall'Ucraina

<u>Original content (it)</u> :

Negli ultimi 3 anni ho vissuto in Ucraina, con mia moglie, lavorando entrambi per organizzazioni umanitarie. Ci siamo trasferiti lì dopo l'inizio dell'invasione da parte della Russia nel 2022, e qualche mese fa siamo tornati in Spagna. Al ritorno in UE, ho chiaramente sentito una generalizzata mancanza di comprensione ed attenzione per il tema dell'Ucraina, della realtà e conseguenze della guerra, per il ruolo e la responsabilità dell'Europa in questa guerra e per la vita delle centinaia di migliaia di rifugiati ucraini in Europa. Al di là di alcune eccezioni, ed alcuni contesti particolari, trovo difficile capire - e in parte accettare - questo basso livello di coinvolgimento, informazione e attività, anche indiretti o solamente emotivi, di tante delle persone nel posto in cui vivo, così come trovo la risposta e determinazione della maggior parte delle istituzioni europee nel cercare una soluzione, assolutamente insufficiente.

## 8. Ecological shortsightedness of industries and workers.

For years, I have been fighting against the fact that in industries and workplaces, the bare minimum is done to protect the health and safety of workers, environmental impact is neglected, and European regulations are considered a bureaucratic burden and a drag on profits. The reality is that these rules protect everyone, yet those directly affected seem unaware of the risks and damage they cause to the environment, to others, and, above all, to themselves.  
  
Workers themselves aren't concerned about this situation, and even when they are empowered to perform well, they tend to operate without the safety measures provided.  
  
In other words, there is a lack of culture and awareness, and widespread shortsightedness regarding workplace safety and health.

<u>Original title (it)</u> : Miopia ecologica delle industrie e dei lavoratori.

<u>Original content (it)</u> :

Da anni combatto contro il fatto che nelle industrie e sui luoghi di lavoro si faccia il minimo possibile per tutelare la sicurezza e la salute dei lavoratori, si trascura l'impatto ambientale e si considerano le normative europee un peso burocratico ed una zavorra al profitto. La realtà è che queste regole tutelano tutte le persone, ma sembra che i diretti interessati non si rendano conto dei rischi e dei danni che arrecano all'ambiente, agli altri, ma soprattutto a se stessi.  
  
Gli stessi lavoratori non si preoccupano di questa situazione e, anche quando li metti in condizione di lavorare bene, tendenzialmente operano senza le sicurezze fornite.  
  
In altre parole, c'è una mancanza di cultura e di consapevolezza ed una miopia diffusa sul tema della sicurezza e della salute sui luoghi di lavoro.

<u>Origin</u> : Italy  
<u>Language</u> : it  
<u>Unique identifier</u> : IT_pmt_sp  
<u>EU is like</u> : the compass that indicates the correct way to manage this problem.

## 12. Precarious employment assured

University researchers work in a state of constant precariousness. In recent years, several reforms have attempted to improve job security for these individuals. However, policymakers have proven incapable of addressing this precariousness, or even intent on exacerbating it. This situation makes university research in Italy an unattractive occupation for few people (those who can afford to spend 10-15 years of their career in a state of uncertainty). This condition slows down social development and innovation.

<u>Original title (it)</u> : Precariato assicurato

<u>Original content (it)</u> :

Il personale ricercatore all'interno dell'università lavora in uno stato di costante precariato. Negli ultimi anni, alcune riforme hanno teso a migliorare la stabilità lavorativa di queste persone. Tuttavia,  la politica si dimostra incapace di risolvere questa precarietà o addirittura intenzionata ad accentuarla. Questa situazione rende la ricerca universitaria in Italia un impiego poco attrattivo e per poche persone (coloro che possono permettersi di trascorrere 10-15 anni della propria cariera in uno stato di incertezza). Questa condizione rallenta lo sviluppo e l'innovazione della società.

## 16. Deep state still holds true authority in the Republic of Cyprus

Our High Judicial Council decided not to hire a judge that was hired on probation for 2 years. This is the standard procedure. This decision is highly political since she was the judge responsible to re-examine the investigation into the death of a young man that was deemed to have committed suicide (no further investigation from the police) even though he was a highly religious person that had just whistle blown the distribution of drugs in his army garrisson. The case was reopened after 17 years when the family got a favourable court decision from the European Court of Human Rights, that deemed the investigation a joke. So this judge had the guts to deem the suicide a murder investigation and demand the re-opening of the case. Pressure was made towards her to change her decision, which was both illegal and unconstitutional. So they sacked her indirectly.

## 18. career advice

I have not transitioned into the workforce from STEaPP yet but I am working while studying and I found that STEaPP prides itself on supporting students in their endeavors but actually falls short of their own expectations. As a part-time student with a job, I've found that accommodations were not made and the structure of part-time studying is pushed to the side for certain opportunities. For instance, during guest workshops and panels, I had asked if the session could be recorded for those of us who had prior work obligations since they were outside of scheduled contact hours. These workshops were great for learning more about the workforce we are studying to enter and meeting/networking with experts and professionals in those spheres, but I was shut down about recording because it would be too difficult to get consent to record. In this sense, as a student who worked I was often, though not purposefully, locked out of networking and career informing opportunities.   
  
Another thing is that the career sessions I have attended seem very geared towards international students and what it means to stay in the UK rather than just career transitioning advice. Most of the discussion that wasn't basic brainstorming and glorified dream-boarding was centered around visa transitions, local salaries and cost of living comparisons, and other rather universal experiences. There was not much about targeted networking and STEaPP specific career fields.

## 31. Language Barrier

## 45. Political discourse in business

I'm thinking about the role of companies in a democracy. At my workplace, I've noticed that discussing political topics, for example during lunch breaks, isn't part of the culture. Even business matters are discussed purely in terms of their impact on the company – with little consideration given to the broader societal consequences. I find this regrettable. We spend so much time at work that it's like a mini-social space for us, and we often encounter people with different political views there (unlike perhaps in our circle of friends). Why not use these opportunities more to practice constructive discussion, to consider things from different perspectives, and to live democracy?

<u>Original title (de)</u> : Politischer Diskurs in der Wirtschaft

<u>Original content (de)</u> :

Ich mache mir Gedanken über die Rolle von Unternehmen in der Demokratie. An meinem Arbeitsplatz erlebe ich, dass es nicht Teil der Kultur ist, sich zB in der Mittagspause über politische Themen auszutauschen. Auch Geschäftsthemen werden rein auf Businessimpact diskutiert - und kaum die weiteren gesellschaftlichen Folgen mit betrachtet. Ich finde das schade. Wir verbringen so viel Zeit in der Arbeit, dass sie wie ein reduzierter Gesellschaftsraum ist für uns, und wir begegnen dort auch noch oft Menschen mit anderen politischen Einstellungen (anders als vielleicht im Freundeskreis). ## 48. Balance in ChatGPT usage

I use ChatGPT quite a lot in my daily life, for work, study, and quick daily questions. Many things simply go faster by letting ChatGPT write, summarize, or provide ideas "just like that." Due to my frequent use, I am afraid I will become dependent on it. Recently, I almost had an entire job application letter written by ChatGPT, which shocked me a bit. Because of this, I have been thinking more and more lately about not using it at all anymore, but precisely because it sometimes takes away work, I find it difficult to give it up. Moreover, this is simply the society we live in, so shouldn't we just learn to deal with it? And that is not even mentioning the other things that make me question my usage: the water consumption of this technology, the bias inherent in it, and the tech giants making money off it.

<u>Original title (nl)</u> : Balans in ChatGPT-gebruik

<u>Original content (nl)</u> :

Ik gebruik ChatGPT best veel in mijn dagelijks leven, voor werk, studie en dagelijkse snelle vragen. Veel dingen gaan nu eenmaal sneller door ChatGPT "even" te laten schrijven, samenvatten of ideeën te geven. Door het vele gebruik ben ik bang dat ik er afhankelijk van word. Laatst liet ik bijna een hele sollicitatiebrief door ChatGPT schrijven, daar schrok ik een beetje van. Hierdoor denk ik de laatste tijd steeds vaker over na het helemaal niet meer te gebruiken, maar juist omdat het soms ook werk wegneemt vind ik het moeilijk er afstand van te doen. Bovendien is dit nu eenmaal de maatschappij waarin we leven, dus moeten we niet ook gewoon leren ermee om te gaan? En dan hebben we het nog niet eens over de andere dingen die mij over mijn gebruik laten twijfelen: het waterverbruik van deze technologie, de bias die erin zit en de techgiganten die hier geld aan verdienen.

## 51. AI and the disappearing voices

## 62. Cycling in Munich

I cycle a lot around the city. There are places where it works really well – for example, on new, wide cycle paths, or those separated by bollards. But at many pillars, there are no cycle paths at all. On my commute, there's a cycle path on the road, but very often a car is parked there, and everyone has to swerve. Or it's complicated at construction sites – at the Maxmonument, there's currently no cycle path – actually, there isn't even a road. At Königsplatz, all cyclists recently had to dismount because of construction. At the same time, it's really lovely to cycle along the Isar River, undisturbed by the road. Or from the Friedensengel to Odeonsplatz, it's also great, well-developed – that's a wonderful cycling experience. A few more paths like that would be fantastic. Cycling could be given more consideration and made more attractive. Lots of people cycle anyway! But in some places, it's not made easy.

<u>Original title (de)</u> : Fahrrad fahren in München

<u>Original content (de)</u> :

Ich fahre viel mit dem Fahrrad durch die Stadt. Es gibt Orte an denen das sehr gut geht - zB an neuen breit ausgebauten Radwegen, oder welche die mit Bollern abgetrennt sind. Aber an vielen Stelen gibt es gar keine Fahrradwege. Auf meinem Arbeitsweg ist ein Fahrradweg auf der Straße, aber sehr häufig parkt dort ein Auto und alle müssen ausweichen. Oder bei Baustellen ist es kompliziert - am Maxmonument gibt es gerade keinen Fahrradweg - eigentlich auch keine Straße. Am Königsplatz mussten kürzlich alle Radfahrer absteigen wegen einer Baustelle. Gleichzeitig ist es voll schön zB an der Isar entlang zu fahren, ungestört von der Straße. Oder vom Friedensengel an den Odeonsplatz läuft es auch super, gut ausgebaut - das ist ein schönes Fahrraderlebnis. Ein paar mehr solcher Wege wären toll. Fahrradfahren könnte noch mehr mitgedacht und attraktiver gemacht werden. Es fahren eh viele Fahrrad! Aber es wird einem an manchen Stellen nicht ganz leicht gemacht.

## 66. Processing

As an East German, I like to recount the chaotic times of the 1990s: a period characterized above all by widespread uncertainty and the fact that nobody really knew "what to do." This complex situation created a toxic social climate. Many felt left behind, or indeed, fell through the cracks. I think people wished someone had explained the rules of the free world to them more clearly. Instead, they experienced little sense of self-efficacy: just muddling through, dropping out of school, starting an apprenticeship or not, and usually ending up with bad jobs. What's so remarkable about this is that the public narrative portrays reunification as an Elysian moment of liberation. The shift to the right and the deterioration of the political discourse don't add up in the light of this liberation narrative. In my view, it's important to be open to the perspective of many East Germans and not to label them as ungrateful or crazy.

<u>Original title (de)</u> : Aufarbeitung

<u>Original content (de)</u> :

Als Ostdeutscher erzähle ich gerne, welche chaotischen Zeiten in den 90ern herrschten: die Zeiten waren vor allem durch eine allgemeine große Unsicherheit gekennzeichnet und dadurch, dass niemand so richtig wusste „was man machen muss“. In dieser Gemengelage gab es ein toxisches gesellschaftliches Klima. Viele haben sich abgehängt gefühlt, bzw. sind auch tatsächlich durchs „Raster“ gefallen. Ich glaube, die Leute hätten sich gewünscht, dass ihn jemand die Regeln der freien Welt besser erklärt. Stattdessen wenig Selbstwirksamkeit: Vor sich hin machen, Schule abbrechen, Lehre machen oder nicht, meistens schlechte Jobs. Was daran so bemerkenswert ist, ist, dass das öffentlich narrativ die Wende als elysischen Befreiungsmoment charakterisiert. Der Rechtsruck und die Verwahrlosung des politischen Tons ergeben im Licht des Berfreiungsnarrativ keinen Sein. Es ist aus meiner Sicht wichtig offen für die Perspektive vieler Ostdeutscher zu sein und sie nicht als undankbar oder irre Abzustempeln

## 67. When will we start storing water?

Recently, a huge amount of EUR in my country was allotted to windmills. One of the reasons is that the money comes from the EU. A lot of focus is on building windmills - but not on storing the energy (on the infrastructure needed for storage and distribution).  
Seeing this, I'm shocked at the lack of attention on water storage. The weather is becoming more extreme: we experience both extreme droughts and extreme rains. Why is no one, at the national level, strategically thinking about the infrastructure that allows for storing the water (for drought times)?

## 70. Prejudices about state aid for foreigners

Very recently, a friend of mine, who isn't a French citizen, had to get a blood test. Even though he had a prescription, a simple blood test cost him €160. Normally, for a French citizen with a prescription, a blood test only costs between €17 and €25.  
  
Fortunately, my friend can afford this blood test, which he had no choice but to get. However, many foreigners in France wouldn't be able to afford such a sum, even for such vital and necessary treatment.  
  
Despite this, many people spread hateful rhetoric towards foreigners in France. They accuse them of coming to France and not paying anything, of "taking advantage of state aid," of being able to get "free" treatment in hospitals, and of therefore "exploiting" the system.  
  
However, this is far from the reality, but prejudices are so strong that they prevail over public opinion, which is reflected in the ballot box.

<u>Original title (fr)</u> : Les préjugés sur les aides d'Etat pour les étrangers

<u>Original content (fr)</u> :

Très récemment, un ami à moi, n'ayant pas la nationalité française, a dû aller faire une prise de sang. Alors même qu'il avait une ordonnance pour la faire, une simple prise de sang lui a couté 160€. Normalement, pour un ressortissant français avec une ordonnance, une prise de sang ne coûte qu'entre 17 et 25€.  
Heureusement, mon ami a les moyens de payer cette prise de sang qu'il n'avait pas le choix de faire. Cependant, de nombreux étrangers en France ne pourrait pas financer une telle somme, même pour des soins aussi vitaux et nécessaires.  
  
Malgré ça, de nombreuses personnes ont des discours haineux envers des personnes étrangères en France. Elles leur "reprochent" de venir en France et de ne rien payer, de "profiter des aides de l'Etat", de pouvoir se faire soigner "gratuitement" dans les hôpitaux et qu'ils "profitent" alors du système.  
Toutefois, cela est loin d'être la réalité, mais les préjugés sont si forts qu'ils l'emportent sur l'opinion publique, ce qui se répercute dans les urnes.

## 72. Unacceptable justification of my teacher for my oral marks

During my second year of bachelor's degree in law as an international student in France, despite my frequent participation and interest towards the class I wasn't satisfied with the oral mark I got from this class. ## 73. Resistance to climate change is against our own interests.

I have all the green stuff, my energy bill is only €17,-/month so clearly it's working! The energy transition is also the solution to the cost of living crisis here in the Netherlands.  
  
However we see a lot of unfounded resistance. For example: my friend owns a company called inductie.nu which sole business is to make rental homes gas free. It's funded by the rental company not having to pay for the gas supply anymore. That money is used for a loan to pay my friend. Renters get a free induction stove and free pans. It doesn't cost them anything!  
  
Yet quite often people slam the door in his face because they don't want to know anything about it. Only to then call back in tears 2 months later that they cannot cook anymore since gas supply has been cut off, begging him to deliver the free stove anyway.  
  
It's honestly sad how people are so stuck in their ways and act against their own interests.  
  
Its also maddening that the Dutch gouvernement is cutting gasoline taxes yet trains tickets continue to rise.

## 78. All people become brothers

This summer, I went on a solo cycling trip along the Danube: from its source in Germany, straight through Austria, Slovakia, Hungary, Serbia, Bulgaria, and Romania to the Black Sea. In all those countries, I received overwhelming hospitality and kindness from countless people, which initially surprised me, but which I later realized: this is essentially how people are. I believe in the good of humanity. And in all those countries, I felt at home. All of Europe turned out to be my home.  
  
Moreover, not a day went by during my entire journey that I did not speak German, mostly with people who were not fluent in English. It was a real eye-opener: between Enschede and the Black Sea, it is not English, but German that is the lingua franca connecting people.

Ik heb in al die landen van talloze mensen overweldigende gastvrijheid en vriendelijkheid ontvangen, waar ik me eerst over verbaasde, maar waarvan ik me later realiseerde: dit is hoe de mens in wezen is. Ik geloof in het goede van de mens. En in al die landen heb ik me thuis gevoeld. Heel Europa is mijn thuis gebleken.  
  
Er is bovendien gedurende mijn hele reis geen dag voorbijgegaan dat ik géén Duits heb gesproken, veelal met mensen die het Engels niet machtig waren. Het was echt een eye-opener: tussen Enschede en de Zwarte Zee is niet Engels, maar Duits de lingua franca die mensen met elkaar verbindt.

## 81. Overhyped and underdelivered

In general, as I've been looking at job options, I can see a discrepancy between the practical knowledge required in the job market and the coursework. The jobs I've looked at and spoken to recruiters about typically require strong policy knowledge (tech trends, ethics and responsible tech, AI and data governance etc.) and some technical knowledge of tech systems and how specific types of tech work. This is because policy students come out of academic systems that don't interact well with the technical aspects of emerging technologies (at least not sufficiently enough to understand how to create policies for them). While some coursework specifically claimed to cover these, they gave a surface-level understanding that is not helpful to confidently speak about in an interview. I expected the master's degree to provide a year of in-depth learning. I've come out of the programme feeling like I will need to look at more short-course options to meet industry requirements. This defeats the purpose of a 1-year programme at a reputed college, especially for international students and working professionals who either have to travel far, spend a considerable amount of savings, or pause their steady flow of income.

## 83. Too much and too little water

This summer we had the biggest downpour every in the area I live. The water came through the ground into the cellar, which has just never happened before. Fortunately we live in an old farmhouse, and water can easily flow without damaging the construction. It makes me think that people in the olden days really understood how to build and take the natural flow of ground and surface water into consideration.  
We are lucky because on our part of the valley we haven't experienced water shortages yet. In a way, our house is build on the area with most water. The other side of the valley is a different story. This year, there were no major problems (yet) but the last few years people on that side of the valley experienced shortage: the sources started to dry up. They were replenished, but you wonder, will they next time? We are too far from the village to get town water. People are concerned, but they do not think about what could be done.

## 86. the blind society

## 90. Nihilistic consumer society.

I experience Europe as American-dominated. Consumer culture is destroying humanistic European ways of thinking. I myself live within this culture and find little secure footing in my search for alternatives to this superficial and narcissistic culture. I long for humanistically oriented people for whom intellectual cultivation holds value. Instead, I find nothing and distract myself from this disorientation with drugs and social media. The people around me are content with watching anime on Netflix. As a student, I experience shallow, anonymous, and cold seminars. There's hardly any genuine discourse or critical thinking. I struggle to find people who share my deep intellectual needs. I feel lonely. The few people who strive for similar ideals are already studying in other cities.

## 93. The impossible comparison

I often find myself having to argue on the social media I frequent, namely Facebook and LinkedIn, about some important current issues (energy and artificial intelligence) with people who clearly have a lack of knowledge on the subject. They refuse to admit their own shortcomings on the subject, fail to understand informed and documented responses, and counter with clichés, incorrect or even false information, prejudices, and sometimes personal insults. This phenomenon, known as functional illiteracy, affects even people with impressive professional resumes, making the discussion similar to a verbal clash between fans of two bitter rival teams.

<u>Original title (it)</u> : Il confronto impossibile

<u>Original content (it)</u> :

Mi trovo spesso a dover controbattere sui social che frequento, cioè Facebook e LinkedIn, sui alcuni temi importanti di attualità (energia e intelligenza artificiale) con persone che hanno una evidente scarsa conoscenza dell’argomento, non ammettono le loro mancanze in materia, non capiscono le risposte informate e documentate, e controbattono con luoghi comuni, informazioni errate se non false, pregiudizi e talvolta insulti personali. Il fenomeno, conosciuto come analfabetizzazione funzionale, affligge anche persone che hanno un curriculum professionale di rilievo, facendo diventare il confronto assimilabile ad uno scontro verbale tra tifosi di due squadre acerrime nemiche.

## 109. Surprisingly service oriented

The other day I got a call from the registration office in The Hague. They wanted to make sure I was aware that if wanted to vote for the Dutch list in the European Parliament I needed to fill a form declaring that I would not vote for the French list. I am living in France, so I have the option to vote for the Drench or the Dutch list. He was mentioning that he wished he had the option for choosing a person from another country for the Europeans, and I jokingly said: Vote Volt! That's what they stand for. As Europeans we should be able to vote for the best European, and the best may not be from our own country.   
I was really impressed that they call all Dutch voters abroad who are registered in The Hague, and I said so. We had a pleasant conversation, and I was thinking: that's the kind of government I hope for. They take initiative, they help out (even though they did send 3 mails already about it, which I could have read), and they follow-up. The next day and signed the form and send it back by email.

## 121. Populism all around me, not just far away anymore

I was with one of my best friends, she is a couple of years younger than me (about 25). She voted Volt for the national election, she is progressive, keeps up (from a distance) with geopolitical events, is social etc. However, in the days of the election and afterwards, she saw a bunch of small videos on social media, after which I had (for me) a very weird, alienating conversation with her. She said that she saw Geert Wilders (ultranationalist) on Nieuwsuur (serious intellectual tv show) and that she thought he was a very reasonable guy, that she was happy that he would finally take the drama out of political debate, and just sit down with people and FINALLY come up with solutions for the country. Turns out she saw some very smartly cut out (populist) videos, and she never really heard any speeches from the guy. It is like history of the last 20 years of hateful speeches was just completely not there anymore. To me this was a very alienating feeling, trying to tell her what this guys ideology actually is, but I could not convince her... I've had more of these conversations with different people and it feels disappointing that even very smart, nuanced people are falling for the cleverly layed out populist arguments.

<u>Language</u> : en  
<u>Unique identifier</u> :

## 141. What's in a name: identity and the law vs. bureaucracy and prejudice

As a naturalised citizen (of Cyprus), I tried to change my surname. I was met with a stumbling block of being unable to proceed as I was told I had to amend my birth certificate in my country of birth first.  
Problem is, having renounced my citizenship of birth (Russia) earlier, I was unable to proceed with the birth certificate change as thr consular authorities were not in a position to assist me, a now-foreign national, with the matter.  
As a result, I found myself in a limbo state of being unable to exercise my law-protected right to change my name, which is unaffected my the nature in which nationality is acquired - all because the authorities in Cyprus are well known for being notoriously backwards-minded when it comes to many areas of law they consider 'sensitive' (like dealing with matters arising in relation to naturalised citizens).

## 144. Why I love healthcare insurance & healthtech innovation

I was diagnosed with chronic leukemia 2 years ago. 10-20 years ago I could not have been treated, and would have been dead within 5 years after diagnosis. Thanks to international academic cooperation in the '90's and and farmaceutical innovation in the 00's I can now be treated with a simple pill. A pill that enables me to grow old, just like anyone else. A pill which costs 100 euro per day and which would be challenging to finance without universal healthcare   
  
This simple example shows what we are doing globally in preventing diseases. And fuels my technology optimism. And why I strongly believe in an optimistic & pragmatic future that we need to fight for via Volt.

## 147. Feeling our ideas aren't heard

Recently I've been caring more and more about mobility. I've sent a suggestion via email for the bus company that operates in my city explaining why intermodality is so important and why the bus driver should wait about 2 minutes before leaving if a metro has just arrived to the platform (so that those that want to transfer can arrive to their destination at 16:30 instead of waiting half an hour for the next bus and arriving at 17:30). I'm not sure I'll get a response, or when, or if it will be a helpful one with desire to correct the problems around intermodality. And not being sure inhibits me from proposing even more ideas, such as creating a voluntary group chat for everyone who uses the bus "706" or the "yellow" metro line. It could be so good for people to connect with each other and enjoy public transportation more. And I wonder how many more amazing ideas everyone has but doesn't share cause they don't know how to or if it's worth their time to try and share them.

<u>Origin</u> : Portugal  
<u>Language</u> : en

## 177. Wanting to do it properly is not always the easiest and quickest way

My father has passed away and we took over his old car. I wanted to park the car (our only car that we want to share with our neighbours) in my neighboorhood and tried to arrange the necessary park permit. Trying to arrange this permit, I discovered that this was not possible since the municipality marked our garden as parking place on own premises. Our garden was paved when we bought our house 15 years ago, but we were not aware that we were obliged to use this as parking spot. Also the real estate agent did not inform us about this. It turned out I had to make an official objection to this 'parking place on own premises' and that this would take at least 2 months. After that we could possibly arrange the parking permit. Duration: approx 1-2 months. Meanwhile I have to search for parking spots in the neighbourhood where a parking permit is not required. Bothering other people in their parking possibilities. While I really just want to pay for a permit in the neighbourhood of my house.  Why is the municipality so slow in deciding to give me a permit? Why does the decision that I cannot park on my own premises take so long?

It does not feel like a team, but rather as a bunch of people working next to each other. We develop software to save a huge amount of energy using AI, and this is a good thing. On the other hand, the company sticks to the "old" attitude of an economy based on infinite growth. And this is not a good idea, if we want to solve the environmental and climate crises (and others). I think these aspects I described are related, somehow. It's all related to the way we see the relationship of ourselves to others (including environment and nature). ## 210. Why financial literacy should be a feminist issue

I am a woman, born woman, and I have been in therapy for almost 2 years. Because my father, a conservative man, psychologically abused my mother and me for our gender, and finances were one of his bigger weapons.   
He, aside from more pshycologically based abuses, like conditional love or strictness and control and isolating us, convinced my mother women could not handle money, a belief that was then passed to me. "The man handles the money. Women are bad with money". He would spend my mothers money, when she earned more than him. But not let her learn about or do taxes on her own. He would choose insurances, banks to open accounts in, investments, without consulting her, and always said and assumed that, until I was married, he could just do the same with me.   
  
I still have anxiety attacks when I do expensive purchases or handle my IRS, I also have panic attacks when I start searching for house loans or ways to invest in real state, so I can buy a house. Because it was induced in me this idea of "if you try, it will go wrong, you will loose all your money and live in the streets". Something he would repeat often.   
  
Did you know that there are cases of financial bullying, coersion, coerced debt, damaged credit scores, and deep correlations between womens lack of financial literacy and the amount of time women will stay in abusive relationships? The data exists.   
  
One of the reasons I cannot trust the far-left on this topic, is that leftist forces, like portuguese party Bloco de Esquerda (left block) have correlated financial literacy as a capitalist trap that makes people do bad decisions, almost calling it a "liberal" conspiracy to promote capitalist think tanks and ideas. How can a party that is supposedly pro social-justice ever present themselves as feminist and pro working class defend such a statement? On the other side of the spectrum, conservative political groups just want the women to return to more traditional roles, leaving these situations more open to become the norm.   
  
If you are truly a feminist, you will defend  the hability of women to financially protect themselves from any kind of financial abuse. Not shame them from engaging in this type of education, for the sake of protecting a supposed anti-capitalist utopia you have as a goal to construct. If not for ideological reasons, do it for pragmatic ones. The anti-capitalist utopia will not come in our lifetime, if ever, but there are women being convinced they are financially unstable and abused by the men in their lives right now. And not just women, anyone with lack of financial literacy is more prone to make bad decision with their money. Not everyone can precisely throw their money at a personal assistant or consultant to gain or not loose money. And leaves them more vulnerable to any miracle worker that tells them how to get rich quick. If you truly are for feminism, you will teach them to have a positive relationship with money and teach them how to handle it alone.   
  
This is where Volt can make a difference. Differenciate from other parties that fall under this trap. Don't run away from the idea that money and grow personal wealth can be a positive thing. And pass the message that women can do it as well as men. Not for the purpose of getting rich, but for the purpose of being free from an actual form of patriarchy.

And it's not just homophobia. Xenophobia, hate speech against welfare recipients, etc. This trend worries me. I've been verbally attacked several times on the street by groups of strangers. "Is it a man or a woman?" "What's in your pants?" "All LGBTQ people should be killed." Gagging noises.

<u>Original title (de)</u> : Queerfeindlichkeit und Hass

<u>Original content (de)</u> :

Immer mehr Menschen in meiner Umgebung sagen Dinge wie "Die Regenbogenflagge ist ein Symbol für die Unterdrückung der Mehrheitsgesellschft". Das kann Jede Person sein. Ein Arbeitskollege, mein Nachbar, mein Opa. Und es bleibt nicht bei queerfeinlichkeit. Ausländerhass, Hetze gegen Bürgergeldemfangende etc. Die Entwicklung mach mir Sorgen. Auf der Straße wurde ich mehrfach von fremben Personengruppen verbal angegriffen. "Ist es ein Mann oder eine Frau?" "Was hast du in der Hose?" "LGBTQ Menschen sollte man alle Töten" "Würggeräusche"

## 225. Exchanging commonalities from different perspectives, consciously developing them, and co-creatively initiating them from the future.

My heart beats for Europe. As a 15-year-old convent school student, I first declared myself European. I place my hope in Europe's historic opportunity to realize meaningful freedom, to develop shared progress and global citizenship – based on universally valid human rights. Currently, I am active in integration courses and witness the blatant breaches of trust within established democratic systems. Precisely because I sense that the capacity for personal integrity among citizens in individual European countries leaves much to be desired and hopeful, the projections onto the difficulties of migration and integration, the lack of understanding of climate-related disasters, war propaganda, and much more are merely distractions from the global challenges facing us Europeans. Therefore, I seek solutions through integrated politics and wish to contribute, currently through the development of an integrated educational approach with relevance in the political arena.

<u>Original title (de)</u> : Gemeinsamkeiten in unterschiedlichen Perspektiven austauschen, bewusst entwickeln und von der Zukunft her co-creativ einleiten

<u>Original content (de)</u> :

Mein Herz schlägt für Europa. Als 15-jährige Klosterschülerin sagte ich erstmals, ich bin Europäerin. Ich hoffe auf die historische Chance Europas, vernünftige Freiheit zu realisieren, gemeinschaftlichen Fortschritt &amp; Weltbürgertum zu entwickeln - auf der Basis global gültiger Menschenrechte. Aktuell bin ich in Integrationskursen aktiv und sehe die krassen Vertrauensbrüche in etablierten demokratischen Systemen. Gerade weil ich spüre, dass die Fähigkeiten zur persönlichen Integrität der Bürger:innen in den einzelnen europäischen Ländern zu Wünschen und Hoffen lässt, sind die Projektionen auf die Schwierigkeiten mit Migration und Integration, das Unverständnis klimatisch bedingter Katastrophen, Kriegspropaganda u.v.m. nur Ablenkung von globalen Herausforderungen für uns Europäer:innen. Darum suche ich Lösungen in integraler Politik und möchte meinen Beitrag leisten, zurzeit mit der Konzeptentwicklung integraler Bildungsansatzes mit Relevanz im politischen Raum.

<u>Language</u> : de  
<u>Unique identifier</u> : voltsense

## 227. Increase polarization even with the right setting

A friend of mine was visiting us here in Mecklenburg with her family. She's incredibly politically active, very aware, and well-informed. When our neighbor came over for a friendly chat and a barbecue, he immediately informed the family, as he likes to be a bit provocative: "I vote for the AfD, and you guys from the West have no clue..." My friend was completely taken aback and immediately set about trying to "convert" our neighbor. She wanted to know why, wanted to understand. But her indignation came across, and the neighbor just became even more entrenched in his position. This makes me realize once again that even highly informed, interested, and active people don't know how to deal with polarization properly, and on the contrary, can even exacerbate it. It's given me a lot to think about!

<u>Original title (de)</u> : Mit der richtigen Einstellung Polarisierung trotzdem verstärken

<u>Original content (de)</u> :

Eine Freundin war mit ihrer Familie hier bei uns in Mecklenburg zu besuch. Sie ist super politisch aktiv, super bewußt und informiert. Als unser Nachbar kam, zum freundlichen Plausch und zum Grillen, hat er die Familie gleich mal informiert, da er gerne etwas provokativ ist: Ich wähle AFD, und ihr aus dem Westen habt ja keine Ahnung...  Meine Freundin war völlig baff und hat sich gleich ins Zeug gelegt, unseren Nachbarn zu "bekehren".  Sie wollte wissen, wieso, wollte verstehen. Aber ihre Entrüstung kam rüber, und der Nachbar hat sich nur noch versteift auf seine Position. Das macht mir wieder klar, dass auch super informierte, interessierte und aktive Menschen nicht wissen, wie man mit Polarisierung richtig umgeht, und im Gegenteil, sie noch verstärken können. Gibt mir sehr zu denken!

## 233. The Mobility Paradox

Realising the complexity of public planning in mobility.  
  
How even the smallest things that are not aligned, will create lots of frustration.  
  
E.g. i was leaving office and needed to go to the bus stop on the other side of the road (to cross). While the bus wasnt there yet, while Iwaiting at the red light, the bus arrived and the red light didnt go green still.  
  
Finally it went green and I ran and the bus left at the same time. Now me and a few other people who were waiting for the red light had to wait an extra 10 minutes before we were able to enter the next bus.  
  
I mean, it is not the biggest problem, but it is an interesting misalignment (or perceived misalignment) that creates frustration

## 253. Overqualified workers in poorly paid jobs

When we bought a new bathtub, it was only supposed to be delivered to our front door. The delivery man was kind enough to carry it up to the third floor with my husband. He was from Morocco, spoke hardly any German, and only broken English. Once inside our new apartment, he walked around it in long strides. My husband remarked that the apartment was 70 square meters. The Moroccan man corrected him: 72 square meters, including the balcony. He studied architecture and works as a delivery man in Germany. I don't believe there's a German architect who can determine the exact square footage of an apartment simply by walking around it. There are certainly many skilled workers (which Germany needs) stuck in underqualified jobs. My husband wanted to give him a tip as a thank you, which he accepted only very reluctantly. To me, this also means he helped simply for the sake of helping.

<u>Original title (de)</u> : Überqualifizierte Arbeiter in schlechtbezahlten Jobs

<u>Original content (de)</u> :

Als wir uns eine neue Badewanne gekauft haben, sollte diese eigentlich nur bis zur Haustür geliefert werden. Der Lieferant war so freundlich und hat sie mit meinem Mann noch bis in den dritten Stock getragen. Er kam aus Marroco, sprach kaum deutsch und nur schlechtes Englisch. Als er in unseren neuen Wohnung war, ging er diese in großen Schritten ab. Mein Mann meinte daraufhin, dass die Wohnung 70m2 groß sei. Der Marokkaner korrigierte ihn: 72m2 mit Balkon. Er hat Architektur studiert und arbeitet in Deutschland als Lieferanten. Ich glaube nicht, dass es einen deutschen Architekten gibt, der durch das abgehen der Wohnung die exakte Quadratmeterzahl bestimmen kann. Es gibt bestimmt viele gute Fachkräfte, (die Deutschland braucht), die in unterqualifizierten Jobs stecken. Mein Mann wollte ihm als Dank ein Trinkgeld geben, dass er nur sehr widerwillig annahm. Das bedeutet für mich auch, er hat geholfen, um des Helfenswillen.

## 260. Incompetence and profiteering hidden behind chatbots and AI systems instead of interpersonal communication.

A shift has taken place from face-to-face interpersonal contact to digital contact with chatbots and, if you are lucky, helpdesks. The latter are annoyingly unreachable or place you in a terrible queue with even worse music to keep you occupied. Many, if not all, phone numbers on supplier and government websites have simply disappeared. The names of officials and their bosses have also suddenly vanished. Most people simply accept this resignedly. You can no longer hold anyone accountable. You are increasingly talking to systems with limited functionality. The time you lose as a customer or citizen is considered normal, while the profits of companies (suppliers) continue to rise. You are increasingly encountering these kinds of mechanisms within the government as well.  
  
It is time for a law that defines the right to contact and human interaction, before we end up talking only to chatbots and AI systems. And what about the people who are not, cannot, or do not want to be digitally savvy?

<u>Original title (nl)</u> : Onkunde en winstbejag verstopt achter chatbots en AI systemen in plaats van intermenselijke communicatie.

<u>Original content (nl)</u> :

De laatste zijn  irritant onbereikbaar of plaatsen je in een verschrikkelijke wachtrij met nog ergere muziek om je bezig te houden.  Veel zo niet alle telefoonnummers op websites van leveranciers en overheid zijn gewoon verdwenen. De namen van de functionarissen en hun bazen zijn ook plotseling allemaal verdwenen. Gelaten wordt dit door de meeste mensen allemaal maar geaccepteerd.  Je kunt niemand meer verantwoordelijk stellen. Je praat meer en meer tegen systemen met beperkte functionaliteit. De tijd die je verliest als klant of burger wordt als normaal beschouwd.  Terwijl de winsten van de bedrijven (leveranciers) verder oplopen. Ook bij de overheid loopt je meer en meer  tegen dit soort mechanismen aan.   
Het wordt tijd voor een wet die het recht op contact en menselijk contact definieert voordat we straks alleen nog maar tegen chatbots , en AI systemen praten.  En hoe zit het met de mensen die niet zo digitaal zijn , kunnen of willen zijn ?

## 262. Every life is a universe

Over the course of the last 11 months, I've been part of a group of Muslims and Jews in German-speaking Switzerland that come together to share feelings and thoughts about the "Israeli-Palestinian conflict". Our goal is to create a safe space of understanding that offers room for diverging feelings and narratives - in a time when there are few spaces where people feel like they can share their fear, anger, despair, and hope openly - without being misunderstood or attacked. The group is an attempt to not let our communities in Switzerland be drawn into division in the face of all the unspeakable violence in Israel, Gaza, the West Bank, and Lebanon. This groups is one of the few places where I feel I can breathe. Where there is room for the complexity of lives, narratives, collective identities. And mostly pain. There is so much pain that festers in people as long as they cannot share it and as long as they feel they aren't seen. Every meeting we've had is a small universe in itself. Calm, deep, sad, and hopeful. After each meeting I leave the room both heavier and lighter. Heavier as I start to understand more perspectives on the unspeakable violence and suffering. Lighter as I see that there are wonderful people dedicated to coming tother and emphasising the holiness of life and solidarity to each others' humanity - without forgetting their particular identities.

## 263. civil society engagement

Currently, I'm preoccupied with the proposed ban on the AfD (Alternative for Germany). We're discussing with friends why it's so difficult to secure the necessary majorities in politics, even though at the beginning of the year, so many people (over a million) took to the streets across the country to demand precisely that.  
  
Furthermore, the question naturally arises regarding opportunities for participation. On the one hand, there's such public engagement, involving many politicians and invoking the power of civic engagement, and then it all fizzles out in the hesitant inaction of professional politicians.  
  
The perceived effectiveness of personal activism thus feels depressingly low. So, with so many issues these days, the question is once again: how to stay motivated, how to remain hopeful?  
  
On a positive note, it's worth noting that the growth of renewable energy (PV) is primarily driven by private households (including in Bavaria). So, personal commitment does make a difference and sometimes achieves more than official political actors.

<u>Original title (de)</u> : zivilgesellschaftliches Engagement

<u>Original content (de)</u> :

Aktuell beschäftigt mich das angestrebte AfD-Verbotsverfahren. Wir besprechen gerade im Umfeld, wieso es so schwierig ist, in der Politik entsprechende Mehrheiten zu gewinnen, obwohl doch Anfang des Jahres genau dafür so unglaublich viele Menschen (über eine Millionen) überall im Land dafür auf den Strassen waren.  
Darüber hinaus entsteht natürlich die Frage nach Möglichkeiten der Beteiligung. So ein Engagement der Bevölkerung auf der einen Seite unter Beteiligung vieler Politiker:innen, Beschwörung des zivilgesellschaftlichen Engagements und dann verpufft das Ganze in der zögerlichen Tatenlosigkeit der Berufspolitik.  
Die Wirksamkeit des persönlichen Engagements rutscht so natürlich gefühlt ins deprimierende Minus. Die Frage bei so vielen Themen dieser Tage lautet also wieder: wie motiviert, wie hoffnungsvoll bleiben?  
  
positiv hingegen ist die Meldung, dass der Zuwachs der erneuerbaren Energien (PV) im Wesentlichen von Privathaushalten getragen wird (auch in Bayern). Also bewirkt der persönliche EInsatz doch etwas und erreicht manchmal mehr, als die offiziellen politischen Akteure.

## 270. A distributor of indifference

Once upon a time, there was a tired worker returning home from work at 6:00 PM.  
Schuman Metro, packed with people putting an end to their European glories and ambitions for the day.  
A man, clearly drunk or ill, was lying on the ground in front of a vending machine.  
Who knew what was wrong with him? Why didn't anyone ask? The metro started up again, and all that remained was the memory of a vending machine of selfishness and indifference.  
The man was still lying there. Who knows what became of him?  
It was impossible to find first responders.

Un uomo, chiaramente ubriaco o malato, e' steso a terra davanti ad un distributore automatico.  
Chi poteva sapere cosa avesse? Perche' nessuno lo ha chiesto? La metro e' ripartita ed e' rimasto il ricordo di un distributore di egoismo ed indifferenza.  
L'uomo ancora li' disteso. Chissa' cosa ne sara' stato di lui.

## 271. Short sad story

I've been in Brussels for a few years. After finishing my master's degree, I did three internships, two of which barely paid (250 euros a month).  
After the last internship (which ended in April), I went to Oslo for a prestigious course for a few months.  
Now I'm back in Brussels, and I don't know how many applications I've sent. I can't find anything: I think I have enough experience for a junior position, but there are few.  
The competition is sky-high, and many don't take on overqualified people.  
The situation is dire.

## 272. The invisibles of society

Mine is more of a constant reality than a singular experience: In Saint-Gilles, almost every day I see homeless people living on the streets, in the cold, with all the differences and suffering that comforts them.  
Whenever someone does lend them a hand, it's through civic or religious associations or initiatives. But (it seems to me) never from the municipality, and I don't understand why so many people are still allowed to be abandoned, without any point of reference in society or even without a roof over their heads to shelter them from the cold and rain.

Le volte che qualcuno da loro una mano, sono associazioni o iniziative civiche o religiose. ## 277. Unlocking social value in healthcare

There is a citizens initiative* in The Netherlands running as a village cooperative where a network of volunteers are the first point of contact for care requests. This social layer sits in between the care companies of the privatised public healthcare. I believe this is a brilliant way to unlock social value at the long tail of the pareto scale.  
BTW on average it saves almost €40K per person that would have ended up with long term care in the old system.  
*) It is called Domein Overschrijdende Samenwerking DOS.

## 278. Disruptive changes through AI technology

The newest thing that keeps me busy is AI technology, which will change a lot in very unpredictable ways. I do small experiments with ChatGPT, my own chatbots and most recently NotebookLM. I think it's scary what this technology is capable of. It can be used for good things, but it can certainly be used for destructive purposes as well. One of the things that will happen is that it will become increasingly difficult to distinguish between what is authentic and what is simulated. This increases the risk of polarization, manipulation and disintegration of societies.

Jag tycker det är skrämmande vad denna teknologi är förmögen till. Den kan användas till bra saker, men den kan säkert användas till destruktiva ändamål också. En av de saker som kommer att hända är att det blir allt svårare att skilja på vad som är autentiskt och vad som är simulerat. ## 279. Woking ourselves to death

My contribution to society is alienated seemingly because expertise does not count unless it is accompanied by a socially acceptable label - my label carries no value in the currency of wokery. The inheritance of respect is discredited!  
  
I see policy makers oblivious to the evidence and science where I am familiar with the subject and I see charlatans and the grossly unqualified claiming expertise in other areas. The marquee example is Greta Thunberg - who claims a knowledge of climate impacts and moderation and proclaims 'the science is settled' [few scientists are climate experts and have no specific insight into the problem, science never works by consensus nor is science ever settled - it is a democratic process in which any person however humble can produce evidence which over-turns the theories of the greats].  
  
The Greta Thunberg phenomenon - led by the palpably unqualified nonetheless proclaimed by the system - is evident across so many of our institutions and the policies they develop. It is anti-democratic, anti-meritocracy and often corrupt.

## 281. Carbon tunnel vision distracts city council from the real problem

The muncipality I work for organized an information session for the city council about sustainability. They hired an engineering firm to explain topics such as 'climate neutral' and 'energy neutral'.  
  
After introducing climate neutral, it was mentioned the city is responsible for emissions from ships that fare the rivers. Somebody said those emissions were already compensated by national solar and wind energy parks. Therefore, the muncipality does not have to compensate those emissions. As a response, the speaker tried to explain that it does not matter how it is compensated (national or in the muncipality), the muncipality just hast to provide reasoning for it.  
  
I felt helpless as I thought: why are we bickering over CO2 budgets, when this is about ecological overshoot, the breaching of 6 out of 9 planetary boundaries? The warming build in the pipeline has too big of a momentum to stop, and climate chang is just one of the factors.   
  
So painful to see a completely sidetracked dicussion.

## 295. Alienated youth in a broken housing system

A housing crisis is devastating the future perspectives of young spaniards. In the news, a long queue of university students was being reported, waiting for a meeting with a housing agency. Through the meeting, the students would access the opportunity to rent a room or a flat with their friends during the year, in order to attend the university.  
  
The prices are totally disproportionate, the flats are small and often with poor living standards, and young students were peacefully waiting for a meeting with the agency, looking at their phones, totally alienated from their reality. I am certain that most of them know and care about the unfairness of the system, that brings workers (their parents or them) to devote most of their working hours to keep enriching landowners, often constituted as societies with multiple properties, often international companies, with no other purpose than to live off the work of others.   
  
The DOCILITY of university students (as myself!), which is supposed to be the most politically active group in the society, left me astonished. Why weren't housing agencies being brought down to flames all over the country? Wouldn't that be the expected response from university students under these conditions? If students do not raise their voices now, what are we to expect from the future?

## 298. Versatile, open Europe

I have recently completed three international cycling trips. Through the Netherlands, Germany, Austria, Italy, France, England, and Scotland. Simply on a narrow country lane, with my bike on the train, at a bench, in the hotel bike storage, or on a terrace—everywhere I went, I struck up conversations with locals, other cyclists, and tourists. I received tips, gave them myself, chatted casually, or was genuinely interested in a particular topic. Now, I speak the languages ​​of all the countries I visited well, so that certainly helps, but that is precisely what makes Europe such a wonderful continent: many cultures and many languages ​​on a small, easy-to-cycle surface.

<u>Original title (nl)</u> : Veelzijdig, open Europa

<u>Original content (nl)</u> :

Ik heb de afgelopen tijd drie internationale fietstochten gemaakt. Door Nederland, Duitsland, Oostenrijk, Italië, Frankrijk, Engeland en Schotland. Gewoon op een smal landweggetje, met de fiets in de trein, bij een bankje, in de fietsenstalling van het hotel of op een terrasje, overal kwam ik in gesprek met lokalen mensen, andere fietsers en toeristen.  Ik kreeg tips, gaf ze zelf ook, kletste vrijblijvend of juist geïnteresseerd in een bepaald onderwerp. Nu spreek ik de talen van alle bezochte landen goed, dus dat helpt zeker, maar juist dat maakt nu dat Europa zo'n fijn continent is: veel culturen en veel talen op een klein, makkelijk te befietsen oppervlak.

## 299. Not legally provided for: queer and multinational families

My wife and I (female) would like to have a child, but the legal situation is complicated. However, our biological clocks are ticking, so we will probably have to make a decision soon. If I carry the child to term, my wife will not be registered as the mother but will have to go through a lengthy stepchild adoption process. At the same time, we don't know if the child would also receive French citizenship, since my wife is French, but under current German law, she wouldn't initially be considered the legal mother.

## 301. Inadequate health care

For over a year now I am going to psychotherapy due to mood swings and unreal expierences (probably hallucinations) I have been expierencing for the past 3 years. Going to therapy was hard for me due to the stigma mental illness has in our society. After 3 moths on the waiting list I finally could start the therapy. Now due to the severity of the symptoms I have been advice to also contact a psychiatrist about possible medication. I am trying to get in with one. However no one in a radius of half an hour drive is taking any new clients in. I have also tried expanding my radius of search to an hour drive, but still no one has a free spot for me.   
I know that many people have the same problem with all kinds of doctors (neurologists etc.) to get with a new genegologistis after my last one closed due to retirment I have been waiting 8 moths for the next free spot. The situation with doctors is bad across the board, especially if you do not have private insurence.

## 303. Appreciating my country from the window of the train

I was driving in the train in The Netherlands. I usually take the car, as I have this feeling public transport always represents trouble. I was so wrong. While driving the train and looking out the window, I felt a deep appreciation for how enormously high the quality of living in my country is, and how well we have organised society for all. Notwithstanding the trouble we face as society in several areas (housing, welcoming refugees, education, healthcare in the years to come), we are doing so well. This felt really good, and it’s a memory I told many of my friends about.

## 309. Make healthy food cheaper.

I was listening at a podcast and hearing that in the US 42% of the people have Obesitas and 74% (!!!) is overweight. I also heard that in Europe we are slowly crawling towards those numbers. I am very worried that in the Netherlands, where I live, things are going to be the same. Thes numbers cause an extreme burden on our social health system and lots can be done by regulation. Why don't we have a sugar tax yet?! And why don't we lower the tax on fresh fruit and veggies. They say these things are too complicated, but some countries already do this. I think the lobby of big industries that produce unhealthy food is too strong. Being healthy should be a human right, but with these companies making all these processed foods, full of starch, corn and sugar, it is a lost battle.

## 319. The healthcare system cannot continue like this much longer.

I'm studying medicine and am currently in the clinical phase of my studies. I'm gaining so much insight into the daily lives of doctors in Germany. And these insights are making me seriously question my career choice – but I'm too far along in my studies to drop out. The doctors are overworked; today, a resident (on call) told me she'd been working for 26 hours and needed to go home soon. Friends who have already received their medical licenses talk with dark circles under their eyes about the overstuffed schedules and the long lists of overtime hours, and at the same time say that it's all right, there's just no other way. Medications are in short supply. Currently, it's saline solution; before that, it was fever syrup and various other medications whose vital importance shouldn't be underestimated. Patients are becoming increasingly unruly and expect service from those who are currently caring for emergency cases. At the same time, there's very little capacity left for teaching. Germany's future doctors are sent home after a quarter of an hour of practical instruction because there is too much to do on the wards for teaching. In some cases, the doctors don't even manage to attend lectures at all.

<u>Original title (de)</u> : Das Gesundheitssystem kann nicht mehr lange so weitermachen

<u>Original content (de)</u> :

Ich studiere Medizin und bin im klinischen Abschnitt des Studiums. Ich bekomme so viele größere Einblicke in den Alltag von Ärzt:innen in Deutschland. Und diese Einblicke lassen mich sehr stark an meiner Berufswahl zweifeln - fürs Abbrechen bin ich aber zu weit im Studium fortgeschritten. Die Ärzt:innen sind überarbeitet, heute hat mir eine Assistenzärztin (in Bereitschaft) noch erzählt, dass sie seit 26h arbeitet und langsam nach Hause muss. Freunde, die ihre Approbation bereits erhalten haben sprechen mit tiefen Augenringen von den viel zu vollen Dienstplänen und den großen Überstundenlisten und sagen im gleichen Moment, dass das schon ok sei, es ginge halt nicht anders. Medikamente sind knapp. Aktuell NaCl, vorher schon Fiebersaft und diverse andere Medikamente, deren Überlebensnotwendigkeit nicht zu unterschätzen sind. Patient:innen werden häufiger ausfallend und erwarten einen Service von Leuten, die sich gerade um Notfallbetroffene kümmern. Gleichzeitig bleiben nur noch wenig Kapazitäten für Lehre. Deutschlands Ärzt:innen von morgen werden nach einer viertel Stunde Praxisunterricht nach Hause geschickt, weil auf Station zu viel zu tun ist für Lehre. Teilweise schaffen die Ärzt:innen es nicht, zu Lehrveranstaltungen aufzutauchen. 

<u>Origin</u> : Germany  
<u>Language</u> : de  
<u>Unique identifier</u> : voltnws  
<u>EU is like</u> : a large family  
<u>Europe is like</u> : a fortress  
<u>Democracy is like</u> : lesser evil (evil because it is becoming clear in many places that democracy also has its downsides when actively anti-democratic people are democratically elected (how is that even possible?!))

<u>Question</u> : Do you really believe that minority groups, who have hardly any power, can be to blame for the problems in our country? Or was I simply lucky enough to share with others?  
<u>The experience was</u> : Very negative

## 341. Polluted habitats

I find it extremely distressing to be exposed to smoke from tobacco or tobacco-like products, as well as cannabis, which is unfortunately ubiquitous outdoors. Added to this is the noise and exhaust pollution from motor vehicles, especially mopeds, scooters, trucks, and cars; buses and trains are less of a problem due to their lower frequency and consequently lower pollution levels compared to private motorized transport.  
  
Finally, particularly in the outskirts of metropolitan areas, where the city's cleaning services seem to pay little to no attention, there are often mountains of trash that simply cannot be ignored: from clothing and garbage bags along waterways to broken washing machines and other (special) waste, there's practically nothing that isn't lying around neglected and seemingly belonging to no one (anymore).

<u>Original title (de)</u> : Verdreckte Lebensräume

<u>Original content (de)</u> :

Ich empfinde es als äußerst belastend, Qualm aus Tabak- oder tabakähnlichen sowie Cannabiserzeugnissen wahrzunehmen, welcher draußen leider an jeder Ecke anzufinden ist. Hinzu kommt die Lärm- und Abgasbelastung durch Kraftfahrzeuge, insbesondere Mopeds, Mofas, LKW und PKW; Busse und Bahnen eher weniger aufgrund der geringeren Häufigkeit und der damit einher gehenden geringeren Belastung als der motorisierte Individualverkehr.  
Schließlich gibt es insbesondere in Randgebieten von Ballungsräumen, deren Relevanz seitens der städtischen Reinigung kaum bis nicht bemerkbar zu sein scheint, häufig Abfallberge, die man einfach nicht ignorieren kann: Von Kleidung und Müllsäcken an Gewässern über defekte Waschmaschinen und sonstigen (Sonder-)müll gibt es eigentlich nichts, was nicht irgendwo verwahrlost herumliegt und niemandem (mehr) zu gehören scheint.

<u>Democracy is like</u> : Fair access to power—independent of inheritance, income, wealth, social class, innate characteristics, or origin—is used, guided by just discourse, possibly involving multiple individuals, to strive to satisfy as many people as possible. Decisions are made in the best interests of "the people," adhering to both the rule of law and scientific principles to prevent arbitrariness. Everyone has the right (initially) to participate equally in decision-making (e.g., through elections or referendums), but no one has the right to present their own position as infallibly good without legitimacy (i.e., support or trust from actors other than themselves), facts, or arguments. In short, democracy is the only form of government that aims to offer everyone equal legal opportunities, such as the right to shape their own life, and thus justly dismantle the monopoly of power de jure. The separation of powers is arguably the most important characteristic of such a system.

## 342. step by step

It is becoming increasingly clear to me that almost all things, or rather processes, that are truly important to humanity and form interconnected wholes are deemed insignificant by economic developments. I experience examples of this daily: Who remembers the name of a 16th-century Tuscan banker? And who remembers the names of artists from the same period? I know almost exclusively artists who live on the margins of society, while those who make their lives increasingly difficult are busy giving each other monuments for breakfast. To witness this, I need only take a walk in my city on any given day.

<u>Original title (de)</u> : Schritt für Schritt

<u>Original content (de)</u> :

Es wird mir zunehmend klarer, dass fast alle Dinge oder besser Vorgänge, die menschlich wirklich wichtig sind und Zusammenhänge bilden, von den ökonomischen Entwicklungen für unwesentlich gehalten werden. Beispiele erlebe ich täglich: Wer erinnert sich an den Namen eines toskanischen Bankiers aus dem 16 Jh? Und wer erinnert sich an die Namen der Künstler aus derselben Zeit? Ich kenne fast nur Künstler, die materiell am Rande der Gesellschaft leben, während diejenigen, die ihnen das Leben immer schwerer machen, sich gegenseitig Denkmäler zum Frühstück schenken. Um das zu erleben, brauche ich nur einen Spaziergang in meiner Stadt, an einem beliebigen Tag.

## 343. chance encounters

## 346. Looking ahead to the inclusive society of the future

We (as senior pensioners) have the unique opportunity to get to know and be part of the youngest generations of adults in their most diverse composition, at the purest and most intimate moments.  
  
For these generations, there are no issues regarding skin color, origin, gender, sexual orientation, etcetera.  
Despite, or perhaps even thanks to, the algorithms of the social media they consult, they grew up with the daily realization that their desires and needs do not differ from one another. Whether your cradle stood in Amsterdam, Jakarta, or Nairobi.  
To them, a border is merely an arbitrarily drawn, useless line in the sand.

<u>Original title (nl)</u> : Vooruitblik op de inclusieve samenleving van de toekomst

Voor deze generaties bestaan geen issues rondom huidskleur, afkomst, gender, seksuele oriëntatie, etcetera.  
Zij zijn ondanks of zelfs misschien wel dankzij de algoritmes van de door hen geraadpleegde sociale media opgegroeid met het dagelijkse besef dat hun verlangens en behoeften niet onderling afwijken van elkaar. Of je wieg nu staat in Amsterdam, Djakarta, of Nairobi.  
Een grens is voor hen slechts een willekeurig getrokken nutteloze streep in het zand.

## 348. A future through diversity

During my three-day hospital stay, I interacted with numerous doctors and medical professionals—the vast majority of whom had a migration background. The treatment and communication were excellent, and I found myself imagining what our healthcare system would be like without all these people—it probably wouldn't exist at all.  
  
This experience underscored how crucial migration and integration are for Europe and how much more we need to do to promote them.  
  
Without immigration, Europe has no future!

Eine Erfahrung wie wichtig Migration und Integration für Europa sind und das wir vielmehr dafür tun müssen.   
Ohne Zuwanderung hat Europa keine Zukunft!

## 349. Politics for and with the citizens

The ability to engage in discourse and compromise is increasingly being lost. Perspectives that don't align with one's own view are marginalized or dismissed. There's a growing emphasis on absolutes, where the focus isn't on learning, cooperation, or the well-being of future generations, but solely on optimizing the individual. The progressive wing must engage and include the conservative wing – the conservative wing should learn that criticism of exclusionary attitudes and unsustainable lifestyles isn't an attack on their own way of life, but rather an invitation to reflect (though the criticism should be formulated accordingly).  
  
We must learn to learn together, and politics must become authentic and transparent. Society sees that promises are frequently broken and that misconduct goes unpunished. Even unpopular but necessary decisions are made from above without involving those affected.  
  
A sense of "those in power" is emerging.

<u>Original title (de)</u> : Politik für und mit den Bürger*innen

<u>Original content (de)</u> :

Der Fähigkeit zum Diskurs und zum Kompromiss geht zunehmend verloren. Sichten, die nicht dem eigenen Bild entsprechen, werden ausgegrenzt oder gecancelt. Es geht vermehrt um Absolutheiten in der nicht auf das Lernen, das Miteinander oder das Wohl der zukünftigen Generationen, sondern ausschließlich auf die Optimierung des Individuums wert gelegt wird. Der progressive Teil muss den konservativen einbinden und mitnehmen - der konservative Teil sollte lernen das Kritik anausgrenzenden Haltungen und nicht nachhaltigen Lebensweisen nicht als Angriff auf den eigenen Lebenstil ist, sondern zum Nachdenken auffordert (die Kritik sollte aber auch entsprechend formuliert werden).  
Wir müssen lernen miteinander zu lernen und Politik muss authentisch und transparent werden. Die Gesellschaft sieht das vielfach Versprechen gebrochen werden und Fehlverhalten keine Konsequenzen folgt. Auch unliebsame erforderliche Entscheidungen werden von oben herab ohne die Einbindung der Betroffenen getroffen.  
Es entsteht ein Gefühl von „die da oben“.

## 351. Appearances can be deceiving….

I was standing in line at a gas station to pay. A man in front of me turned around and said: "That's what you get when you want to pay cash." I said: "But I want to pay by card." "Oh," he said, "then you have to go over there by that wall; you can pay by card there and you don't have to talk to anyone." I looked at him smiling and said: "But I did have a nice little chat with you." I thanked him for his helpfulness and went to withdraw money. The man in question didn't exactly look average: short hair, heavy tattoos, and a broad Amsterdam accent. Not someone I would normally strike up a conversation with, but we were both friendly to each other, which I hadn't experienced otherwise.

<u>Original title (nl)</u> : Schijn bedriegt….

<u>Original content (nl)</u> :

Ik stond in een tankstation in de rij om af te rekenen. Een man voor mij draaide zich om en zei: dat krijg je als je cash wilt betalen. Ik zei: maar ik wil pinnen. O zei hij dan moet je daar bij die muur zijn daar kun je pinnen en hoef je met niemand te praten. Ik keek hem lachend aan en zei: maar nu had ik toch een leuk gesprekje met u. ## 354. Where PNRR funds would be useful

Today I went for an MRI scan with the National Health System at the San Raffaele Turro Hospital in Milan.  
Having booked an appointment through my health record (which includes the GP's prescription, a prerequisite for getting an appointment) and having both a Lombardy Region and hospital certificate confirming my appointment, I was surprised to discover at the reception desk that without a written paper prescription to hand in at the time, I couldn't have the test.  
The test was booked a year ago. With a prescription from a year ago that I obviously no longer had. Or who knows where it was...  
I was convinced everything was online: they gave me the appointment because I had the doctor's prescription.  
So why should I "re" produce it?  
Why is the entire healthcare system—not just the entire country (I wish!), but at least the region? The city! Why isn't it online? What use is AI if we can't or aren't capable of connecting this data? Rather than flying forward (or we'll crash), it would be worth staying at the base.  
Very kind and professional staff.

<u>Original title (it)</u> : Dove i fondi del PNRR sarebbero utili

<u>Original content (it)</u> :

Oggi sono andata a fare una risonanza magnetica con il sistema sanitario nazionale a Milano ospedale san Raffaele turro.   
Avendo preso appuntamento attraverso il fascicolo sanitario ( dove compare la prescrizione del medico di base, condizione sine qua non per avere l’appuntamento) e essendo munita di foglio sia di regione Lombardia sia dell’ospedale che attestavano il mio appuntamento, sono rimasta sorpresa quando all’accettazione ho scoperto che senza prescrizione scritta cartacea da consegnare al momento, non avrei potuto fare l’esame.   
Esame prenotato UN anno fa. Con una ricetta di un anno fa che ovviamente non avevo più. O chissà dov’era..   
Ero convinta che tutto fosse online: l’appuntamento me l’hanno dato perché c’era la ricetta medica.   
Quindi perché doverlo “ri” produrre?  
Perché tutto il sistema sanitario non dico di tutto il paese ( magari!) ma almeno della regione? Della città! Perché non è in rete? Che ci serve l’AI se non possiamo o non siamo capaci di mettere in connessione questi dati? Più che volare in avanti ( che ci schiantiamo) varrebbe la pena siatemare le basi.   
Personale  molto gentile e professionale.

## 368. transforming from a Science - Technology - Capital system to a S-T-Ecology system

## 369. Green grassland is too acidic

Last week, I helped at our picking garden to prepare the land for winter. The vegetable beds had yielded their produce and now needed to be provided with a fair amount of lime. I understood that this would need to be done for another six years or so, as it was previously grassland where cows had grazed for years. The result was very acidic soil. I was shocked by this. What is humanity doing to the earth and the animals? Unilateral use completely depletes it. I was confronted with this directly in my city life.

<u>Original content (nl)</u> :

Ik begreep dat dit nog zo’n 6 jaar zou moeten omdat het voorheen grasland was waar jarenlang koeien hadden gelopen. Gevolg was hele zure grond. Ik schrok daarvan. Wat doet de mens met de aarde en de dieren? Eenzijdig gebruik put het totaal uit. Ik werd daar in mijn stadse leventje direct mee geconfronteerd.
