## 542. Epidemic of language deprivation

I repeatedly observe that public institutions, whether administrative or educational, do not truly support inclusion. The UN Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (CRPD) has been ratified, but anything that needs to be changed is perceived as an imposition by many people in our society. This underlying attitude, which no one—except the AfD—publicly articulates, leads to a situation where only a charade of action is taken for marginalized groups. In reality, nothing changes. This widespread tokenism is a disgrace because so much money is wasted without any tangible results.  
  
Meanwhile, there are still far too many violations of human rights and physical integrity in marginalized communities.  
  
It is simply unbelievable what is currently being done to children born deaf in wealthy Western countries. Medicine has invented the cochlear implant, and now every baby diagnosed as severely hard of hearing or deaf shortly after birth has it implanted in a major, expensive operation. This involves a lot of money, and the clinics are profiting handsomely. It's completely unclear whether these children are actually benefiting from it. And what's even worse: under pressure from doctors, parents have stopped communicating with their children using sign language. This is currently leading to what's called a language-induced intellectual disability in these children because they receive too little linguistic input, preventing their linguistic and cognitive systems from developing properly. If the child then doesn't develop as desired—a situation the doctors, by the way, have no control over and for which they assume no responsibility—unvalid diagnostic tools are used, and the children, who are actually only deaf and would develop cognitively quite normally with sign language, are then diagnosed with "intellectual disability." This is how these children end up in special education schools for people with learning difficulties, where they receive no sign language input at all, and the input they get with their cochlear implant is deficient in spoken language. This means that healthy, typical children who would have experienced normal cognitive development with sign language are suffering irreversible cognitive and neurological damage as a result of this practice. They later end up in institutions or psychiatric hospitals.  
  
It is not only outrageous but simply scandalous that we are currently experiencing an epidemic of language deprivation. The World Federation of the Deaf (https://signhealth.org.uk/wp-content/uploads/2024/08/2022-Position-paper-on-access-to-national-sign-languages-as-a-health-need-World-Federation-of-the-Deaf.pdf) and the National Association of the Deaf (https://www.nad.org/language-deprivation/) have long been pointing this out. Deaf people are not heard, even though they should have a voice.

<u>Original title (de)</u> : Epidemie der Sprachdeprivation

<u>Original content (de)</u> :

Ich stelle immer wieder fest, dass öffentliche Institutionen, seien es Verwaltung oder Bildungsinstitutionen, Inklusion nicht wirklich unterstützen. Die UN-BRK wurde ratifiziert, aber alles, was verändert werden muss, wird von vielen Menschen in unserer Gesellschaft als Zumutung empfunden. Diese innere Haltung, die keiner – außer der AfD - laut artikuliert– führt dazu, dass nur so getan wird, als ob man etwas für marginalisierte Gruppen tut. In Wahrheit ändert sich nichts. Dieser weit verbreitete Tokenismus ist eine Schande, weil so unheimlich viel Geld verschwendet wird, ohne dass etwas dabei herumkommt.   
  
Dabei gibt es noch immer viel zu viele Verstöße gegen die Menschenrechte und die körperliche Unversehrtheit in marginalisierten Communitys.   
  
Es ist schlicht unglaublich, was beispielsweise derzeit taub geborenen Kindern in den westlichen reichen Ländern angetan wird. In der Medizin hat man das Cochlea-Implantat erfunden und nun wird es jedem Baby, das kurz nach der Geburt als hochgradig schwerhörig oder taub diagnostiziert wird, in einer großen, teuren OP eingepflanzt. Da geht es um viel Geld, und die Kliniken verdienen gut daran. Es ist völlig unklar, ob diese Kinder überhaupt davon profitieren. Und was noch viel schlimmer ist: Eltern haben auf Druck der Ärzte aufgehört, mit ihren Kindern gebärdensprachlich zu kommunizieren. Das führt aktuell zu einer sogenannten sprachlich induzierten geistigen Behinderung bei den Kindern, weil sie zu wenig sprachlichen Input bekommen und ihr sprachliches, kognitives System sich nicht entfalten kann. Wenn das Kind sich dann nicht so entwickelt, wie gewünscht, womit die erste übrigens dann nichts mehr zu tun haben und dafür auch keine Verantwortung übernehmen, werden irgendwelche nicht validen Diagnostik-Instrumente herangezogen und die Kinder, die eigentlich nur taub sind, und sich mit Gebärdensprache kognitiv ganz normal entwickeln würden, bekommen dann die Diagnose "geistig behindert". So landen die Kinder in Förderschulen für Menschen mit Lernschwierigkeiten, wo sie gar keinen gebärdensprachlichen Input mehr bekommen und der Input mit dem CI auf lautsprachlicher Ebene defizitär ist. Das bedeutet, dass gesunde normale Kinder, die mit einer Gebärdensprache eine normale kognitive Entwicklung genommen hätten, durch diese Praxis einen kognitiven neurologischen Schaden erleiden, der niemals wieder gutzumachen ist. Sie landen später in Heimen oder in der Psychiatrie.  
Es ist nicht nur empörend, sondern einfach skandalös, dass es aktuell zu einer Epidemie der Sprachdeprivation kommt. Darauf weist die "World Federation of the Deaf" ( https://signhealth.org.uk/wp-content/uploads/2024/08/2022-Position-paper-on-access-to-national-sign-languages-as-a-health-need-World-Federation-of-the-Deaf.pdf )und die 'National Association of the Deaf' ( https://www.nad.org/language-deprivation/ )schon lange hin. Taube Menschen werden nicht gehört, obwohl sie eine Stimme haben sollten.

## 550. Shaping the future together: A Europe for people and the environment

1. Volt advocates for the comprehensive digitalization of government processes, which should be accessible, transparent, and resource-efficient. The goal is to create an efficient administration that serves citizens as a service provider and minimizes unnecessary bureaucracy.  
  
2. Volt supports an ambitious climate strategy and calls for an end to subsidies for CO₂-intensive structures. The saved tax revenue should be invested in sustainable projects to achieve climate goals and enable the phase-out of coal by 2030.  
  
3. Volt promotes access to education and champions values ​​such as social cohesion and respect for diversity. Integration in Germany and Europe is an important aspect that is supported by education.  
  
4. Volt calls for a comprehensive immigration law and advocates for a progressive integration policy. Integration should be seen as a task for society as a whole, promoting respectful coexistence and enabling access to social services for all.  
  
5. Volt supports government funding and financing of critical infrastructure, particularly in the energy sector. The transition to sustainable and CO₂-neutral energy sources is to be secured through government investment.

2. Volt befürwortet eine ehrgeizige Klimastrategie und fordert den Stopp von Subventionen für CO₂-intensive Strukturen. Die eingesparten Steuermittel sollen in nachhaltige Projekte investiert werden, um die Klimaziele zu erreichen und den Kohleausstieg bis 2030 zu ermöglichen

## 551. Loss of tolerance

Germany and the world were more progressive in the 1970s to 1990s: hippies, punks, and artists dressed and made up as women—this was imitated. ## 552. Gender Bias, Chauvinism in the Dutch Labour Market

As a woman of 60 who built a career in IT and worked her way honestly to leadership level, I moved to Netherlands, and find that I am not taken seriously when applying for a senior role.  I know the language, culture, and have a Dutch passport.  There are no barriers to working at my career level. And yet, I have been unemployed over a year, have experienced a great deal of sexism from male hiring managers and male CEO's as interviewers. I note, no women in the process other than the secretary, and I hear statements of bias that are cringeworthy. And I hear those statements alone, which adds to my streee.   When Dutch companies want a seasoned expert on their board or running their department, they find they have confidence in a man, regardless of skills, experience, or seniority, and declare that they hire the "best &amp; brightest regardless of gender". There may be a smaller pay gap than in my mother's generation, however, there is less career mobility: women are 8% of C-level in the EU, less in IT, even if we comprise 47% of the entry level. Experts tell me to go to LinkedIn (everybody did already), and yet, in my experience as a woman, "equal rights" does not translate to my experience in the Dutch labour market. What a waste of human potential.

## 556. Cynical politics

Donald Trump recently won the American elections. The America First policy, expressions of hatred, the belittling of population groups, lying about others, and the smearing of the media cast a somber light on the situation. The shock during Trump's first election was great; his victory this time is far greater, yet the shock seems smaller. There is a sense of normalization. In the Netherlands and in Europe, we are going to suffer even more from Trump and the US stance on the world stage. However, this is not an isolated incident. I find the parallels that can now be drawn with Dutch politics sad. Should the cabinet fall tonight, the gains made by the (extreme) right will only increase. Meanwhile, the centrist and left-wing parties are failing to make concrete enough what they will mean for the ordinary man and woman on the street. It is mainly about the 'how' (with or without Europe, etc.), not about the 'why' and 'what'. The major themes, the vision, and the result remain largely absent. Is the PVV voter screaming loudly about this? Not as far as I know. People seem quite satisfied with merely a message without results. Other politicians could learn something from this, unfortunately.

<u>Original title (nl)</u> : Cynische politiek

<u>Original content (nl)</u> :

Onlangs won Donald Trump de Amerikaanse verkiezingen. De America first politiek, uitingen van haat, het kleineren van bevolkingsgroepen, het liegen over anderen en het zwart maken van media stemmen somber. Bij de eerste verkiezing van Trump was de schok groot, zijn winst is dit keer vele mate groter maar de schokt lijkt kleiner. Er is sprake van gewenning. In Nederland en in Europa gaan we nog meer last krijgen van Trump en de stellingname van de VS op het wereld toneel. Dit staat echter niet op zichzelf. Treurig vind ik de parallellen die inmiddels met de NL politiek zijn te trekken. Mocht het kabinet vanavond vallen dan zal de winst van (extreem) rechts alleen maar groter worden. Ondertussen weten de midden partijen en linkse partijen onvoldoende concreet te maken wat ze voor de gewone man en vrouw op de straat gaan betekenen. Het gaat vooral over het hoe (met of zonder Europa etc), niet over het Why en What. De grote thema’s, de visie, het resultaat blijft toch wel grotendeels uit. Wordt er hard over gegild door de PVV stemmer? Niet voor zover ik weet. Men lijkt wel tevreden te zijn met enkel een boodschap zonder resultaat. Andere politici kunnen hier nog wat van leren, helaas.

## 558. Autism in our current healthcare system

I suspect I have ASD (Autism Spectrum Disorder). This suspicion was confirmed by an autism counseling center. However, the official diagnosis must be made by a psychiatrist. The problem is: no one in the field of psychiatry who I can reach can treat or diagnose me because no one is familiar with it. Specialists and therapists are overwhelmed because health insurance companies aren't issuing new practice licenses, meaning there are too few practitioners. Consequently, many patients are vying for the few available practices. This leaves no time for practitioners to familiarize themselves with new, less familiar health topics (e.g., autism).  
  
My daily life is severely limited; I can barely go shopping, can't hold down a job long-term, and can't study, even though I'm intellectually above average. There are government-funded support services for autistic people, but you only receive them with a corresponding diagnosis.  
  
Psychiatrists and psychotherapists refuse treatment as soon as they hear the word "autism."  
  
The few specialists in the field of autism have waiting lists of up to two years and are very difficult for me to reach. I need someone to accompany me to appointments. Due to work commitments and family members requiring care, there is no one in my immediate circle who could accompany me. State-funded support is only available with a confirmed diagnosis.  
  
According to German statistics, I now live in poverty. I know that I am fundamentally capable of leading a relatively independent life, but I need support and assistance with daily living activities for a while to achieve this independence. Even just a disability card would help me. But even for that, I have to provide the corresponding diagnoses and expert opinions.  
  
Conclusion:  
  
More funds must be made available for psychiatric/psychological treatment services. Furthermore, the limit on the number of psychiatric/psychotherapeutic practices imposed by public health insurance companies must be lifted. Medical care must not be restricted! That should be more important than the car and coal industries.

<u>Original title (de)</u> : Autismus in unserem derzeitigen Gesundheitssystem

<u>Original content (de)</u> :

Ich habe den Verdacht, dass ich ASS (Autismusspektrumstörung) habe. Dieser Verdacht wurde von einer Beratungsstelle für Autismus bestätigt. Die offizielle Diagnose muss aber durch eine*n Psychiater*in erfolgen. Das Problem: Niemand aus dem Fachbereich Psychiatrie, der für mich erreichbar ist, kann mich behandeln/diagnostizieren, weil sich niemand damit auskennt. Die Fachärzt*innen und Therapeut*innen sind überlastet, weil von den Krankenkassen keine neuen Praxisgenehmigungen ausgestellt werden, sprich es gibt zu wenige Behandler*innen. Entsprechend kommen viele Patient*innen auf die wenigen vorhandenen Praxen. So bleibt keine Zeit für Behandler*innen, um sich in neue, weniger bekannte Gesundheitsthemen (z. B. Autismus) einzuarbeiten.  
  
Ich bin im Alltag stark eingeschränkt, kann kaum einkaufen gehen, keinen Job langfristig halten, kann nicht studieren, obwohl ich intellektuell überdurchschnittlich bin. Es gibt staatlich geförderte Unterstützungsangebote für Autist*innen. Die bekommt man aber nur mit einer entsprechenden Diagnose.  
Psychiater*innen und Psychotherapeut*innen lehnen die Behandlung ab, sobald sie das Wort "Autismus" hören.  
  
Die wenigen Spezialist*innen im Bereich Autismus haben eine Wartezeit von bis zu 2 Jahren und sind für mich sehr schlecht erreichbar. Ich brauche eine Begleitperson, um die Termine wahrzunehmen. In meinem Umfeld gibt es aufgrund von Arbeitstätigkeit und Pflegefällen in der Familie niemanden, der mich begleiten könnte. Eine staatlich geförderte Begleitung bekomme ich auch wieder nur mit gestellter Diagnose.  
  
Ich lebe mittlerweile laut deutscher Statistik in Armut. Ich weiß, dass ich prinzipiell in der Lage bin, ein halbwegs selbstständiges Leben zu führen, benötige aber für einige Zeit Unterstützung und Alltagsbegleitung, um diese Selbstständigkeit zu erlangen. Schon allein ein Schwerbehindertenausweis würde mir helfen. Aber auch hierfür muss ich die entsprechenden Diagnosen und Gutachten vorweisen.  
  
Fazit:  
Es müssen mehr Gelder für psychiatrische/psychologische Behandlungsangebote freigemacht werden. Außerdem muss die Begrenzung der Anzahl an psychiatrischen/psychotherapeutischen Praxen durch die staatlichen Krankenkassen aufgehoben werden. Medizinische Versorgung darf nicht eingeschränkt werden! Das sollte wichtiger sein, als die Auto- und Kohleindustrie.

## 559. The "asshole" poster polarizes party members: Time for a cross-generational debate

My political party used a campaign poster in the last election with the slogan "Don't be an asshole, don't vote for the far right." I was disappointed and outraged that my party was creating such blatant enemy images. After some hesitation, I decided to speak out publicly because I had encountered similar rejection of this type of communication in conversations with people over 50. My call to keep the poster in the basement sparked a lively debate. And I sensed a clear difference between the younger and older generations. Younger people generally found the poster positive because it took a clear stance. Older people, for the most part, found the language repulsive and the condemnation of those with differing opinions misguided. This experience showed me, among other things, that my party needs to engage more with the older generation and their thought patterns in order to successfully convey the party's predominantly positive message and vision to this voter group in the long term.

<u>Original title (de)</u> : Das Aschloch Poster polarisiert Parteimitglieder: Zeit für eine generationsübergreifende Debatte

<u>Original content (de)</u> :

Meine politischen Partei hat ein Wahlkampfposter mit Aufschrift „sei kein Aschloch, wähle nichts rechtsextrem" im letzten Wahlkampf verwendet. Ich war enttäuscht und empört, dass meine Partei in dieser plakativen Form Feindbilder schafft. Nach einigem Zögern beschloss ich mich dazu auch öffentlich zu äußern, weil ich in Gesprächen mit Menschen der älteren Generation über 50 eine ähnliche Ablehnung dieser Art der Kommunikation erfahren hatte. Mein Aufruf, dieses Poster das im Keller zu lassen löste eine lebendige Debatte aus. Und ich spürte dass hier ein deutlicher Unterschied zwischen der jüngeren und älteren Generation besteht. Jüngere Menschen fand im allgemeinen das Poster positiv, weil es klare Kante zeigt. Ältere Menschen fanden überwiegend die Sprache abstoßend und die darin beinhaltete Verurteilung Andersdenkender Menschen für verkehrt. Diese Erfahrung zeigte mir, unter anderem, dass meine Partei sich stärker mit der älteren Generation und ihren Denkmustern beschäftigen muss, um langfristig auch in dieser Wählergruppe die überwiegend positive Botschaft und Vision der Partei erfolgreich zu vermitteln.

## 561. Unwittingly a “fundamentalist”

## 564. Livability falls victim to commercial decisions

The only supermarket (Jumbo) in our village closed last month. It was doing well, but because another Jumbo opened in a large town just across the border with Belgium, 8 km away, the management decided to close down here. Now there is only a fruit shop and a butcher. For me, this is merely an inconvenience. I have a car. But a considerable number of residents do not have one and cannot cycle. For them, it is a disaster. The nearest supermarket is 8 km away – and you can only take the bus at the beginning and end of the day (there is only a school bus during the school period, or you have to order a stop bus 2 hours in advance). The streets are also much emptier; there was always a constant coming and going of Dutch and Belgian customers. I think this is having a negative effect on the quality of life in our village.

<u>Original title (nl)</u> : Leefbaarheid de dupe van commerciële beslissingen

<u>Original content (nl)</u> :

De enige supermarkt (Jumbo) in ons dorp is gesloten afgelopen maand. Hij draaide prima maar omdat er in een grote plaats net over de grens met België, op 8 km afstand, ook een Jumbo opende heeft de directie besloten dat ze hier stoppen. Er is nu alleen nog een fruithuisje en een slager. Voor mij is dit slechts lastig. Ik heb een auto. Maar een behoorlijk aantal inwoners heeft dat niet en kan niet fietsen. Voor hen een drama. De dichtstbijzijnde super is op 8 km - en met de bus kan alleen aan begin en eind van de dag (er is alleen in de schoolperiode een scholierenbus of je moet 2 uur tevoren een haltebus bestellen). de straten zijn ook veel leger; het was altijd een af en aan rijden van NL en B klanten. Ik denk dat dit een negatief effect heeft op de leefbaarheid in onze plaats.

## 568. Web portals place impossible demands on the digital skills of older people.

I helped an elderly lady who wanted to sell her oversized home and move to a rental apartment. The bureaucracy she faced was dreadful. It was impossible for her to complete the registration via a web portal. We spent two hours working on it together, and she still wasn't registered. First, she had to create an account with the rental agent. She had to expose her entire personal and financial life. This had to be done through an intermediary (which also required creating another account first), whom she had to authorize via DigiID to gather all her information from various government websites: the Tax Authorities, the Land Registry, the Population Register, the Social Security Administration, and so on. For many older people, it is an impossible task to arrange a move in this way. Furthermore, I wonder if it is desirable that so much information is requested from and stored from a potential tenant in this manner.

<u>Original title (nl)</u> : Webportalen stellen onmogelijke eisen aan de digitale vaardigheden van oudere mensen.

<u>Original content (nl)</u> :

Ik heb een ouder mevrouw geholpen die haar te grote eigen huis wil verkopen en naar een huurflat wil verhuizen. De bureaucratie waarmee ze geconfronteerd werd was afgrijselijk. Voor haar was het ondoenlijk om via een webportaal de inschrijving tot een goed einde te brengen. Twee uur zijn we samen bezig geweest en nog was ze niet ingeschreven. Eerst moest ze een account aanmaken bij de verhuurmakelaar. Ze moest haar hele persoonlijke en financiële leven bloot geven. Dit moest verplicht via een tussenpersoon (ook eerst weer een account aanmaken) die ze via DigiID moest machtigen om al haar informatie van diverse overheidswebsites bij elkaar te schrapen. Belasting, Kadaster, bevolkingsregister, SVB enzovoort. Voor veel oudere mensen is het een onmogelijke opgave om op deze manier een verhuizing voor elkaar te krijgen. Daarnaast vraag ik me af of het gewenst is dat op deze manier zo veel informatie van een potentiële huurder wordt gevraagd en opgeslagen.

## 569. British expat and the German border

I am a British citizen living in Germany with a German residence permit. For residents, the electronic passport gates work at German border control. More than once I have been stopped by border guards before reaching the gate, who tell me that as my passport is British and I am not an EU citizen the gate won't work. Each time I first explain that I am resident in Germany before then demonstrating that the gate does work for me. Mildy annoying but better than the long queue for a person.  
When I moved back to Germany after living in Switzerland, I simply drove over the border without getting an entry stamp. When I travelled whilst waiting for my residence permit to be processed, the German border guard was very confused how a British citizen managed to have a German exit stamp but no entry stamp. After a long discussion and pointing out that my temporary visa was issued from the German embassy in Bern, I was finally let through. Such things happen post-Brexit.

## 571. In villages you can build communities

We went to city hall in the small village (45.000 people) of where we moved to in July of this year, in order to apply for our German citizenship. While we were with the civil servant who was reviewing our documents, our kids left the private office and went the larger open office area. They started talking with one of the female civil servants and she "entertained" them, our twins are 5yo, while my wife and I finished up the process for our application. By the time we came out, the nice lady knew our kids names and everyone was in a good mood. It felt like they would remember us next time we would have to come to city hall for something. It felt like here, in the village, you can get to know people as opposed to the bigger city where we lived before.

## 574. Barriers and fears in my life

I enjoy living in my country and welcome everyone who, like me, follows the rules. Equal rights and equal opportunities for all would be my wish. But alongside wonderful moments of consideration, like the bus driver who helped a blind person, I'm experiencing increasing disrespect towards others. Walking home alone as a woman is sometimes just an unpleasant experience, but there have also been situations where I felt afraid. The rise of right-wing populism also worries me, as I have a migration background.  
  
And for me personally, as a visually impaired person, there are so many obstacles that most people aren't aware of and that play no role in politics. Sometimes I feel abandoned and powerless.

Aber ich erlebe neben sehr schönen Momenten der Rücksichtnahme wie zum Beispiel der Busfahrer, der einem blinden Menschen hilft, immer mehr Respektlosigkeit anderen Mitmenschen gegenüber. Der Nachhauseweg alleine als Frau ist manchmal nur eine unangenehme Erfahrung, aber es kam auch schon zu Situationen, wo ich Angst hatte. Auch die Zunahme von Rechtspopulismus macht mir Sorgen, da ich einen Migrationshintergrund habe.  
Und für mich persönlich als Sehbehinderte gibt es so viele Hürden, die den meisten Menschen nicht bewusst sind und in der Politik keine Rolle spielen. Da fühle ich mich manchmal alleine gelassen und ohnmächtig.

## 575. Bureaucratic madness in health insurance for self-employed people from abroad

I still don't have health insurance, despite it supposedly being mandatory in Germany. I'm amazed at how difficult it is to get health insurance when you move here from abroad as a self-employed person. You'd think that founders would be in high demand in Germany as potential employers, but instead, the interminable bureaucracy and far too many levels of expertise required in every aspect make settling in incredibly difficult.  
  
Take the aforementioned health insurance problem, for example. As a self-employed person, you're not required to have health insurance if you're coming from abroad, and even voluntary statutory insurance isn't so easy. So you think you can get private insurance, because that should be possible somehow. Not a chance. You enter your information online, then you get a call from an insurance agent, with whom you have five meetings before it finally goes to the risk department, where the information is interpreted differently, resulting in the insurance being rejected. Then you ask if the relevant condition can simply be excluded. Then it all goes back again and you wait and wait and can't even get health insurance in this shitty country.

<u>Original title (de)</u> : Bürokratischer Irrsinn in der Krankenversicherung für Selbstständige aus dem Ausland

<u>Original content (de)</u> :

Ich hab ja immer noch keine Krankenversicherung, trotz angeblicher Pflicht in Deutschland. Wie schwierig es ist krankenversichert zu werden, wenn man als Selbstständiger aus dem Ausland herzieht hat mich fasziniert. Man sollte ja meinen, dass gerade Gründer in Deutschland massiv gesucht werden, als potentielle Arbeitgeber, aber stattdessen macht die unsägliche Bürokratie und viel zu viele Level von Kompetenzen in jedem Aspekt das Ankommen hier unglaublich schwer.  
Beispielsweise oben genannte Krankenversicherungsproblematik. Man ist als Selbstständiger nicht pflichtversichert, wenn man aus dem Ausland kommt, ist auch eine freiwillige gesetzliche Versicherung nicht so einfach möglich. Also denkt man sich, man versichert sich privat, weil das ja irgendwie gehen sollte. Pustekuchen. Man gibt online Daten an, dann wird man von einem Versicherungsvertreter angerufen, mit welchem man 5 Meetings hat, bis es dann an die Risikoabteilung geht, dort werden die Angaben anders interpretiert, sodass die Versicherung abgelehnt wird. Dann frägt man nach, ob die entsprechende Condition nicht einfach ausgeschlossen werden kann. Dann geht das wieder zurück und man wartet und wartet und kriegt in diesem Scheißland nichtmal ne Krankenversicherung.

## 580. The oppression of youth

Young people aren't listened to when they talk about their concerns. That was true when I was a teenager, and it's still true today.  
  
For example, I'm hearing from more and more young people that they're tired of being addicted to screen time. They know they're addicted, but they can't break free. At the same time, the education system believes that schools must become increasingly digital. There's an online classroom for every subject where assignments have to be posted and submitted, etc. Online tutoring is being pushed by tutoring agencies. The one thing young people aren't getting is a solid digital education. They don't want to be glued to screens so much, but they're being forced to. Who would have thought this 30 years ago, when people said that young people weren't going outside anymore and that they were getting "square eyes" from watching TV?  
  
This is just one of hundreds of examples. Whether it's about education policy, mental health, or whatever else: the concerns of young people are dismissed as inferior by adults—politicians and everyone else—or simply ignored. What are young people supposed to know? They are forced into a system by adults that oppresses them. This has to stop.

<u>Original title (de)</u> : Die Unterdrückung der Jugend

<u>Original content (de)</u> :

Man hört Jugendlichen nicht zu, wenn sie über ihre Anliegen sprechen. Das war schon so, als ich Jugendlicher war, und es ist immer noch so.   
Beispielsweise höre ich von immer mehr Jugendlichen, dass sie es leid sind, süchtig nach Bildschirmzeit zu sein. Sie wissen, dass sie süchtig sind, aber kommen nicht weg davon. Gleichzeitig ist das Bildungssystem er Meinung, die Schule muss immer digitaler werden. Für jedes Fach gibt es einen Online-Klassenraum, wo Aufgaben gestellt und abgegeben werden müssen etc. Online-Nachhilfe wird von Nachhilfeinstituten forciert. Das einzige, was die Jugendlichen nicht mitkriegen, ist eine fundierte digitale Bildung. Sie wollen nicht so viel am Bildschirm kleben, werden aber dazu gezwungen. Wer hätte sich das vor 30 Jahren  gedacht, als es hieß, die Jugendlichen gehen nicht mehr raus und sie bekämen "viereckige Augen" vom Fernsehen?   
Das ist nur eines von hunderten Beispielen. Egal ob es um Bildungspolitik, mentale Gesundheit, oder was auch immer geht: Die Anliegen der Jugendlichen werden von Erwachsenen – der Politik wie aller anderen – als minderwertig abgetan oder gar nicht erst gehört. Was sollen Jugendliche schon wissen? Sie werden von Erwachsenen in ein System gepresst, das sie unterdrückt. Das muss endlich aufhören.

## 582. Taking the train to Paris.

My girlfriend is from the United States and she absolutely loves Paris. When she first visited me earlier this year (2024) I made sure to book tickets to Paris for us.  
We walked to the station got on the train to France and then got on the HSR and were in Paris within 2h no problems. We walked to our hotel and spent a lovely few days there.  
The ease of travel, crossing the border with no problems, train infrastructure and the fact there was a high speed connection at all surprised her and made her love Europe. She now absolutely wants to live in Europe with me, something she wasn't entirely sure of before visiting.  
Now seeing Schengen being used as a suggestion to be ignored, borders reappearing and the Commission just letting that happen with no consequence for the countries that destroy something we worked so hard to create... it deeply worries me that experiences like these will disappear in the future

<u>Unique identifier</u> : eurosense

<u>Question</u> : Why hesitate when our grandparents didn't? The Treaty of Rome was bold and wishful, the Maastricht Treaty was progressive and left room to grow,...  
Now it's troubling times where those who wish to destroy what we've done are emboldened by our fear. Why hesitate? What's at risk is greater than anything we've ever done in our lives. So why hesitate?

## 583. They'll never see you as just another one of them

I live abroad and often feel like I have to prove, every day, in every action, that I deserve to live here. I feel like I have to be more excellent, a better citizen, a better worker than anyone else. And even though I have the same rights and pay my taxes, the migration experience makes you a second-class citizen (and I'm European in a European country, so my friends and students from the Global South experience this with even more anxiety). For example, at work, I'm not considered for positions of greater responsibility than I'm capable of handling, as my past experiences demonstrate, because my command of the local language isn't profound, and yet everyone speaks English, which is our common language and which I speak perfectly.

## 587. Mediation versus cultural appropriation

A very difficult situation. I was brought in as a service provider to  play a very small role in using complexity thinking to mediate the Israeli-Palestinian conflict. The people who commissioned my services were Americans. On the call were Americas, Brits, Israelis and Palestinians. A Palestinian woman who was part of the process became enraged at the service we were providing yet was gracious enough to apologise to me afterwards. I felt sick thinking about how much space she holds for others even as a bulls-eye is painted on her back. I am a British woman of Irish descent. My great-grandmother had to hide in her back-garden from murderous British soldiers. My grandma who moved to England faced a lifetime of brutal prejudice. She had to live with the paradoxical decision of fleeing to the UK to escape the British occupation of Ireland. Her children and grandchildren are of course Brits. She tried to distance us from our Irish roots to gain us freedom.  For example she pretended she could not speak the Irish language even though she had to learn English as a second language as a child. This felt like a betrayal at first. I would ask her about a Gaelic word that she had carved on the house. She would say "I don't know." I later found out, after she had passed, that that word translated meant "freedom" in Gaelic. I couldn't understand why she wouldn't tell me. I'm technically still an EU citizen by virtue of my Irish roots though I haven't applied for the Irish passport to which I'm entitled yet. I'm somehow more acutely aware of my difference from other Brits and the prejudice I face post-Brexit. I remember The Guardian (supposedly a progressive newspaper) publishing a column commenting on every 'Tom, Mick and Paddy' applying for an Irish passport post-Brexit. This is a play on the British expression "Tom, Dick and Harry" meaning everyone (Thomas, Richard, Harry are very common English names) and the racial slur against the Irish ("Micks and Paddys" being a common slur.) Of course though that racism has always been there. I find the pro-european sentiment in my country uncomfortable post-Brexit. Are you asking me to identify with immigrants (I do)? Are you asking me to identify with people because they are white (I don't)? I guess Im sharing all this to say that even in our small corner of Europe things are so complicated and so small and volatile. Don't forget us because en masse we voted to Leave. Don't forget the value of seeing our shared humanity. It's not about us being Europeans. It's about us being human beings. 

<u>Origin</u> : Other  
<u>Language</u> : en  
<u>Unique identifier</u> :   
<u>EU is like</u> : A non-existent non-entity arrogant and distant. Irrelevant.  
<u>Europe is like</u> : A concept that my grandparents hated and which I have been encouraged to hate. Nevertheless, I want to see it. I want Pan-Europeanism.   
<u>Democracy is like</u> : For the love of God. Give the dispossesed a voice! Stop pretending genocide and tax rates belong in a pro/anti column about who to vote for!!  
<u>Who should hear this</u> : European bureaucrats who think they are above listening to the people of Europe.

## 592. Democracy in Peril: A Growing Fear for Our Future

I have to tell you, I'm really scared right now. Last September, SMER won the election here in Slovakia, and I just can't shake this feeling of dread. There are rumours that Fico wants to copy how elections are done in Belarus, and it's terrifying. This isn't how democracy is supposed to work. And now, on top of that, Trump has won the elections in the US. It feels like the world is shifting in a way that's so dangerous for democratic values. Leaders who seem to thrive on division and control are gaining power, and it's like we're watching these foundational principles erode in real-time.  
I can’t help but think about how fragile democracy is, and how quickly things can spiral if we don’t push back. I’m worried about what kind of future we’re heading into not just for us but for the next generation too

## 593. The municipality disregards the participation process with the neighborhood and unilaterally changes a plan with a very negative impact on local residents.

I served on the advisory group for a housing project in our neighborhood. We went through an intensive participation process in which a plan was adopted by the city council that all stakeholders could agree on—a balance between housing and greenery in our very built-up neighborhood.  
  
As an advisory group, we were subsequently very unpleasantly surprised because the municipality suddenly had a plan to replace the greenery with a four-story above-ground parking garage in the middle of a residential area, meaning that many homes would suddenly be facing a parking garage instead of a small green park. This had not been communicated, and it was suddenly a fait accompli... A negative experience, therefore.

<u>Original title (nl)</u> : Gemeente heeft lak aan participatietraject met de buurt en veranderd eenzijdig een plan met zeer negatieve impact op omwonenden

<u>Original content (nl)</u> :

Ik heb in de klankbordgroep gezeten van een woningbouwproject in onze wijk. We hebben een intensief participatietraject doorlopen waarbij een plan is vastgesteld door de gemeenteraad waar alle betrokkenen zich in konden vinden, een afweging tussen woningbouw en groen in onze zeer versteende wijk.  
We werden vervolgens als klankbordgroep zeer onaangenaam verrast omdat de gemeente opeen een plan had om het groen te vervangen voor een vierlaags bovengrondse parkeergarage in het midden van een woonwijk waardoor veel woningen in plaats van een groen parkje opeens tegen een parkeergarage aankijken. Hier was niet over gecommuniceerd, en was opeens een voldongen feit... Een negatieve ervaring dus.

## 595. Three reasons not to engage in political/ social discussion

I notice that with political discussions I tend to withdraw and hold back. One motivation for that is that I don't want to engage at the level of exchanging opinions, most of all, when the views expressed are superficial and somewhat triggered. It's like this is lost energy. A second motivation for not engaging is the apparent lack of a debating culture in our society. People are no longer (have they ever?) willing to engage in real debate and really listen to other people's viewpoints that are unlike their own - with an openness to explore and some curiosity.  The Corona times in Germany was a terrible period, people could not state their viewpoints and positions without being marginalised, categorised, or stigmatized - sometimes with incredible social, financial and health consequences. I guess that shock is still in my system.  A third motivation for not engaging: generally, people are not really well informed about what is going on. Too much information, misinformation or biased information around.

## 597. Change in society, how is this accepted?

KOZP is celebrating its 10th anniversary this year. A gathering was held to look back on everything that has happened over those 10 years. And during this meeting, you notice that steps have been taken to bring about change in society through demonstrations and lectures. However, there is still a kind of misunderstanding, ignorance, and stubbornness regarding change and listening to one another—where the sore point lies. It is not yet present everywhere. As a result, quite intense reactions can arise from opponents, even bordering on violence such as name-calling.  
  
Nevertheless, I remain positive and am always open to dialogue.

Maar dat er nog steeds een soort onbegrip, onwetendheid, koppigheid voor veranderingen en luisteren naar elkaar, waar het pijn punt zit. Nog niet overal zit. Waardoor en nog al heftige reacties van tegenstanders kunnen komen, tot bijna geweld als uitschelden.   
Toch blijf ik positief en sta altijd open voor een dialoog.

## 599. A lack of a vision for the future

With the recent national elections, I was surprised by how willing people were to vote for centre-right or right-wing parties. I experienced deep divisions pitting us versus them. The "them" comprised a motley collection of characteristics that, depending on the issue, differed from "our" perceptions of issues. The general tone was that nothing worked anymore; it was all very anti-political.  
On a deeper level, people held a vague idea about things being better in the past and could not specify how they saw the future. There was nothing concrete; there was no sentiment of hope.

## 601. Expat Odyssey

I moved from Italy to Brussels this September, only moving into my home in October. Since then, the registration process at the Brussels-City town hall has proven particularly complicated (despite the fact that, in theory, it should be a breeze for EU citizens enjoying freedom of movement). I'm caught between two fires: the manager of my residence, who asks me to register with the municipality without having to register (otherwise I risk eviction), and the municipal offices, who maintain that registering as a domicile is the only possible procedure (if I don't do that, I risk a fine from the Belgian authorities if they find me without the documents proving my domicile).

<u>Original title (it)</u> : Odissea expat

<u>Original content (it)</u> :

Mi sono trasferita dall’Italia a Bruxelles questo settembre, entrando in casa solo ad ottobre. Da allora il procedimento per la registrazione al municipio di Bruxelles-Ville si sta dimostrando particolarmente complicato (in barba al fatto che, in linea teorica, dovrebbe essere una cosa da poco per l3 cittadin3 UE che godono della libertà di movimento). Sono tra due fuochi: il gestore della mia residenza che mi chiede di registrarmi al comune senza domiciliarmi (altrimenti rischio lo sfratto) e gli uffici comunali che sostengono che la domiciliazione sia l’unica procedura possibile (se non faccio quella, rischio una multa dalle autorità belghe nel caso in cui mi trovassero senza i documenti sull’avvenuta domiciliazione).

## 617. Homelessness and trust in society

My story is about homelessness:  
  
In my city, where I live, people often sit on the street begging for money. I used to give them some small change now and then. Then one day, my roommate told me he'd seen a woman being driven to her "begging spot" by car early in the morning. In his opinion, she wasn't homeless, but part of an organized group posing as beggars. Since hearing this from my roommate, I've become much more skeptical and no longer give money to people begging.  
  
I'm asking myself questions like: How can we build trust instead of distrust towards the most vulnerable members of society? How can we combat homelessness in general?

<u>Original title (de)</u> : Obdachlosigkeit und Vertrauen in der Gesellschaft

<u>Original content (de)</u> :

Meine Geschichte bezieht sich auf Obdachlosigkeit:  
In meiner Stadt in der ich wohne sitzen oft Menschen auf der Straße, die um Geld betteln. Früher habe ich ab und zu etwas Kleingeld gegeben. Bis eines Tages mein Mitbewohner erzählt hat, er habe gesehen, wie eine Frau am frühen Morgen von einem Auto zu ihrem „Bettelplatz“ gefahren wird. Seiner Ansicht nach war sie also keine Obdachlose, sondern Teil einer organisierten Gruppe, die sich als Bettler ausgeben. Seitdem ich diese Ansicht von meinem Mitbewohner gehört habe, bin ich viel skeptischer geworden und gebe kein Geld mehr zu bettelnden Personen.  
In meinem Kopf sind Fragen wie: Wie können wir in der Gesellschaft Vertrauen statt Misstrauen gegenüber den schwächsten der Gesellschaft aufbauen? Wie können wir allgemein Obdachlosigkeit bekämpfen?

## 634. My extraordinary life

In fact, I am proud to be a world citizen but more than that, I am proud to be a European citizen.   
Born on the African continent, I am French but I leave in Germany. My husband is from East Ukraine (Dombass). Through our marriage, we avoided him having fighting against his own people.   
My children have the German nationality. My dog is a ex street dog from Romania. My best friend is from former Yougoslavia. We share our home with a expatriated worker from Hungary.   
I studied partially in the US, in Germany and of course in France.  These are roughly good reasons for me being part of VOLT because of the European spirit.

## 645. Hospital, healthcare

It was a weekday afternoon. All the doctors' offices were closed, I was experiencing severe chest pains, and I wanted to see a doctor. The emergency hotline told me they couldn't refer me to an ambulance until 7 p.m. The pain worsened, and eventually, I couldn't breathe. My husband tried to call an ambulance, but no one was available, so he had to drive me to the hospital himself. He and our young daughter had to wait there.

Mein Mann versuchte den notarzt zu rufen aber es war kein Krankenwagen verfügbar und er musste mich selbst ins Krankenhaus fahren. Zusammen mit unser kleinen Tochter musste er dort warten.

## 646. Higher education

I am a recent college graduate and I am not at all familiar with how it works here (with higher education in general). It would take too long to describe all the individual problems, but in short - basically anyone who wants to can graduate from school (insufficient requirements leading to a decrease in the value of a diploma/title - caused by a lack of students at the school - caused by the school's bad reputation - quality students leave for the Czech Republic or elsewhere and the school tries to produce the same number of students from the people who apply to the school (which are both quality and poor quality students).   
I can also compare the school based on my experience from my study stay at the Politecnico di Torino. Based on this, I think that the school does not cooperate sufficiently even at the faculty level (frog-mouse wars between departments - who is the bigger boss) and there is no joint effort for research, moving the school forward.  
I would like to continue my studies at the PhD level, but this makes absolutely no sense in our country (which is not only my opinion, but also the opinion of colleagues I work with now who left school either before, during or after completing their PhD for the same reasons) and if I want to work in the field on state-of-the-art research, I have to apply to schools abroad, which is very difficult.  
It should also be said that there are also very high-quality people at the school who have taught me a lot, but unfortunately, the unemployable people who are sitting in their "warm" positions are blocking their development as well as the lack of money to buy equipment but also for decent salaries for these people.

<u>Original title (sk)</u> : Vysoké školstvo

<u>Original content (sk)</u> :

Som nedávny absolvent vysokej školy a nie som vôbec stotožnený s tým ako to u nás funguje (s vysokým školstvom všeobecne). Opisovať všetky jednotlivé problémy by bolo veľmi na dlho, ale v skratke - školu v podstate skončí každý kto chce (nedostatočné nároky vedúce k znižovaniu cennosti diplomu/titulu - spôsobené nedostatkom žiakov na škole - spôsobené zlou reputáciou školy - kvalitní študenti odchádzajú do Česka alebo inde a škola sa z ľudí ktorí sa prihlásia na školu (čo sú aj kvalitní ale aj nekvalitní študenti) sa škola snaží vyprodukovať stále rovnaké množstvo študentov.)   
Školu viem porovnať aj na základe skúseností z môjho študijného pobytu na Politecnico di Torino. Na základe toho si myslím, že škola nespolupracuje ani na úrovni fakulty dostatočne (žabomyšie vojny medzi ústavmi - kto je väčší pán) a neexistuje spoločná snaha o výskum, posun školy.  
Rád by som pokračoval v štúdiu na PhD úrovni, no toto u nás nemá absolútne zmysel (čo nie je len môj názor, ale aj názor kolegov s ktorými teraz pracujem a odišli zo školy či už pred, v priebehu alebo po ukončení PhD z rovnakých dôvodov) a ak chcem pracovať v odbore na state of the art výskume, sa hlásiť na školy v zahraničí  čo je veľmi náročné.  
Treba povedať aj to, že na škole sú aj veľmi kvalitní ľudia ktorí ma veľa naučili, ale bohužiaľ nezamestnateľní ľudia čo sedia na svojej "teplej" pozícii blokujú ich rozvoj rovnako ako nedostatok peňazí na kúpu vybavenia ale takisto na dôstojné platy pre týchto ľudí.

## 647. Injustice

Now in our part there is the feeling that injustice in all the civil aspects is prevailing.

## 648. Connecting with people

## 652. Off-topic or lacking empathy

A colleague, we're both in middle management, senses that I'm having some difficulty settling into my new job. He approaches me, speaks to me in a friendly, jovial manner, and says, "Come on, in our positions we enjoy these and these perks. Think of the subordinates who don't have these freedoms, and you'll be fine!" Now I feel really awful, and settling into my new job becomes even harder. I don't want to motivate myself by thinking that others are having a worse time than me. That feels wrong.

<u>Original title (de)</u> : Thema verfehlt oder keine Empathie

<u>Original content (de)</u> :

Ein Kollege, wir sind beide mittlere Leitungsebene, spürt dass ich mich mit der Einarbeitung in meinen neuen Job etwas schwer tue. Er kommt auf mich zu, spricht mich kumpelig-jovial an und sagt: "Ach komm, in der Position, in der wir sind, können wir doch die und die Vorteile genießen, denk an die Untergebenen, die diese Freiheiten nicht haben, dann wird es schon werden!" Ich fühle mich jetzt erst richtig mies und das Ankommen in meinem neuen Job fällt mir noch schwerer. Ich möchte mich nicht damit motivieren, dass es anderen schlechter ergeht als mir. Das fühlt sich falsch an.

## 653. Public Cypriot Buses are a hassle!

It seems that many people now have concerns but struggle to articulate them because they are afraid of being challenged for their views. ## 655. No train traffic for at least 4 months

It has been announced that train traffic in my region (Zeeland) will be suspended for at least 4 months in a few years. A new component for European railway tracks is being tested. That is fine in itself, but we have no alternative route. This means that we will have to do everything by car or "replacement transport" (which has not yet been tendered). We would therefore prefer to have this test conducted somewhere else, for example where there is a double track. Otherwise, people without a car will experience far too much inconvenience.

## 657. Railway problems

I have a train station right next to my house (a 2-minute walk) in Fuzeta, and another where I could get off in Olhão (which is about a 15-minute walk from work), but the train schedules are very inconvenient. When I had to leave my car at the mechanic, I had no choice but to take the train. Unfortunately, in addition to the inconvenient schedules, this line also has significant delays. ## 659. False promises

People are searching for something: in the belief in spiritual movements, for example, that everything will be better from 2027 onwards, or in the belief that everything will improve if they just work on themselves. And I experience this again and again in my own circle.

## 660. Entangled Everything

I have always wanted to work with and for nature. Then I got interested in people and human relationships. I have never really been interested in Politics with a capital P. Still, I am slowly recognising that all of it, everything we do in this relational space is in some way or another inherently political. On that smaller level. Whether this is working with kids, with neighbourhoods, with nature, or with climate change, there is some connective tissue inherent in the world and the participation with it that connects all of it.  It is tiring to think that big Politics is still about party politics, power dynamics, single issues, linear thinking, this versus that, as if the world wasn't connected. It is good to see that there are more and more initiatives around that operate with a different logic...

## 670. Putting a stop to nuisance

For months, 'fatbike' youths have been causing a nuisance in our residential area. They damage personal and communal property, set off illegal fireworks, and local residents feel threatened and intimidated by them. Last week, following numerous reports of nuisance, the police intervened by bringing a number of these youths 'out of anonymity' and noting down their names. This did not happen without a struggle. During the police operation, the father of one of the youths arrived at the scene to confront the officers and free his son from the police's grasp. He did so in such an aggressive manner that police officers wrestled him to the ground and took him to the police station. Two other youths were also taken away. The father apologized and was immediately released. The two youths spent a night in a cell. The following day, attention was drawn to this incident on national television by Elly Lust, a nationally known former police officer. She particularly condemned the behavior of the ringleader's father and urged her viewers to help put an end to such behavior. I was pleasantly surprised by the decisive action of the police and the positive media attention for this incident. The provisional result is that the young people in question have not been seen in the residential area again.

<u>Original title (nl)</u> : Paal en perk aan overlast

<u>Original content (nl)</u> :

In onze woonwijk veroorzaken 'fatbike' jongeren al maandenlang overlast. Ze beschadigen persoonlijke en gemeenschappelijke eigendommen, steken illegaal vuurwerk af en buurtbewoners voelen zich door hen bedreigd en geïntimideerd. Vorige week heeft de politie na vele meldingen van overlast ingegrepen door een aantal van deze jongeren 'uit de anonimiteit' te halen en hun namen te noteren. Dat ging niet zonder slag of stoot. Tijdens het politieoptreden kwam een vader van een van de jongeren naar de plaats-delict om verhaal te halen en zijn zoon te bevrijden uit de greep van de politie. Dat deed hij op een dusdanig agressieve manier dat politieagenten hem tegen de grond werkten en meenamen naar het politiebureau. Ook zijn twee jongeren meegenomen. De vader heeft zijn excuses aangeboden en werd direct vrij gelaten. De twee jongeren hebben een nacht in de cel gezeten. De volgende dag is op de nationale tv aandacht gegeven aan dit incident door Elly Lust, een landelijk bekende oud-agente. Zij hekelde vooral ook het gedrag van de vader van de raddraaier en spoorde haar kijkerspubliek aan dergelijk gedrag te helpen stoppen.  Ik was aangenaam verrast door het kordate optreden van de politie en de positieve media-aandacht voor dit incident. Het voorlopige resultaat is dat de betreffende jongeren zich niet meer hebben laten zien in de woonwijk.

## 676. The village in the city

My husband recently lost his driving licence temporarily due to a health condition and we lived in a small village in East Devon, England.  With me travelling away a lot, he suddenly experienced himself as being utterly cut off, and powerless to make choices for simple things like shopping.  Attempts to use public transport led to frustration and increased powerlessness, as there is no local train station and the buses are utterly unreliable, often not turning up at all, let alone on time.  
  
He found himself having to ask neighbours for lifts (which he hated doing), and I experienced myself becoming more and more unwilling to accept work that kept me away from home for more than a day or two at best.  We felt our world closing in on us.  
  
Ultimately, even though he got his licence back when the health issue was resolved, we decided to leave the village, and have now moved to central London - the opposite to what many people do at our age.  We have been surprised to find that local engagement and invitation to get to know others is BETTER here than it was in our Devon village, which we now realise was cliquey and hard to enter if you weren't born there, and didn't have school aged kids, or belong to a religious community.  
  
What started as a transport problem, was actually more to do with becoming vulnerable in a community that we found it hard to engage with, and made little effort to engage us.  We are much happier in the "village in the city".

## 678. senseless vandalism

My neighbors across the street are young people who are hard of hearing. Young people live there permanently with support, but there is also a so-called Cluster 4 primary school for children who would normally attend a 'regular' primary school, provided they do not have a hearing impairment. There is a playground and, of course, toys such as bicycles, sandbox equipment, etc. Young people from our town broke into the shed in the evening and threw the items onto the playground. Pointless, therefore. A neighbor and I attempted to speak to the young people, but they became verbally aggressive. We then walked away and filed a report with the police and the organization.

## 679. Inability to honestly argue about political topics

For many years now, I experience a drastic increase of mistrust and conspiracy theories amongst my family and close friends in eastern Germany. I find this very disturbing, as the way arguments are made (without any real facts, just vague claims that "the government does this, and the media hide that", make it impossible for me to argue and the discussions tend to make me very uncomfortable. As a result, I tend to avoid discussions about current political topics, despite the fact, that I believe they should be discussed and I want to have a good and honest argument about different political positions. But in my experience, the culture of a good political discussion got lost, not only in parliament, but also in the inner circle of family and friends.

## 681. Housing problems

Although I work for a multinational corporation as a clerk, I don't have enough money for housing. ## 683. Voiceless and powerless

I remember the city of Karlsruhe's plan to build an underground tram system. A citizens' veto clearly rejected the project, but construction had already begun. In the end, the project was implemented "in part," meaning the "half-underground tram" was built, and the citizens were informed that their approval wasn't needed. The situation is similar with old trees in the city center. The city administration has plans to cut them down. Many citizens are against it and have already demonstrated. Nevertheless, the city's plan will most likely be implemented. My experience is that politicians decide according to their own interests, even when the citizens are clearly against it.

<u>Original title (de)</u> : Stimm- und machtlos

<u>Original content (de)</u> :

Ich erinnere mich an den Plan der Stadt Karlsruhe, eine U-Strab zu bauen. Durch eine Bürger*innen-Veto wurde das Projekt eindeutig abgelehnt, während der Bauvorgang jedoch schon startete. Am Ende wurde das Projekt "zur Hälfte" umgesetzt, also die "Halbe U-Strab" gebaut und den Bürger*innen mitgeteilt, dass man hierfür keine Zustimmung bräuchte. Ebenso verhält es sich mit alten Bäumen in der Innenstadt. Die Stadtverwaltung hat "Fällpläne". Viele Bürger*innen sind dagegen und haben bereits demonstriert. Dennoch wird der Plan der Stadt mit großer Wahrscheinlichkeit durchgesetzt werden. Meine Erfahrung ist, dass die Politik auch dann nach ihrer Interessenlage entscheidet, wenn die Bürger*innen ganz klar dagegen sind.

## 684. Democracy in family systems

I'm currently experiencing firsthand that, as a man, I'm not taken seriously when it comes to child-rearing issues. Since my wife left me, she claims sole authority over the interpretation of what's best for the children, and even the youth welfare office intuitively assumes that a mother is inherently more capable of raising children. I notice this particularly in the way mistakes are handled. I'm not perfect, and I have to justify my deviations from the norm (the norms of which are also questionable, and who actually defines them) much more rigorously than my ex-partner did. The distinction between the couple level and the parental level is especially difficult, as I get the impression that critical opinions on the parental level are ignored with the argument that this issue is a couple matter and therefore doesn't need to be discussed further. If I want to express my views to the children, I'm forced to conform with the argument of a potential loyalty conflict for them. In my opinion, this is incompatible with freedom of expression and information, as the children and I can't freely exchange views. The fact that my ex-partner is de facto a single parent and actively restricts my parenting is also incompatible with democratic principles in my view. When adults are alone with children, they hold a position of power that faces no adequate opposition. In our case, my partially differing opinions are excluded from daily family life, communication, and decision-making. Legislative, executive, and judicial power are concentrated in one person. Therefore, my family currently resembles a totalitarian dictatorship more than a pluralistic democracy. This development is particularly critical because the family is the primary environment for children's socialization. As a society, we should therefore pay attention to fostering democratic attitudes and values, especially within family structures, so that these are well-trained and resilient against anti-democratic forces when the children grow up. The issue of sexism against men is also still insufficiently addressed in society, allowing men and women to blindly enter situations that further fuel the spiral of violence between the sexes.

<u>Original title (de)</u> : Demokratie in Familiensystemen

<u>Original content (de)</u> :

Ich mache zurzeit selber die Erfahrung, dass ich als Mann in nicht ernst genommen werde, wenn es um Fragen der Kindererziehung geht. Nachdem sich meine Frau getrennt hat beansprucht sie die alleinige Deutungshoheit des Kindeswohls und auch beim Jugendamt wird intuitiv davon ausgegangen, dass eine Mutter grundsätzlich fähiger ist Kinder zu erziehen. Das merke ich vor allem an der Fehlerkultur. Ich bin nicht perfekt, muss meine Abweichungen der Norm (bei der auch fraglich ist, wer die eigentlich festlegt) viel stärker rechtfertigen, als meine Expartnerin. Vor allem die Differenzierung zwischen Paar- und Elternebene ist sehr schwierig, da ich den Eindruck habe, dass kritische Meinungen auf Elternebene ausgeblendet werden mit dem Argument, dass sich dieses Thema auf einer Paarebene befindet und damit nicht mehr diskutiert werden muss. Will ich meine Standpunkte vor den Kinder vertreten, werde ich mit dem Argument eines drohenden Loyalitätskonfliktes bei den Kindern zur Konformität gezwungen. Das ist meines Erachtens nach nicht mit einer Meinungs- und Informationsfreiheit vereinbar, da sich die Kinder und ich nicht frei austauschen können. Auch die Tatsache, dass meine Expartnerin de facto alleinerziehend ist und meine Erziehung aktiv einschränkt ist für mich nicht mit demokratischen Grundsätzen vereinbar. Wenn Erwachsene alleine mit Kindern sind, haben sie eine Machtposition, die keine angemessene Opposition erfährt. In unserem Fall werde ich mit meiner in Teilen abweichenden Meinung aus dem Familienalltag, der Kommunikation und der Entscheidungsfindung ausgeschlossen. Legislative, Exekutive und Judikative sind in einer Person vereint. Daher gleicht meine Familie aktuell leider mehr einer totalitären Diktatur als einer pluralistischen Demokratie. Besonders brisant ist diese Entwicklung, da die Familie für Kinder das primäre Sozialisationsumfeld darstellt. Als Gesellschaft sollten wir also darauf achten gerade in Familienstrukturen demokratische Haltungen und Werte zu fördern, damit diese wenn die Kinder Erwachsen sind gut trainiert und resilient gegen antidemokratische Kräfte sind. Auch das Thema Sexismus gegenüber Männern ist in der Gesellschaft noch zu wenig präsent, sodass Männer und Frauen blind in Situationen geraten, welche die Spirale der Gewalt zwischen den Geschlechtern weiter antreibt.

## 689. German elections - no one to elect

The upcoming elections in Germany are approaching, and reading through the party programs feels deeply frustrating. Many lack authenticity and fail to address real issues in a meaningful way. On the rare occasions when they do, their proposals often seem poorly substantiated, inadequately thought through, and devoid of integrity or courage.  
  
Values like courage, authenticity, and integrity feel like relics of a distant past. Where are the leaders of substance and vision? Too many politicians seem to hide behind platitudes, chase superficial victories, indulge in bluster, and prioritize short-term gains over long-term solutions.  
  
Worse yet, many party leaders appear more focused on securing their own positions than on serving the greater good. The infighting within their ranks ignores the bigger picture, paving the way for gains by the far right. Have they learned nothing from history?

## 696. Car sharing as a stepping stone to local democracy

Last Saturday, I attended a get-together hosted by a citizens' initiative within my municipality that offers the shared use of electric cars. My wife and I have been participants/'customers' of this car-sharing service for two years now. This means you can reserve, unlock, use, and pay for a car via an app. This gathering was the first time I met and spoke with other participants. I enjoyed hearing a bit more background on how this initiative originated, who had contributed to it, etc. We got into a conversation about how everyone experienced using the shared cars and what other possibilities we saw. Could we apply for a subsidy from the municipality? Could we, as a cooperative, handle this even more ourselves (setting rates, etc.)? How great would it be if there were fewer cars parked on the street? How can we achieve that, in particular? I had never had conversations like that via the app. In short: the introduction and connection naturally led to conversation and ideas for follow-up action. It leaves me wanting more. Especially if the government also provides support for this and leaves sufficient room to build on it further as a society.

<u>Original title (nl)</u> : Autodelen als opstap naar lokale democratie

<u>Original content (nl)</u> :

Afgelopen zaterdag was ik bij een borrel van een burgerinitiatief binnen mijn gemeente dat het samen delen van elektrische auto's aanbiedt. Ik ben samen met mijn vrouw al twee jaar deelnemer / 'klant' van dat autodelen. Dus via een app kan je auto reserveren, ontgrendelen gebruiken en afrekenen. Deze borrel was voor het eerst dat ik andere deelnemers trof en sprak. Ik vond het leuk om wat meer achtergrond te horen over hoe dit initiatief was ontstaan, wie er aan hadden bijgedragen etc. We raakten in gesprek over hoe ieder het gebruik van de deelauto's ervaarde. En over welke mogelijkheden we nog meer zagen. Zouden we subsidie van de gemeente kunnen vragen? Zouden we dit als cooperatie nog meer zelf kunnen doen (tarieven vaststellen etc)? Hoe mooi zou het zijn als er minder auto's geparkeerd in de straat staan? Hoe kunnen we dat vooral krijgen? Dat soort gesprekken had ik via de app nog nooit gehad. Kortom: door de kennismaking en verbinding ontstaat vrij natuurlijk gesprek en ideeën voor vervolg actie. Smaakt naar meer. Zeker als vanuit de overheid hier ook steun aan wordt gegeven en voldoende ruimte lijft om het als samenleving verder op te bouwen.

## 704. Explosion in the south of Rotterdam

There was an explosion in our neighbourhood in the south of Rotterdam. My boyfriend had heard it but I do not believe I did (as there are a lot of fireworks in the area so sometimes I do not pay attention to those kind of sounds). A few days later we received a letter (from what I've gathered every house in the neighbourhood received one) to inform us about the explosion, what happened and the fact that the police is now doing an investigation to find out who is behind this and why they targeted a specific house in the neighbourhood. Any witnesses were asked to call a specific number to give information about the incident. Even if the explosion startled us, receiving that letter was reassuring and it, at least, made me feel a sense of security in a world that feels less and less safe.

## 727. Unfounded and only

Something that strikes me daily is the hasty judgments made without factual data or nuances. Let’s ban all wood burning to reduce particulate matter emissions—a very good reason. A more nuanced approach would be to ban appliances that do not meet certain conditions. For a long time, there have been wood stoves—and ovens—that have virtually no emissions and, provided they are burned with the right wood in the right way, actually contribute to a better environment. Let’s ban a (fictional) series because it gives a wrong impression of farmers (BBB). Based on 1 scene without context. The series actually provides a beautifully nuanced picture of the dilemmas farmers face, and in that scene, it is not the farmers but violence that is condemned. All opinions about the wolf without real knowledge, and especially the retreat into one’s own small circle without addressing common problems on a larger scale. We are facing a significant global threat of shortages, overheating, diseases, and violence. You cannot solve that within national borders. The climate, viruses, and environment do not adhere to that.

<u>Original title (nl)</u> : Ongefundeerd en alleen

<u>Original content (nl)</u> :

Iets wat me dagelijks raakt is het snelle (ver)oordelen zonder feitelijke gegevens of nuances. Laten we voor om fijnstofuitstoot te minderen - zeer goede reden - alle houtverbranding verbieden. Genuanceerder is apparaten die niet aan bepaalde voorwaarden voldoen verbieden. Er zijn al heel lang houtkachels - en fornuizen - die zo goed als geen uitstoot hebben en mits met het juiste hout op de juiste manier gestookt juist bijdragen aan een beter milieu. Laten we een (fictie)serie verbieden omdat het een verkeerd beeld van boeren geeft (BBB). Gebaseerd op 1 scene zonder context. de serie geeft juist een heel mooi genuanceerd beeld van de dilemma's waar boeren mee kampen en in die scene worden niet de boeren, maar geweld veroordeeld.Alle meningen over de wolf zonder echte kennis. en vooral het terugtrekken naar de eigen kleine kring zonder gemeenschappelijk problemen in grotere kring aan te pakken. We krijgen een flinke mondiale dreiging aan tekorten, verwarming, ziekten en geweld. Die kan je niet oplossen binnen landsgrenzen.Daar houdt het klimaat, virussen en milieu zich niet aan.

## 728. Confused and incredibly sad

I was in Dubai for work last week. Everything glitters, everything shines, everything runs smoothly. A multi-diverse society with a clear division of roles, where highly skilled foreign labor contributes to the society's wealth, and modern-day slavery exists (people building skyscrapers in 50-degree heat).  
  
I'm back in Europe and so glad to be back in Vienna. A lot of things are working well; the city where I live actually looks good and well-maintained. Then there's the whole Friedrich Merz debacle. I don't even know how to express the frustration and sadness I feel. Why do so many people vote for the AfD? WISO wants a party like the CDU to work with the AfD. The 80th anniversary of the preparation of the concentration camps. I don't know what to do with my thoughts.

<u>Original title (de)</u> : Confused und unendlich traurig

<u>Original content (de)</u> :

Ich war letzte Woche Beruflich in Dubai. Alles glänzt, alles scheint, alles läuft. Multi diverse Gesellschaft mit klarer Rollenverteilung wo high skilled foreign labor zum Reichtum der Gesellschaft beiträgt und es moderne Sklaverei gibt (die bei 50 Grad Hitze Wolkenkratzer bauen).   
Ich komme zurück nach Europe bin so froh wieder in Wien angekommen zu sein. Es funktioniert viel, sieht eigentlich gut und gepflegt aus in der Stadt wo ich lebe. Dann der Scheiß mit Friedrich Merz. Ich weiß gar nicht wie ich dem Ausdruck verleihen soll der Frustration und Trauer die ich spüre. Wieso wählen so viele Leute AFD. WISO will so eine Partei wie die CDU mit einer AFD zusammen arbeiten. 80. Gedenktag der Bereitung der KZ. Ich weiß nicht wohin mit meinen Gedanken.

## 734. Neither protection, help, nor justice can be expected from the state.

A friend of mine worked as a train driver for Deutsche Bahn and was beaten so badly by a passenger that she ended up in the hospital. The titanium plates in her face have since been removed.  
  
She can no longer work, one side of her face is numb, and she's on the verge of becoming destitute.  
  
The police had no incentive to catch the perpetrator. Due to his own stupidity, the perpetrator went to the police himself about an unrelated matter and was subsequently arrested.  
  
A year later, she and another witness had to sit across from the aggressive, previously convicted (attempted murder) as a violent offender in court.  
  
The perpetrator was sentenced to 1.5 years and ordered to be committed to a psychiatric hospital. He will probably even be released early because he "no longer poses a danger."  
  
The perpetrator is receiving support, and every (imagined) positive aspect is being interpreted in his favor. Until then, the state is fully responsible for his therapy. My friend is unemployed, severely traumatized, has lifelong physical limitations, and will likely end up needing social assistance. The far right has a term for this.

Sie kann ihren Job nicht mehr ausüben, eine Gesichtshälfte ist taub und sie ist auf dem Weg mittelstandslos zu werden.  
Die Polizei hatte keinen Anreiz den Täter zu fassen. Der Täter ist aufgrund eigener Dummheit selber wegen eines anderen Themas zur Polizei gegangen und wurde dann festgenommen.  
1 Jahr später durfte sie und eine andere Zeugin im Gerichtsaal dem aggressiven vorbestraften (versuchter Mord) Gewalttäter gegenübersitzen.  
Der Täter wurde zu 1,5 Jahren und Psychatrie verurteilt. Dann darf er wahrscheinlich sogar (wieder) früher raus, weil er "keine Gefahr mehr darstellt".  
Der Täter wird betreut und es wird alles (erdachte) positive für ihn ausgelegt. Bis dahin kümmert sich der Staat vollumfänglich um ihn in der Therapie. Meine Freundin ist arbeitslos, schwer traumatisiert, hat lebenslängliche körperliche Einschränkungen und wird wohl ein Sozialhilfefall. Das rechte Pack hat einen Kampfbegriff dafür.

## 735. Cycling without any infrastructure

I was recently cycling to work, and in my country the cycling infrastructure is severely underdeveloped, so I'm cycling on the road alongside cars. In the morning there is a lot of traffic, so I have to squeeze past a lot of cars, which do not leave a lot of space for me. There was this big white van that was especially close to the side of the road, so the only way I could get past it was by getting on the sidewalk with my bike, moving forward 2-3 metres, and then getting back on the side of the road right in front of this van. I then continued cycling up to the traffic light, and once it turned green I continued my journey. Shortly after that the same white van made an especially close pass right in front of me, and that made me feel very uncomfortable and angry.

## 738. Middle Ages (from digitalization to the Renaissance)

What communication meant to people who switched from radio to television is now evident among those who have turned off the TV and turned on social media. The syllogism that linked TV programs to truthful information now applies to social media. TV and social media overlap with written sources, creating a narrative of the past through the lens of the morality and ethics of today's think tanks. ## 750. Accessibility of society

As a wheelchair user, I have certain experiences. For example, when I want to leave the house, I always have to ask myself whether I can use the toilet at my destination, if there is an elevator, or if the sidewalk is accessible. I need to be able to park my car there. I am willing to use public transport, but there is no bus service in my village. The tram or train are far from ideal for a wheelchair. In my municipality, several disabled parking spaces are unusable. Following a report about this, I was recently invited by the alderman to discuss these parking spaces.

## 751. Defending a free and democratic order in Europe – but how?

I am moved by the release of the Israeli hostages, and horrified by the way they are escorted by masked men carrying a certificate and a gift basket, and by how clearly this is staged for the world to see. It troubles me that in Germany, the discussion so quickly turns to fascism (especially regarding März, whom I cannot stand and consider a political enemy), yet we remain largely silent when a terrorist organization like Hamas, which despises humanity and, above all, women, is being promoted on German streets. We need migration, and we need tolerance based on our constitution, and especially as Europe, we must stand together, regardless of which extremists threaten the free and democratic order. Unfortunately, this is very complex, and the populism from the right, and sometimes even from the left, infuriates me.

<u>Original title (de)</u> : Feiheitliche, demokratische Grundordnung in Europa verteidigen - aber wie? 

<u>Original content (de)</u> :

Berührt mich wie die israelischen Geiseln frei kommen und erschreckt mich wie sie mit einem Zertifikat und Geschenkkorb von maskierten flankiert werden und wie deutlich die Inszenierung für die Weltöffentlichkeit wird. Es stimmt mich nachdenklich das es in Deutschland so schnell um Faschismus geht (Bei März, den ich nicht leiden kann und politisch als Feind betrachte) wir jedoch weitgehend schweigen wenn auf Deutschen Straßen für eine Terror und Menschen und vorallem Frauenverachtende Organisation wie die HAMAS Stimmung gemacht wird. Wir braucht Migration und wir brauchen Toleranz auf Basis undserer Verfassung und gerade als Europa müssen wir zusammenstehen egal welche Extremisten die freiheitliche demokratische Grundordnung gefährden. Leider ist das sehr komplex und der Populismus von Rechts und manchmal auch von Link macht mich wütend.
