## 752. Taking the population hostage is not the solution

The union actions currently taking place in Belgium, and previously in France, are perhaps understandable but inefficient, and above all frustrating for ordinary people. Imagine being dependent on public transport, or not knowing where to take your children, or missing doctor's appointments, or having to rebook flights with all the associated hassle… I have now ended up in one of the aforementioned situations three times in a row due to union actions, and that needs to change. The frequent demonstrations also cause a great deal of chaos and grievances. We must also achieve this through citizen participation and democratic consultation. I, and many others with me, are tired of being held hostage time and again by unions that always resort to the easiest means and governments that are too stubborn to listen.

<u>Original title (nl)</u> : Bevolking in gijzeling nemen is niet de oplossing

<u>Original content (nl)</u> :

De vakbondsacties nu in België en ervoor in Frankrijk, misschien begrijpelijk maar niet efficiënt, en vooral frustrerend voor de gewone mens. Je zal maar afhankelijk zijn van openbaar vervoer, of niet weten waar naar toe met je kinderen, of doktersafspraken missen, of ook nog vluchten moeten herboeken met alle rompslomp die er bij komt … Ik ben nu al 3 keer op rij in 1 van de genoemde situaties terecht gekomen door vakbondsacties en dat moet anders. Ook zorgen de veelvuldige betogingen voor veel chaos en wantoestanden.  
Met burgerparticipatie en democratisch overleg moeten we er ook geraken. Ik, en met mij veel anderen mensen, zijn het beu om telkens opnieuw gegijzeld te worden door vakbonden die steeds naar het gemakkelijkste middel grijpen en regeringen die te koppig zijn om te willen luisteren.

## 755. Are EU citizens welcome at VoltCH?

I joined VoltCH and found out, in the common WhatsApp group of all members, my introduction as EU citizen living in Switzerland (CH) was met by some very ugly response. The key theme I raised was voting rights for migrants in CH, somebody from the group thought, it was a good idea to instruct me on how to enter a Swiss casino, that a EU passport would be enough for me. Nobody from the group intervened, so I stood alone in the WhatsApp group, without any bystanders to support my point.  
When I found out, maybe a week and a couple of very unpleasant interactions with this person in the group later, that this situation would not improve, I left the Volt CH WhatsApp community and contacted my mentor at Volt CH. He agreed with my point of view and reported, he would address this problem (I was not the first one who had this kind of bully experience in the WhatsApp) with the Presidium.  
We are now 2 weeks since then and no follow-up has been shared with me. I hope this will be done without any further delays. I feel very unwelcomed as an EU citizen in the political movement Volt that should foster European collaboration and civil rights.  


<u>Origin</u> : Switzerland

<u>Unique identifier</u> : voltnws

## 760. Polarization getting closer

Polarization is all around us. The time when conspiracy theories and right-wing radical ideology were a niche, something far removed from you, something belonging to others, from the past, a small group of weirdos you marveled at, good for a Netflix documentary—that time is over. Absurdly enough, the insane ideology of these people has now been normalized. There are many of them. And very close by. In my case, even within my family.  
  
I wish I had an answer. A sharp counter-argument, to silence the madness. But facts are no longer enough. The truth is no longer enough. It makes me angry, and anxious. Anxiety about democracy. Our freedom, stability, peace, open dialogue with one another.  
  
If only I knew.

<u>Original title (nl)</u> : Polarisatie steeds dichterbij

<u>Original content (nl)</u> :

Polarisatie is overal om  ons heen. De tijd dat complottheoriën en rechts-radikaal gedachtengoed een niche waren, iets ver weg van jou, iets van anderen, van vroeger, een klein groepje weirdo's waar je je over verbaasde, goed voor een documentaire op Netflix - die tijd is voorbij. Absurd genoeg is het krankzinnige gedachtegoed van deze mensen nu genormaliseerd. Ze zijn met velen. En heel dichtbij. In mijn geval zelfs binnen mijn gezin.   
Ik zou willen dat ik een antwoord had. Een scherp tegenargument, om de waanzin de mond te snoeren. Maar feiten zijn niet langer genoeg. De waarheid is niet langer genoeg. Het maakt me boos, en angstig. Angst voor de democratie. Onze vrijheid, stabiliteit, vrede, het onbevangen gesprek met elkaar.   
Wist ik het maar.

## 762. Existential dread caused by government changing the rules.

I'm a 51 year old man. I'm trying to get things together for retirement. I have dual UK and French nationality. I have a house in Spain and in the UK and my long term girlfriend  lives in Hamburg. If you cut me in half I'd have the EU flag running through me. The UK government, because the economy is tanking is messing with pensions, inheritance, taxes. The Spanish government wants to impose property tax on non EU residents, the French politicial climate is swinging to far left or right, same in Germany. I can't plan anything when the rules keep changing. I want stability with long term vision and guidance from government. I want to be able to make money now, and save it effectively. Inheritance taxes from my parents and to my children should have long term  rules set which I can follow. It's not right to keep changing them. I'd like a fully federal Europe, a European ISA, harmonised tax, banking and insurance. Strong European defence and joint procurement. The middle classes need a regulatory and tax space to thrive, The super rich need to be forced to spend or lose their wealth. Inequality is destroying our democracy. In 2020 the richest 1 percent grabbed nearly two thirds of all new wealth. If we can't address this then capitalist democracy is finished.

<u>Language</u> : en  
<u>Unique identifier</u> : voltnws  
<u>EU is like</u> : A safe loving home, but it needs some serious work and upgrades otherwise it's going to all fall down. Less/ better regulation, enable individual and equitable wealth creation   
<u>Europe is like</u> : This amazing geographic and cultural space that I can live and work and play in. I was so sad when Brexit tried to take that away from me  
<u>Democracy is like</u> : It's dying, traditional political parties are lost and rudderless unable to make meaningful change to improve people's lives. If you don't democracy itself will fall.

## 763. lack of immigration policy

I volunteer with Serve the City Brussels. Once a week, I either bring meals from the community kitchen to migrant drop-in centers, or I hand out coffee at 6:00 a.m. to migrants waiting outside the initial reception center.

## 764. I feel protected as a consumer

My laptop's trackpad went defect. The company is famous of their planned obsolescence, and usually their devices go bad after the warranty has expired. Replacing that somewhere else would've cost more than 700 Euros. Luckily, since I live in Germany, the consumer laws protected me from the malpractices of greedy corporates, and I got the thing fixed for free !  
I'm like the next expat in Germany, feel some times that we overpay taxes, forced insurances, and social contributions, but moments like this remind me of what a healthy society feels like :-)

## 767. Free and mobile!

I can't imagine any more border controls within Europe right now! I grew up in a Europe with border checks. I still remember the times when we were on the bus to visit family in Portugal, waiting at every border crossing, and the border guards would sometimes walk right through the bus and want to see everyone's passport. The same thing happened on the way back, of course! Nowadays, I just set off and feel like I'm in a single, large country. Even flying is more relaxed. I can't really judge what the economic advantages are, but it's logical that the commercial benefits are easily quantifiable. I pray to God that you get over the 5% mark! 😘 You have my vote!

## 771. Social cohesion

In my daily work, I work a lot with vulnerable people, such as those who are (functionally) illiterate, people with disabilities, and also people whose native language is not German. Therefore, I consciously avoid using gender-inclusive language in both written and spoken form and use simple language. This makes me wonder what inclusion actually means. If identity excludes and divides more than it improves everyone's lives, I don't see the point.  
  
For example: I'm often asked what I'll vote for – usually Volt. The reactions are almost always the same. Environment and Europe, yes. But too much focus on identity. The LGBTQ+ issue, in particular, is perceived as too prominent in light of our current problems. Not because my conversation partners don't respect the rights of queer people, but because other issues are considered far more important. Around 10% of the vote is an attractive prospect, but at least as many people might not vote for Volt because of it.  
  
It would be great if Volt could also reach the LGBTQ+ community with issues that resonate with all citizens. People are uncertain. My experience is quite clear: people yearn for common ground.  
  
The article on identity politics, published in HPD on January 13, 2025, is highly recommended: https://hpd.de/artikel/identitaetspolitiken-links-und-rechts-perfekte-sturm-22754

<u>Original title (de)</u> : Gesellschaftlicher Zusammenhalt

<u>Original content (de)</u> :

In meinem Berufsalltag arbeite ich viel mit vulnerablen Menschen, z. B. (funktionale) Analphabeten, Menschen mit Einschränkungen und auch mit Menschen deren Muttersprache nicht Deutsch ist. Daher verzichte ich ganz bewusst in Schrift und Sprache auf das korrekte Gendern und verwende einfache Sprache. Ich stelle mir dabei die Frage, was eigentlich inklusiv ist? Wenn Identität mehr ausgrenzt und spaltet als die Lebenswelt aller zu verbessern, sehe den Sinn nicht.   
Beispiel: Ich werde ich oft gefragt was ich wählen werde -  eigentlich Volt. Die Reaktionen sind fast immer gleich. Umwelt und Europa, ja. Aber zuviel Fokus auf Identität. Besonders wird das Thema LGBTQ+ wird in Angesicht unserer heutigen Probleme als zu groß empfunden. Nicht weil meine Gesprächspartner die Rechte queerer Menschen nicht respektieren, aber andere Themen werden eben als sehr viel wichtiger empfunden. Etwa 10 % der Wählerstimmen sind eine attraktive Aussicht, aber mindestens eben so viele werden Volt deswegen vielleicht nicht wählen.   
Wäre toll wenn Volt die LGBTQ+ Community auch mit den Themen erreichen könnte, von denen sich alle Bürger angesprochen fühlen. Die Menschen sind verunsichert. Meine Erfahrung ist ganz deutlich, die Menschen sehnen sich nach common Ground.   
Der Artikel zum Thema Identitätspolitiken, erschienen im HPD vom 13.Jan 2025 ist sehr zu empfehlen: https://hpd.de/artikel/identitaetspolitiken-links-und-rechts-perfekte-sturm-22754

## 774. Optimistic hope for climate and society

Yes, it's true that I think the world, and society in general, has a degree of injustice because talent, sincerity, and honesty aren't necessarily valued, while charisma, leadership, and dominant personalities are emphasized and privileged in Western societies, and indeed in societies in general.  
  
I think that thanks to organizations like yours, which seem aware of all this, and perhaps with the help of tools like artificial intelligence, we are moving towards a fairer world. Perhaps even a world government, or even a European one thanks to you—that would be wonderful. With rules based on justice and fairness, we could identify talent, highlight people's skills while taking their difficulties into account, using targeted algorithms. Everyone could find their place and purpose in society while feeling valued.  
  
Moreover, it will be of great help for the climate and the future of the planet; metadata will be able to make very precise calculations regarding our actions, and shady dealings and vested interests will not be able to be influential without being exposed.

## 781. Maternity care

My son was born a few days ago. The maternity carer helping us the first days (which is a blessing), told me there's a kind of secret way of working for maternity carers all over The Netherlands with how they help undocumented or assylum seeking people with their new borns. There are a lot of rules and regulations prohibiting the maternity careres to help those in need, but they find ways to do so for example by not clocking the right amount of hours, or ficticiously assigning hours to people with better health insurance, to be able to help those that have no insurance. This story broke my heart and simultaneously warmed it. It's heartbreaking to hear that governments and insurance companies go out of their way to prevent people from getting care and it warms my heart to see people bending and breaking those rules to help those in need.

## 784. The cynical game of internships

I've been working for a few months at a social enterprise in my city, completing an extracurricular internship.  
However, I don't want to talk about my own experience (though it's also quite problematic), but rather that of the many student interns I've met.  
I'm increasingly aware of how my fellow students, with curricular internship contracts (without a salary), are shamelessly exploited.  
It's not just the lack of compensation for full-time commitment to the company (which is unacceptable in itself), but rather the system by which these people are deluded into believing they'll receive adequate job training and that this experience will open doors to the world of work, when in reality it's simply a way for companies to work for free...  
Very often, internships are used when someone needs someone to perform a strenuous or uninspiring task and they don't want to pay an employee. Everything is out in the open, everything is explicitly stated: the curricular intern serves only to do the dirty work without paying.  
Sometimes the "boss" doesn't even remember the names of the interns, who come and go at a dizzying pace and very rarely have truly formative relationships with their colleagues.  
The cynicism with which these people are treated is intolerable; the purpose of internships should be fundamentally rethought, without exploiting the weakness of all those young people who know they are vulnerable in the contemporary world of work and who must submit to these unjust practices.

<u>Original title (it)</u> : Il gioco cinico dei tirocini

<u>Original content (it)</u> :

Sto lavorando da qualche mese presso una impresa sociale che opera nella mia città, svolgendo un tirocinio extracurricolare.  
Non voglio però parlare della mia esperienza diretta (pur essendo anch'essa assai problematica) ma di quella dei molti studenti tirocinanti che ho avuto modo di incontrare.  
Mi rendo conto  infatti sempre più spesso di quanto i miei colleghi studenti, con contratto da tirocinante curriculare (senza stipendio) siano sfruttati senza alcun ritegno.  
Non è solo la mancata erogazione di un compenso a fronte di un impegno lavorativo full time in azienda (cosa di per sé inaccettabile), quanto piuttosto il sistema per cui si illudono queste persone facendo loro credere che riceveranno una formazione al lavoro adeguata e che questa esperienza aprirà loro le porte del mondo del lavoro, quando si tratta solamente di un modo per dare alle aziende qualcuno che lavori gratis...  
Molto spesso si ricorre ai tirocini quando si ha bisogno di qualcuno che svolga qualche mansione faticosa o poco stimolante e non si ha voglia di pagare un dipendente. Tutto alla luce del sole, tutto esplicitamente detto: il tirocinante curriculare serve solo a fare il lavoro sporco senza sborsare soldi.  
A volte il "capo" nemmeno si ricorda il nome dei tirocinanti, che vanno e vengono ad un ritmo vertiginoso e molto raramente hanno davvero dei rapporti formativi con i colleghi.  
Il cinismo con il quale questo persone vengono trattate e' intollerabile, andrebbe ripensata alla radice la funzione dei tirocini, senza approfittare della debolezza di tutti quei giovani che sanno di essere vulnerabili nel mondo del lavoro contemporaneo e che devono sottostare a queste pratiche ingiuste

## 793. Fear to live in my own skin

I am a trans woman, who suffers from level 1 autism and ADHD. I was born a woman soul, yet society expected my whole life for me to act as a strong man who doesn’t cry.  
  
I freed myself from judgement and became my truest self by moving out of my far right, hyper conservative, straight out fascist, as in they admire Mussolini, town in southern Italy, to move to Scotland. I felt at home for the first time in my life.  
  
Yet, Brexit forced me to leave: Scotland, as the rUK, had, and still has, serious issues regarding public trans healthcare (as in not enough doctors), hence I was with a private clinic and costs surged up.  
  
I lived across Europe until now, having had financial struggles all my adult life, where I moved back to my home town, as a new me.  
  
Finally self confident, ambitious, and with a will to live.  
  
Yet, all I can see around me is hatred. As if people like me are enemies. Many people here think that a trans woman is synonymous with to feminine sex worker with a penis.   
  
It has been difficult to find jobs, it has been difficult to work and maintain myself, my only luck is that I have my family that covers for me. Yet, I am a skilled, yet heavily underpaid, Software Engineer.

## 794. Statelessness is bureaucratic nonsense.

My highly valued colleague told me yesterday that he was unable to open an online brokerage account to invest in ETFs. The reason was his stateless person's ID card. This wasn't offered as an option for identification. When he inquired, the bank was unaware that such a status even existed. This is just one of the many small and large obstacles he faces because of his status. He was born in 1988 and fled Georgia with his parents and siblings. He went to school in Germany, completed his vocational training here, and has worked continuously ever since. Despite this, he remains denied German citizenship. The legal proceedings have dragged on for years. He cannot marry or vote, even though he lives here and pays taxes. I work with people from all over the world who live in Germany. When people talk about a dominant German culture, it doesn't reflect my reality. My environment is characterized by diverse cultures but similar values. I wish for easier access to citizenship for colleagues and friends who are stateless and want to build their lives here. I wish these friends the same freedom that I enjoy with my German passport.

<u>Original title (de)</u> : Staatenlosigkeit ist bürokratischer Quatsch

<u>Original content (de)</u> :

Mein sehr geschätzter Arbeitskollege hat mir gestern erzählt, dass er daran gescheitert ist ein online Depot zur Investition in ETF zu eröffnen. Der Grund war sein Staatenlosen Ausweis. Dieser wurde nicht als Möglichkeit zur Identifikation angeboten. Auf Rückfrage, wusste die Bank nicht das so ein Status überhaupt existiert. Das ist nur eine der vielen kleinen und großen Hürden die ihm auf Grund seines Status in den Weg gelegt werden. Er ist 1988 geboren und floh mit seinen Eltern und Geschwistern aus Georgien. Er ist in Deutschland zur Schule gegangen, hat hier seine Ausbildung gemacht und arbeitet seit dem ununterbrochen. Trotzdem bleibt ihm die deutsche Staatsangehörigkeit verwehrt. Seit Jahren zieht sich das juristische Verfahren. Er kann nicht heiraten oder Wahlen teilnehmen obwohl er hier lebt und Steuern zahlt. Ich arbeite mit Menschen aus aller Welt zusammen, die in Deutschland leben. Wenn Menschen von deutscher Leitkultur sprechen entspricht das nicht meiner Realität. Mein Umfeld ist geprägt von verschieden Kulturen aber ähnlichen Werten. Ich wünsche mir einfacheren Zugang zu Staatsangehörigkeit für Kolleg/innen* und Freunde/innen die Staatenlos sind und hier ihr Leben aufbauen möchten. Ich wünsche diesen Freunde/innen* die gleiche Freiheit, die ich mit meinem deutschen Pass genieße.

## 796. Discrimination in Germany

I got laid off from my job recently. The company wasn't doing economically well and decided to lay me off. It is sad, but it also makes me angry because I worked there for a long time, and people have joined the company even after me. It also makes me feel discriminated,  because I am the one with an immigration background and am gay. I believe it played a role in the management decision.  moreover, I applied for a different position in another company where a friend of mine is working,too. After going through all the procedures and interviews, my application was rejected without a reason. They even didn't give me a reason. So I asked my friend who works there what the case was, and he replied, "Honestly, they are looking for native Germans" . Why Germany is so racist, I can't understand. I have so many of these experiences in the working environment, in the housing market, and in everyday life. I am basically exhausted of being discriminated.

## 799. Together for a close-knit Democratic Federal European Union

Europe is currently in danger. Russia is pounding at the gates of Eastern European countries, and the ally United States has let Europe, the EU, know that it wishes to be less of an ally. I am nearly 75 years old and have not found the international situation as threatening as it is at this moment. More so than the Cuban Missile Crisis in 1962. My proposal is to relentlessly urge the heads of government of the member states of the European Union to allow international, and as far as I am concerned, national political decisions to be taken by the leaders of the European Union. They must grant the European Union more power and thereby make the EU a more powerful player in international politics.  
  
I am also in favor of reducing the 24 languages ​​of the European Union to six or seven. I am thinking of a main language for the EU and European Regional Languages. For example: one main language, one for Northwest Europe, Southwest Europe, and three or four languages ​​for Eastern Europe of Northeast, Central East, and Southeast Europe. Reducing the number of European languages ​​should happen without coercion; a kind of urgent natural process.

Zij moeten de Europese  Unie meer macht schenken en daardoor de EU ook een machtiger speler in de internationale politiek maken.

Het verminderen van de Europese talen zou zonder dwang moeten gebeuren; een soort urgent natuurlijk proces.

## 800. Stolen bike recovered thanks to police GPS tracker, despite police

My wife's electric bike had been stolen. Fortunately, a GPS tracker was installed in the bike by the police two years ago as part of a collaboration between the police and the Municipality of Utrecht. Five minutes after the theft, my wife calls the police. No urgency is assigned to the case. We file a report that same day, only to discover that the police are unaware of the GPS operation from two years ago. We provide the exact location of the bike. Three weeks later, we find the bike ourselves when the location is near a bicycle dealer. Fortunately, this dealer is willing to cooperate (at his request, without police involvement). We withdraw our report.  
  
Two weeks later, we receive a call from the police: asking if the bike is still at the location we provided with the report. After all, they have a team standing by to intervene there…

<u>Original title (nl)</u> : Gestolen fiets terug dankzij politie-gps-tracker, ondanks politie

<u>Original content (nl)</u> :

De elektrische fiets van mijn vrouw was gestolen. Gelukkig is er twee jaar geleden door de politie een gps-tracker in de fiets geïnstalleerd, in het kader van een samenwerking tussen de politie en de gemeente Utrecht. Vijf minuten na de diefstal belt mijn vrouw de politie. Er wordt geen urgentie aan gegeven. Dezelfde dag doen we aangifte en blijkt dat de politie niet op de hoogte is van de gps-actie van twee jaar geleden. We geven de exacte locatie van de fiets door. Na drie weken vinden we de fiets zelf terug als de locatie in de buurt van een fietshandelaar is. Gelukkig wil deze handelaar (op zijn verzoek zonder politie-bemoeienis) meewerken. We trekken onze aangifte in.   
Twee weken later worden we gebeld door de politie: of de fiets nog steeds op de locatie staat die we bij de aangifte hebben doorgegeven. Ze hebben namelijk een team paraat om daar in te vallen….

<u>Origin</u> : Netherlands  
<u>Language</u> : nl  
<u>Unique identifier</u> : voltnws

## 801. Democracy is in danger, let's stop kidding ourselves.

In light of current events (Trump, Elon Musk's Nazi salute, Elon Musk's interference in the German elections, the anti-European stance of Trump's allies, etc.), it's time for decisive action, not just empty words. We must ban parties that promote values ​​such as racism, hatred, and freedom of expression solely for their own benefit.  
  
Freedom of expression is a good thing, but only if it stops where it begins to denigrate others and prevent them from exercising their own freedom of expression.  
  
It's time to act, not just whine about the far right. Politicians have shown they are equally incapable of doing so. It's time for citizen action: boycotts, demonstrations, media censorship of the far right, and other ways to silence the far right (and the far left and center).  
  
When justice itself is being called into question, we can no longer remain indifferent to the gravity of the situation.  
  
We are fortunate to have photographic and video evidence of what happened during the Second World War, so we have the power to say "never again" and change the course of history.

<u>Original title (fr)</u> : La démocratie est en danger, arrêtons de nous voiler la face.

<u>Original content (fr)</u> :

Au vu de ce qu'il se passe actuellement (Trump, Salut nazi de Elon Musk, ingérence de Elon Musk dans les élections Allemande, le anti Europeen des alliés de Trump, etc.) il est temps d'agir fermement et non plus à coup de parole mais il faut interdire les partis prônant des valeurs telles que le racisme, la haine et la liberté d'expression à leurs seuls intérêts.  
  
La liberté d'expression est une bonne chose, seulement si elle s'arrête là où elle commence à dénigrer les autres et les empêcher d'avoir de la liberté d'expression.   
  
Il est temps d'agir et plus de geindre "oh non l'extrême droite". Les politiques ont montré qu'ils en sont également incapable. Il est temps par des actions citoyennes "boycott, manifestation, censure de l'extrême droite par les médias et autre manière de faire taire l'extrême droite (et l'extrême gauche et centre)".   
  
Lors que la justice elle même est remise en question, on ne peut plus rester insensible face à la gravité de la situation.  
  
Nous avons la chance d'avoir des preuves photos et vidéos de ce qu'il s'est passé lors de la seconde guerre mondiale, on a donc le pouvoir de dire "plus jamais ça" et de changer le cours de l'histoire.

## 807. Journey to the near future

There is a lot of negativity surrounding the energy transition. Unfeasible. Unaffordable. Meanwhile, all generations continue to travel more. At the same time, activists and conservatives are hardening in their trenches. My journey concerns the development of a new technology that you probably haven't heard of yet. But one that we have worked hard on over the past 7 years. With which we can give everyone their own compact power plant in their home. With which the citizen becomes master of their own home again. The transition is given a huge boost, because it is a green technology, cheaper than the most polluting and fossil energy. Decentralized, which prevents grid congestion. Because it is green, cheap, and European, that topic of polarization is off the table again. Win-win. As it should be. It is a typical product for Volt. Green, inclusive, and democratic. ## 810. We are fooling each other

Almost everyone makes a number of sustainable choices, such as separating waste or installing solar panels. But actually, this is an economic choice. If residual waste is not priced or solar panels are not profitable, then we simply won't do it. Furthermore, we misuse sustainable choices to continue using fossil fuels, to fly, etc.  
  
We do not want to formulate and implement necessary policy on a national level, but only within a European context or even more broadly. And there, we stall the process of policy making and accuse "Brussels" of undermining our sovereignty.  
  
In short, we cling to our self-interest even though the climate is deteriorating, poverty is increasing, and we are threatened by Russia, the US, Big Tech, etc. And no politician dares to expose this for fear of losing the favor of the voter. Whoever does dare gets my vote.

<u>Original content (nl)</u> :

Als restafval niet beprijsd wordt of zonnepanelen niet rendabel zijn dan doen we het niet. We misbruiken daarnaast ook nog de duurzame keuzes om wel fossiel te blijven gebruiken, om te vliegen etc.   
  
We willen noodzakelijk beleid niets land formuleren en uitvoeren, maar dat alleen in Europees verband of nog breder. En daar traineren we dat er beleid gemaakt wordt en verwijten "Brussel' dat onze soevereiniteit wordt aangetast.   
  
Kortom we houden vast aan ons eigenbelang ook al gaat het klimaat achteruit, neemt de armoede toe, worden we bedreigd door Rusland, VS, bigtech  etc. En geen politicus durft dit door te prikken om de gunst van de kiezer niet te verliezen. Wie wel durft krijgt mijn stem.

## 813. Rough awakening to a reality of indifference and populism.

Durring jobs in IT and manufacturing in Switzerland since 2022, I was surprised and disappointed by how colleagues reacted to the Russian war in Ukraine, both from the first day and until today. I witnessed some people adapting to Russian propaganda language, or appearing supporttive, and many or most appearing indifferent. Innitially I was part of a small group of people that supported a small humanitarian project, while later it became increasingly difficult to support any such cause. I experienced anything from ignorance to mobbing for being supportive of Ukraine, and it became the main cause for me to leave this company. In the second company, I witnessed an employee wearing an "AK47" T-shirt, which I was told openly as a "Nazi" but was "tolerated". In this company, there was also several business interestes connected to Russia and China. ## 814. European unity at Dreisessel

In November, around my wife's birthday, we went hiking in the Bavarian Forest with our dog.  
  
It's not a big deal, but the national park there, on the German and Czech sides, connects Europeans across borders and is an absolutely exceptional project that has prevailed against all odds and demonstrates what we are capable of as a united Europe.  
  
On the summit of the Dreisessel mountain, at the tripoint (though no longer within the national park), we could feel this connection together with Czechs, Austrians, and Germans amidst the wild nature of a Europe so heavily industrialized and paved over.  
  
More courage to embrace Europe, nature, and wilderness on a large scale is something Europe should champion, because that's how we build bridges.

<u>Original title (de)</u> : Europäische Einigkeit am Dreisessel

<u>Original content (de)</u> :

Im November über den Geburtstag meiner Frau waren wir gemeinsam mit unserem Hund wandern im bayerischen Wald.  
  
Es ist keine große Geschichte, aber der Nationalpark dort, auf deutscher und tschechischer Seite, verbindet Europäer über Grenzen hinweg und ist ein absolutes Ausnahmeprojekt, das sich gegen alle Widerstände behaupten konnte und zeigt, wozu wir als geeintes Europa fähig sind.  
  
Auf dem Gipfel des Dreisessels, am Dreiländereck, allerdings nicht mehr im Nationalpark, konnten wir diese Verbindung gemeinsam mit Tschechen, Österreichern und Deutschen inmitten wilder Natur im so stark industrialisierten und versiegelten Europa spüren.  
  
Mehr Mut zu Europa, zur Natur und zu Wildnis in großem Stil ist etwas, was sich Europa auf die Fahnen schreiben sollte, denn so bauen wir Brücken

## 819. Frozen in citizenship

I was in a hurry from my home walking towards the nearby train station to catch the train to work in the early morning around 7 am. It was cold and dark outside. When I passed over the usual small bridge that crosses over another bicycle pathway, two hooded high-school age boys from what I could see probably Dutch-Moroccan origin, just finished throwing firework from the bridge on the bicycle path below. The fireworks were strong and loud firecrackers and when they went off I felt the bridge tremble. When I looked below I saw that a man on a bicycle just missed the firecracker while cycling there. The boys were laughing and looked ready for another attempt to throw something down below. I wanted to do something to avoid innocent cyclists from getting fireworks in their clothes or being hurt, but was late for my train and already in a quick pace and the boys looked pretty daunting. What if they had knives or would throw the fireworks at me instead? I quickly checked on my phone but also could not really find the right number to call the police for such matters. I felt helpless and also a bit afraid of the situation. Without wanting to be discriminating or racist I wondered how our world has become like this and if I would feel the same if they were blond Dutch guys, but then again realistically I was thinking the chances that that would occur would likely be much smaller. I’m a very inclusive, anti-racist person, but felt very uncomfortable with this situation. What should I have done as a good citizen?

## 823. Guaranteeing equal opportunities is pointless (M. Sandel)

Dilemma: Choosing a long-term strategy.  
  
Europe suffers economically, socially, and politically from the Law of the Inhibiting Head Start. To valorize innovative concepts across these three domains, a shift in thinking is necessary.  
  
Compared to China and the US, Europe is less competitive, and there are leveled economic relations and significant political dependence on the US.  
Due to habituation to the welfare state, entrepreneurship has been undermined, while at the same time the role of the state and public utilities has diminished.

## 824. You always have to look at both sides of the coin.

It troubles me that our times are becoming increasingly turbulent and negative headlines are dominating the discussion more and more often.  
  
Everything that happens around us has two sides. Every problem is an opportunity for someone else.  
  
Anyone who makes a demand must consider the consequences of those desires.  
  
We cannot support climate change, transformations of all kinds, education, and improving the plight of many people with public funds without considering what we either have to cut elsewhere or who will provide us with the necessary resources.  
  
In current politics, especially during election campaigns, all parties outdo each other with promises of benefits.  
  
It's appalling that this still seems to resonate with voters.  
  
When will we start practicing honest politics?  
  
Who dares to deliver uncomfortable truths?  
  
Do our politicians still feel obligated to the well-being of the people, or solely to their clientele and re-election?  
  
It's time for new forces to have their chance – mind you: ONLY if they operate within the framework of our constitution, our laws, and the free and democratic order.  
  
Currently, for me, this is only Volt, the pan-European party.  
  


<u>Original title (de)</u> : Man muss immer beide Seiten der Münze betrachten

<u>Original content (de)</u> :

Mich treibt es um, dass unsere Zeit immer unruhiger wird und die negativen Schlagzeilen immer öfter die Diskussion beherrschen.  
Dabei hat alles, was um uns herum geschieht, zwei Seiten. Jedes Problem ist für einen anderen eine Chance.   
Jeder, der eine Forderung hat, muss die Konsequenzen dieser Wünsche mit berücksichtigen.   
Wir können nicht Klima, Transformationen aller Art, Bildung, Verbesserung der Notlage vieler Menschen mit staatliche Mitteln unterstützen,  
ohne uns Gedanken darum zu machen, was wir   
- entweder dafür woanders streichen wollen oder  
- wer uns die dafür notwendigen Mittel zur Verfügung stellt  
  
  
In der aktuellen Politik, insbesondere zu Wahlkampfzeiten, überbieten sich alle Parteien damit, welche Wohltaten sie verteilen wollen.   
Es ist schlimm, dass es tatsächlich immer noch bei den Wählern zu verfangen scheint.  
Wann fangen wir an, ehrliche Politik zu machen?  
Wer traut sich, unbequeme Wahrheiten zu transportieren?  
Fühlen sich unsere Politiker noch dem Wohle des Volkes verpflichtet, oder ausschließlich ihrer Klientel und Wiederwahl?  
Es wird Zeit, dass neue Kräfte ihre Chance erhalten - wohlgemerkt: NUR, wenn sie sich auf dem Boden unserer Verfassung, unserer Gesetze   
und der freiheitlichen Grundordnung bewegen.   
Aktuell ist dies für mich nur Volt, die pan-europäische Partei.

## 825. The power of connection

Individualism fueled by 20 years of neoliberalism and populism is currently running rampant in politics. It bothers me that citizens seem to behave primarily like consumers: spoon-feed me, tell me what to do so I don't have to think or take initiative myself.  
  
A positive, inclusive, and proactive voice can activate people/citizens to act more collectively from a perspective of living together and being supported. Looking more from a sense of unity at what binds everyone together, rather than what I think I want (because I hear/read/see that I should want it). At the music association, I see that making music together has a connecting effect and sparks and stimulates encounters with those who think and live differently, because we all share the connecting factor in the love of making music.

## 826. How wonderful is it that we can go live, study or work abroad in any EU country and have equal rights and opportunities to locals?

This was a pretty amazing experience for me (and all my fellow students from abroad), and give that some 80 years ago Nazi Germany attacked the Netherlands, I want to stay still for a moment to appreciate how amazing it is that we came that far.   
  
Every Dutch person I met was friendly and welcoming. Some have some stereotypes about Germans ("you're German? You must like cars &amp; beers then"), but that's okay, overall I felt pretty welcome and appreciated. I also learned Dutch, which helped too, but even if I had not spoken any Dutch I would probably still have been welcomed.

## 829. In life in wonder

The recent court ruling in favor of Greenpeace is remarkable insofar as the 'political' response is that the law must be amended accordingly. As if the rules were not made by ourselves and in Europe. It is also noteworthy that everyone subsequently focuses exclusively on livestock, as if industry and transporters like Schiphol do not make an enormous contribution to the nitrogen problem. What is Tatasteel's contribution to society, if on the one hand they receive a subsidy on energy tax and on the other negatively impact the lifespans of local residents? Why is Schiphol so large if the benefits of the hub function are demonstrably absent? Why is the slot system not adjusted, now that it is a relic from the previous century? It ossifies market forces, holds back newcomers, and ensures that KLM and other established airlines prefer to take off with empty planes just to retain their slots. Our surface area is the worst in Europe. I believe that only 1% of it meets the requirements. Due to the unnecessary size of Schiphol, we cannot realize 10,000 homes in South and North Holland. I am actually in favor of market forces and am therefore of the opinion that these types of subsidies must be critically examined.

<u>Original title (nl)</u> : In leven in verwondering

<u>Original content (nl)</u> :

De recente uitspraak van de rechter ten gunste van Greenpeace is in zoverre bijzonder dat de 'politiek' antwoordt dat de wet hierop aangepast moet worden. Alsof de regels niet door onszelf en in Europa zijn gemaakt. Opmerkelijk is ook dat iedereen zich vervolgens uitsluitend op de veestapel stort, alsof de industrie en transporteurs zoals Schiphol niet een enorme bijdrage leveren aan het stikstofprobleem. Wat is de bijdrage aan de samenleving door Tatasteel, als zij enerzijds een subsidie krijgen op de energiebelasting en anderzijds de levensduur van de omwonenden negatief beïnvloeden. Waarom is Schiphol zo groot, als de voordelen van de hubfunctie aantoonbaar afwezig zijn. Waarom wordt het slotsysteem niet aangepast, nu het een relikwie is uit de vorige eeuw. Het verkalkt de marktwerking, houdt nieuwkomers tegen en zorgt ervoor dat de KLM en andere gevestigde maatschappijen liever met lege vliegtuigen opstijgen om maar de slots te behouden. Ons oppervlakte is het slechtste van Europa. Ik geloof dat slechts 1% ervan aan de eisen voldoen. Door de onnodige omvang van Schiphol kunnen we 10.000 woningen niet realiseren in Zuid- en Noord Holland. Ik ben juist voor marktwerking en ben daarom van mening dat dit soort subsidies kritisch tegen het licht gehouden moet worden.

## 836. Studying abroad in the EU due to EU Nationality

Because of my country of origin being in the EU I had the opportunity to complete my bachelor’s degree abroad for the same tuition fees as Dutch citizens in the Netherlands.   
  
It was an amazing opportunity for me and I believe my Dutch classmates as we both got exposed to many people of different nationalities each with also a different way of thinking.   
  
Because of this experience I am more tolerant and more open minded as a person.   
  
Of course the education was also excellent and generally I did not feel discriminated against except only for finding housing where “Dutch only” adverts were common.  I am conflicted on how I feel about that. On the one hand,  I understand that Dutch students-housemates might want to go cohabitate with other Dutch people to feel comfortable but on the other hand it feels slightly wrong to discriminate against in this way.

## 842. Amsterdam welcomes foreigners but leaves them to their fate.

For over a year, I cared for an elderly German man who used to moor his dilapidated sailboat on the bank of the water we overlook. He lived a very unhealthy lifestyle, drank and smoked heavily, but also needed care. Our welfare state could not provide it, especially because he was a foreigner. After more than a year, he passed away on his boat. He was picked up by the municipality, and they gave him a very solitary funeral (just my wife and I, and a representative from the neighborhood team) at the municipality's expense. It is a pity that nothing could really be done for him during his lifetime.

<u>Original title (nl)</u> : Amsterdam verwelkomt vreemdelingen maar laat ze wel aan hun lot over

Hij is door de gemeente opgehaald en men heeft hem een heel eenzame (alleen mijn vrouw en ik, en een vertegenwoordiger van het buurtteam) uitvaart gegeven op kosten van de gemeente. ## 851. We need to listen more

I am very worried about the future of our democracy / democracies. The developments in the US offer a glimpse into the type of oligarchy, cronyism, and corruption that awaits us here in Europe as well. I feel that with social media and billionaires, Russia and China spreading misinformation and propaganda, all we can influence is our direct environment, people in our immediate communities. I am disheartened by the lack of willingness to engage, listen, accept other people's viewpoints. I understand how many people feel nobody is listening to them, and I would really like to help with that. When you listen to people, without judgment, they open up and like feeling heard. I just do not know how sustainable any of this is.  
The specific experience: I ended up in hospital in Austria, and I shared my room with two women I would never have met in my normal life. Both voted for the FPÖ (far right) in the last elections. These were the first people I have ever met who said they voted for that party, and I was a little shocked. They were nice, reasonable, friendly women who tried to make their lives work and who were concerned about the state of the country. They felt that nobody is interested in them and nobody would listen anyway. I did not start fights with them, I just listened and let them explain to me what they thought was the point in elections, in voting for the FPÖ, how they did not take the racism (and homophobia etc.) too seriously, how they felt they had no other choice. It opened my eyes to see they were compassionate and intelligent people and not the dumb racist nazis I had expected these voters to be. I will not vote far right ever, but I know better than to demonise the people we can still reach.

## 852. Future?

A campaign poster in Berlin: The star is a male politician, born in 1948! Everywhere I look, 'old people' and their views dominate the political scene. In Germany, in the EU.  
  
If this doesn't change, we have no future. When I share these thoughts with others of my generation (born in 1976), I encounter incomprehension. Young people are said to be uninterested/incapable/have the wrong priorities.  
  
How presumptuous are we older folks, denying the very people whose future is at stake any say – just because things aren't continuing as usual for us?!?

## 853. Hatred and envy towards everything they have not learned to respect from a young age, or which they can manipulate and exploit for their personal benefit.

A few years ago, I moved within Germany from a western to an eastern state. There, I'm constantly pressured to explain my background, my circumstances, why I moved there, what I want to do there, and why I don't go somewhere else. This is accompanied by repeated false accusations, insults, threats, and sexist remarks directed at me, all from locals and almost exclusively from older people, around 50 years and up. When I realize what they think of me and what they're threatening me with, it hits me like a ton of bricks every time. I'll just pick out one episode with a neighbor as an example:  
  
A neighbor, initially quite friendly, arranged to meet me. She talked about herself, laughed about my birthday on Walpurgis Night, April 30th, and listened to me. Until, after a few months, she started making antisemitic remarks about me in a friendly, conversational tone: She said my clothes were missing a "brooch," two triangles, preferably sunflower yellow. Or she repeatedly recommended that I walk as far as possible along the paths behind the houses on the edge of the settlement. She thought they were especially suitable for me in the spring, regardless of whether I went left or right; whatever I experienced there, she assured me, would be the absolute and highest thing in my life. I thought of beautiful scenery and viewpoints until I realized she was referring to the Nazi routes used to evacuate the camps in April 1945. To the left led to the labor camps, and to the right, the brutal, often deadly marches across the Harz Mountains. There are more examples like this. I try to avoid her now, to keep my distance.  
  
But after the last New Year, I had something to do at the post office on my very first day back at work. We were standing one behind the other in line. She had a bad cold, looked pale and ill. I was simply being polite, greeted her, and automatically wished her a Happy New Year. She sneezed and sniffled and replied that her current information wasn't good enough for her to still be hoping for anything good. I asked if it was because of her cold. Afterward, I wanted to go to the pharmacy myself and offered to pick up some medicine for her. She replied, "Why the pharmacy? You're still here."

<u>Original title (de)</u> : Hass und Neid auf alles, was sie nicht von klein auf zu respektieren gelernt haben oder zu ihrem persönlichen Vorteil manipulieren und ausschlachten können.

<u>Original content (de)</u> :

Ich zog vor einigen Jahren innerhalb Deutschlands von einem westlichen in ein östliches Bundesland. Dort werde ich immer wieder bedrängt, Rechenschaft zu geben über meine Herkunft, meine Lebensumstände, warum ich gerade dorthin ziehe, was ich dort will und warum ich nicht wo anders hin gehe. Dabei werden auch immer wieder falsche Anschuldigungen, Beleidigungen, Drohungen und Sexismus gegen mich vorgebracht, allesamt von den Einheimischen und fast nur von Älteren ab ca. 50 Jahren. Wenn ich dann begreife, was die von mir denken und womit die mir drohen, trifft es mich jedes Mal wie ein Stromschlag. Ich picke hier nur mal eine Episode mit einer Nachbarin als Beispiel heraus:  
  
Eine Nachbarin, zeigte sich anfangs vergleichsweise freundlich, verabredete sich mit mir. Sie erzählte von sich, lachte über meinen Geburtstag in der "Walpurgisnacht" am 30. April  und hörte mir zu.  Bis sie nach einigen Monaten anfing in freundlichem Erzählton antisemitische Aussagen über mich zu machen: An meiner Kleidung fehle eine "Brosche", zwei Dreiecke und die am Besten in Sonnenblumengelb. Oder sie empfahl mir mehrfach, die Wege hinter den Häusern am Rande der Siedlung möglichst weit entlangzuwandern. Die fände sie besonders im Frühling genau passend für mich, egal ob ich nach links oder rechts gehen würde, was ich da erlebe, fände ich bestimmt das Absolute und Höchste in meinem Leben. Ich dachte an schöne Natur und Aussichtspunkte, bis ich herausfand, daß sie die Nazi-Routen zur Räumung der Lager im April 1945 meinte. Nach links ging es zu den Arbeitslagern und nach rechts führten die brutalen oft tödlichen Märsche über den Harz. Es gibt noch mehr solcher Beispiele. Ich versuche sie inzwischen zu meiden, räumliche Distanz zu ihr zu halten.  
  
Aber nach dem letzten Jahreswechsel hatte ich gleich am ersten Arbeitstag etwas bei der Post zu erledigen. Da standen wir hintereinander in der  Warteschlange. Sie war stark erkältet, sah grau und krank aus. Ich war lediglich höflich, grüßte sie und wünschte ihr automatisch ein schönes Neues Jahr. Sie nieste und schniefte und antwortete, so gut wären ihre aktuellen Informationen nicht, daß Sie noch auf Schönes hoffe.  Ich fragte, ob es wegen der Erkältung sei. Im Anschluß wollte ich selber zur Apotheke gehen und bot ihr an, ihr ein Medikament mitzubringen. Sie antwortete, wieso Apotheke? Sie sind noch da.

## 854. Dissolution of the European Union

It seems to me that the citizens of Europe increasingly despise the European Union. Societies are increasingly demanding more nationalist policies, reminiscent of "America First!" and in opposition to the EU. These desires often culminate in exit movements. Many people seem not to understand that only a strong and united (or even a single) EU can lead to the prosperity of each individual member state. The relatively small nation-states would quickly fade into global insignificance.

## 855. Humanity is splitting apart

My current experience is that the world is becoming increasingly divided. AI is promoting monotony of opinion across all social networks, rather than diversity of opinion. People are losing themselves in their virtual bubbles, and healthy exchange of views is becoming increasingly difficult due to prejudices from both the political left/center to the political right and vice versa. This is compounded by mistrust and the denial of facts that don't fit into the worldview of either side. I miss the thought leaders who seek common ground with all factions and stand up against this societal division. No one should be excluded from the discourse.

## 856. The shifting world order versus nationalism

What concerns me most: The voter has lost their way, and this is leading to a very unsafe world. Because of ourselves (the voter), we are saddled (both domestically and internationally) with right-wing radical politicians who think small and populistically, and make decisions on matters like migration in scapegoat terms. Wrong! But, in my view: it is the voter who is poorly informed or is deliberately misinformed. We are now stuck with far too few politicians who are incapable of strategic thinking. This affects us. All European countries—even Germany or France—are too small to make a dent in a pack of butter compared to the US and China. We will only be strong if countries cooperate with each other, for example within a European framework (though it can also be done differently and more broadly). The EU is tool number 1, but national parliaments allow themselves to become paralyzed, and in turn, paralyze the EU. This is problem number 1. Without a strong and cooperating EU, we will become an international plaything instead of a player, and our rule of law, freedom, and economy will depend on other global players. Great. Characteristic of this form is that peace and security are mentioned last.  
  
The greatest challenges:  
  
International security in relation to democracy and the rule of law  
Trade and economy in relation to climate change and defense  
Strong governance (manageable rules and cooperation)

## 863. Misery amidst prosperity

## 867. The new Gold Rush

I live in a small town in northern Extremadura. The Western Spain gas pipeline passes just over a kilometer from the town. One of those companies springing up in the wake of the biogas boom—a modern version of those other "gold rush" episodes throughout history—has set its sights on this and many other small towns to install one of its biogas plants. In this region, as in Castile-La Mancha, Castile and León, Andalusia, and elsewhere, many small towns are threatened by these types of facilities, located in many cases, like ours, just over a kilometer from the town center. Unfortunately, the local authorities see them as a source of income for the municipal coffers through the fees these companies will have to pay the town hall, but the harm they will cause to the population will not be compensated by that revenue. We believe these farms will definitively destroy these small towns, which in recent years had experienced a reversal of the depopulation trend and were seeing new residents choosing to settle there. Above all, we live in terror of the threat posed by these disastrous factory farms. These can be located up to two kilometers from population centers. We feel abandoned, as the two major political parties and their local authorities are generally enthusiastic about these types of facilities. In our case, Podemos is the only party that sympathizes with us and has made some interventions in the Assembly of Extremadura to promote the examination and discussion of this new technology and the current, practically nonexistent, legislation to regulate it. We would be grateful if any other political party would take notice of this issue and promote its discussion.

<u>Original title (es)</u> : La nueva Fiebre del Oro

<u>Original content (es)</u> :

Vivo en un pequeño pueblo del Norte de Extremadura. El gasoducto del oeste de España pasa a poco más de un kilómetro de la población. Una empresa de esas que están surgiendo a raíz de la fiebre del biogás, moderna versión de esos otros episodios de "fiebre del oro" que han ocurrido en la Historia, se ha fijado en éste y otros muchos pequeños pueblos para instalar una de esas planta de biogás. En esta región, como en Castilla- la Mancha, Castilla y León, Andalucía,  etc, son muchos los pueblecitos amenazados con ese tipo de instalaciones, situadas en muchos casos, como el de nuestro pueblo, a algo más de un kilómetro del núcleo urbano.  Desgraciadamente las autoridades locales ven en ellas una fuente de ingresos para las arcas municipales por las tasas que estas empresas tendrán que pagar al Ayuntamiento, pero los perjuicios que van a ocasionar a la población no serán compensados por esos ingresos. Creemos que estas plantas van a acabar definitivamente con  estos pequeños pueblos que en los últimos años habían experimentado un cambio de tendencia en el problema de la despoblación y estaban viendo cómo nuevos pobladores los elegían para instalarse en ellos a vivir sus vidas. Sobre todo vivimos con el terror de la amenaza de las nefastas macrogranjas. Estas pueden instalarse hasta  a dos kilómetros de los centros de población. Nos sentimos desamparados, pues los dos grandes partidos políticos y sus autoridades locales en general son entusiastas de este tipo de instalaciones. En nuestro caso Podemos es el único partido que simpatiza con nosotros y ha hecho alguna intervención en la Asamblea de Extremadura para promover el examen y la discusión de esta nueva tecnología y la actual prácticamente inexistente legislación para regularla. Agradeceríamos que cualquier otro partido político se fijara en este asunto y promoviera su discusión.

## 869. Empathy

Working as a school assistant at a school where certainly over 90% of the students have a migration background. Being right there among the young people and experiencing what moves and worries them.  
  
That keeps me young, even at almost 50, and they give me a predominantly positive impression of our new generation.  
  
Of course, this generation has to deal with more worries and anxieties than before, and it's important to me to help them.  
  
But I don't know how much longer I can afford to do it, since the pay is abysmal.  
  
I would find it very difficult to give up this job due to financial constraints.

<u>Original title (de)</u> : Empathie

<u>Original content (de)</u> :

Als Schulbegleiter an einer Schule mit sicherlich über 90% Migrationsanteil zu arbeiten. Als solcher mitten unter den Jugendlich zu sein und zu erleben was sie bewegt und sorgt.  
Das hält mich, mit fast 50, jung und sie vermitteln mir ein überwiegend positives Bild unserer neuen Generation.  
  
Natürlich hat diese Generation mit mehr Sorgen und Ängsten zu kämpfen als zuvor und es ist mir wichtig ihnen zu helfen.  
Nur weiß ich nicht wie lange ich es mir noch leisten kann, da die Bezahlung unterirdisch ist.  
Ich würde mich sehr schwer damit tun diese Tätigkeit aus wirtschaftlichem Zwang aufgeben zu müssen.

## 876. Empowerment, a job, safety, and hope for women, avant la lettre.

A story for you at Volt  
  
1977: the birth of Moeder’s Geuren floral incense.  
  
Empowerment, a job, safety, and hope for women, avant la lettre.  
  
In 1977, there were no jobs for women. For a woman, there was only domestic work.  
  
A woman was not allowed to work after getting married (as was the case in the Netherlands a long time ago).  
  
At our studio, they were often allowed by their husbands to continue working because it is a safe environment for women here.  
And with us, women found hope for a better life, especially for their children.  
  
And our incense was organic, hand-rolled, and sustainable.  
All types of incense in India were odorless when rolled at home, and later the sticks were dipped in a factory (the dip method) in an incense oil diluted up to 7 to 10 times with phthalates, which are now banned due to hormone disruption. With our incense, the incense oil is not diluted but used directly in the incense dough (the masala method). Therefore, the incense cannot be rolled at home and can only be done under supervision in a workshop. Hence the jobs that were created for women. When I had to leave, there were around 200 women working there.  
  
Now, in India, virtually all incense is ‘rolled’ by machine due to cost-effectiveness. Depending on its size, a machine can take over the rolling from 50 to 200 women.  
  
However, we continue to roll by hand.  
  
A fun fact is that the packaging of the incense consists of hand-marbled paper, making every pack unique since 1977: a unique gift made by women.  
  
https://winkel.wierook.nl/videos/  
  


<u>Original title (nl)</u> : Empowerment, een baan, veiligheid en hoop voor vrouwen, avant la lettre.

<u>Original content (nl)</u> :

Een verhaal voor jullie bij Volt  
  
1977: de geboorte van de Moeder’s Geuren bloemenwierook.  
  
Empowerment, een baan, veiligheid en hoop voor vrouwen, avant la lettre.  
  
In 1977 waren er geen banen voor vrouwen. Er was voor een vrouw alleen werk in de huishouding.   
Een vrouw mocht na haar trouwen niet meer werken (zoals heel vroeger in Nederland).  
Bij ons atelier mochten ze vaak van hun man blijven werken omdat het bij ons vrouw-veilig is.  
En bij ons kregen de vrouwen hoop op een beter bestaan, vooral voor hun kinderen.  
  
En onze wierook was biologisch, handgerold en duurzaam.  
Alle wierooksoorten in India werden geurloos thuis gerold en later werden de stokjes in een fabriek gedipt (de dip methode) in een wierookolie verdund tot zelfs 7 tot 10 keer met ftalaten, die nu verboden zijn vanwege hormoonverstoringen.   
Bij onze wierook wordt de wierookolie niet verdund, maar direct in het wierookdeeg gebruikt (de masala methode). De wierook kan daarom niet thuis gerold worden en alleen onder toezicht in een atelier. Vandaar de banen die voor vrouwen gecreëerd werden. Toen ik moest vertrekken werkten er rond de 200 vrouwen.   
Nu wordt in India vrijwel alle wierook, vanwege goedkoopte, met een machine ‘gerold’. Een machine, afhankelijk van de grootte, kan het rollen overnemen van 50 tot 200 vrouwen.   
Wij blijven echter met de hand rollen.   
  
Een leuk weetje is dat de verpakking van de wierook bestaat uit handgemarmerd papier, waardoor elk pakje sinds 1977 uniek is: een uniek cadeau gemaakt door vrouwen.   
  
https://winkel.wierook.nl/videos/

## 880. Polarisation without reason.

I volunteered to help in litigation against the current government's agricultural policies. Everyone I meet is committed to a fair deal for farmers, and to urging the government to push for a chance to help the transition to a better, more ecological way of farming. No-one has ever said anything against agriculture in general. I cannot fathom the hate we get online, mostly based on lies and identity politics. I am honestly scared for this country, where policies aren't chosen on science and the best way forward, but because groups in society hate 'us' for being 'radical lefties out to destroy society'. I wish I could talk to all these people. I wish I knew, could understand what drives them to hate.

## 882. Rethinking citizenship and nationhood

Categorizing people has always been impossible, yet attempts are constantly made. I'm a youth coordinator at a sports club, naturally with many children (a majority?) from immigrant backgrounds. Even in my own children's school classes, many don't have "German-sounding" names. Almost all of them have German citizenship, perhaps even a second nationality. My children also have dual citizenship, though not from a country typically associated with "repatriation" (would one deport someone to Japan for a crime?). When politicians and the media openly discuss supposedly different categories of German citizenship and distinctions based on first names, what does that do to all these children? How are they supposed to develop a natural sense of self-confidence and trust in their country?

<u>Original title (de)</u> : Staatsangehörigkeit und Staatsvolk neu denken

<u>Original content (de)</u> :

Menschen in Kategorien zu unterteilen, war schon immer unmöglich, wird aber trotzdem immer wieder versucht. Ich bin Jugendwart in einem Sportverein, natürlich mit vielen Kindern (Mehrheit?) mit Migrationshintergrund. Auch in den Schulklassen meiner eigenen Kinder haben viele keinen "Deutsch-klingenden" Namen. Die Deutsche Staatsangehörigkeit haben fast alle, vielleicht auch eine zweite. Meine Kinder haben auch eine zweite Staatsangehörigkeit, wenn auch nicht aus einem Land, das man üblicherweise mit "Rückführung" in Verbindung bringt (würde man bei Straftaten auch nach Japan Abschieben?). Wenn jetzt offen in der Politik und den Medien über wie auch immer unterschiedene Klassen von Deutschen Staatsangehörigkeiten und Unterscheidungen über den Vornamen gesprochen wird, was macht das mit all den Kindern? Wie sollen sie ein natürliches Selbstbewusstsein und Vertrauen in Ihren Staat haben?

## 883. HBO more effective, cheaper. And much more fun for everyone!

Recently, I have experienced just how inefficient and bureaucratic our higher education system is. I speak from my own experience in higher professional education, as a lecturer at two completely different universities of applied sciences. Coming from the field, I see how seemingly intangible, inefficient, and unfortunately not prioritizing the public interest, things are run.  
  
I come from the field myself and see that within higher professional education, it seems to be more about procedures, structure, and the knowledge of textbook authors than about useful knowledge from academia and practice. Consider, for example, lessons learned and the like.  
  
Universities of applied sciences assess each other in order to safeguard quality. The organizations for which students are being trained play only a marginal role.  
  
The system creates its own reality. Once the process has been followed, the outcome is no longer open to debate. A practical example is the notion that student engagement is supposed to come from strict rules in the classroom, which is proclaimed with a straight face. Structure trumps passion for the student.  
And consider, for instance, the hype focused on 'skills'. The skill of 'collaboration' means that almost all assessment is group work. Important, but to put it mildly: it makes grading nice and quick. And the student does not collaborate; tasks are simply divided among themselves.  
  
The HBO system is not useless, but it could be much, much more efficient.  
  
A concrete example of improvement:  
  
Internships in Business Administration are only available in year 2, if the student is lucky. At the HvA, that is something still being investigated, because there it is only mandatory in year 3. And this despite the fact that all my colleagues agree that students only understand what we teach as lecturers after an internship, and that students subsequently show much more interest and 'grab' it.  
  
I advocate for simultaneous internships and theory. Starting from the first year. And then a different internship every few months, in as different an organization as possible.  
  
Advantages:  
  
- direct link with practice, instead of something devised by my colleagues who are detached from the field. - in classrooms, exchange takes place based on the latest insights  
- students contribute to society sooner  
- students know years earlier what they want after their studies, what suits them  
- students understand what they are learning for; this motivates: more attention from the student, a faster learning curve, better understanding, and much less dropout in the first two years, which currently affects half (!) of the students.  
  
In short, quality and enjoyment go up and costs go down!  
  
Another example: student numbers are dropping sharply, new lecturers are not being hired, yet Windesheim Almere is about to start new construction in the center of Almere. In all honesty, that serves egos and not the public interest. That costs money that does not go to education itself.  
  
Raised in an entrepreneurial family, I started working from the age of 15, studied law, and subsequently worked for small and very large organizations. A few years ago, I became a lecturer in Business Administration at the HBO level. First at a small program and recently at a very large HBO program.

<u>Original title (nl)</u> : HBO doeltreffender, goedkoper. En voor iedereen veel leuker!

<u>Original content (nl)</u> :

Recent heb ik ervaren hoe inefficient en bureaucratisch ons hoger onderwijs is. Ik spreek uit eigen HBO ervaring, als docent bij twee totaal verschillende hogescholen. Afkomstig uit de praktijk zie ik hoe schijnbaar ongrijpbaar inefficient en helaas ook niet in met het maatschappelijk belang voorop het er aan toe gaat.  
  
Ik kom zelf uit de praktijk en zie dat het binnen het HBO meer om procedures , structuur en kennis van schrijvers van lesboeken lijkt te gaan dan de nuttige kennis uit de wetenschap en praktijk. Denk ook aan lessons learned e.d.   
HBO's beoordelen elkaar om zo de kwaliteit te borgen. De organisaties waarvoor wordt opgeleid spelen maar een marginale rol.   
  
Het systeem creëert een eigen werkelijkheid. Als het proces gevolgd is, staat de uitkomst niet meer ter discussie. Een praktisch voorbeeld is dat de binding met student zou moeten komen uit strenge regels in de klas, wat met droge ogen wordt verkondigd. De structuur wint het van de passie voor de student.  
En zoals bijvoorbeeld de hype gericht op 'vaardigheden'. De vaardigheid 'samenwerken' maakt dat bijna alle toetsing groepswerk is. Belangrijk, maar flauw gezegd: het is lekker snel nakijken. En de student werkt niet samen, maar men verdeelt alleen onderling de taken.  
  
Het HBO systeem is niet nutteloos, maar het kan veel, veel efficiënter.   
  
Een concreet verbetervoorbeeld:   
Stage bij Bedrijfskunde is er pas in jaar 2, als de student geluk heeft. Bij de HvA is dat iets wat nog onderzocht wordt, want daar is dat pas verplicht in jaar 3. En dat terwijl al mijn collega's het erover eens zijn dat de studenten pas na stage begrijpen wat we als docent onderwijzen en dat studenten daarna veel meer interesse tonen en het 'pakken'.  
  
Ik pleit voor gelijktijdige stage en theorie. Vanaf het eerste jaar. En dan iedere paar maanden een andere stage, in een zo verschillend mogelijke organisatie.  
voordelen:   
- directe koppeling met praktijk, ipv bedacht door mijn collega's met afstand tot de praktijk.  
- in klaslokalen vind de uitwisseling plaats op basis van de nieuwste inzichten  
- studenten dragen al eerder bij een de maatschappij  
- studenten weten jaren eerder wat ze willen na hun studie, wat er bij ze past  
- studenten begrijpen waar ze voor leren; dit motiveert: meer aandacht van de student, sneller leercurve, beter begrip en veel minder uitval in de eerste twee jaar, wat nu de helft (!) van de studenten betreft.  
  
Kortom kwaliteit en plezier omhoog en kosten omlaag!  
  
Nog een voorbeeld: de student aantallen lopen fors terug, nieuwe docenten worden niet aangenomen, maar Windesheim Almere staat op het punt nieuwbouw te gaan plegen in het centrum van Almere. Dat dient in alle eerlijkheid ego's en niet het maatschappelijk belang. Dat kost geld dat niet naar het onderwijs zelf gaat.  
  
Opgegroeid in een ondernemersgezin, vanaf 15e meegewerkt rechten gestudeerd en vervolgens bij kleine en hele grote organisaties gewerkt. Een paar jaar geleden ben ik docent geworden bij HBO Bedrijfskunde. Eerst bij een kleine en recent bij een hele grote HBO opleiding.

## 888. Volt for the elderly

I am a strong supporter of Volt's ideals and have been since far before Volt existed, in fact, ever since I was part of a small group of Dutch and German youth who briefly toyed with the idea of setting up a pan-European party over 40 years ago. That is why I became a member Volt while still living in Canada. At the moment I am in transit between Canada and the Netherlands; due to personal circumstances I can no longer work full-time and I'm obliged to avoid the slippery conditions of Canadian winters by living in Holland during that time. In the course of the next three years I will gradually transition to the Netherlands permanently. Unfortunately, I have found it rather difficult to get in touch with other members of Volt in my community. As far as a person of my generation is concerned, the emphasis Volt places on computer literacy is perhaps overly optimistic, especially as I am a person with certain physical challenges, notably in terms of fine motor skills. I find it difficult enough to keep abreast of basic developments within the world of smart phones and computers and often feel that both expects more of me on this front than I can realistically achieve. I appreciate however that my personal situation is quite complex. Nonetheless I think it would be very helpful if all had a "helpdesk" for those who, like me, find it difficult to chart a course on their own through Volt's online presence. I have, for example, been singularly unsuccessful in finding a way I could volunteer for volt in my community.

## 894. Disinformation

A conversation with someone who went completely wild about the wonderful Trump and expressed the hope that things would turn out just as successfully with Wilders. A conversation with someone who lives across from a primary school and is annoyed that almost all the children are Black. Because: this is how far we have come. A conversation with someone who is at the bottom of society and curses the SP and all left-wing parties. The more right-wing, the better.  
  
You mention his benefits, the subsidies, the allowances, the childcare. It doesn't help. The indoctrination is so intense that these people do not realize that they are not improving their social and societal situation with Wilders and co. It is the most significant shift towards fascistic politics. And because the Left is doing its best but has little new narrative, I agree with MP De Hoop that a new party might be the solution. But Volt can fill that gap by being less of a one-issue party and providing explanations more often in simple terms.  
  
We need to descend to these people.

Maar Volt kan in dat gat springen door minder one issue partij te zijn en vaker uitleg geven in Jip en Janneketaal.   
We moeten afdalen naar deze mensen.

## 896. Policy and support from the bottom up, backed by governments from above

I place my experience in the province of Groningen. I am part of an initiative by Toukomst, part of NPG. The name of our initiative is 't Wad tot Stad', where 'Stad' stands for the city of Groningen. Toukomst is a citizens' initiative. We chose the Reitdiep as the backbone of the area from Lauwersmeer and Middag Humsterland to the city of Groningen in order to protect cultural and historical values ​​without closing off the area to residents, entrepreneurs, and farmers. Our initiative aligns well with the vision of the three municipalities in the area, including the Water Board and the Province of Groningen. The final stage of our work is the development of a Landscape Vision that is supported as broadly as possible.  
  
It is exciting to see how national politics (the BBB in the current government) will position itself in the coming period, as cabinet policy will help shape the framework for the further development of the Landscape Vision. We work from the bottom up and currently still have a lot of administrative support. A promising idea, therefore.

Wij hebben het Reitdiep, als drager voor het gebied van Lauwersmeer, Middag Humsterland tot de stad Groningen, gekozen om de cultuurhistorische waarden te beschermen, zonder het gebied op slot te zetten voor inwoners, ondernemers en boeren. Ons initiatief sluit goed aan bij wat de drie gemeenten in het gebied voor ogen staat, inclusief het Waterschap en de Provincie Groningen. Het sluitstuk van ons werk is het ontwikkelen van een Landschapsvisie, die zo breed mogelijk gedragen wordt.

## 899. Democracy remains a matter for our representatives.

Time and again, I hear in the media that a referendum is the only way to achieve a true democracy. And theoretically, that is true.  
In fact, I once registered (and owned) the domains internetkamer.nl and derdekamer.nl.  
  
However, two important factors make this view (my idealistic view at the time) so incredibly naive:  
  
1. Every decision we can vote on has so many consequences that the average Dutch person cannot comprehend them. Therefore, it is very difficult for a non-expert to take a stance on this, and it can easily lead to unintended 'collateral damage'; we do not send our best people to vote for us for nothing!  
  
2. The media is no longer objective, and what is more, social media is not in the hands of a neutral Dutch (European) party. We stand no chance whatsoever if the social media magnates want anything.

<u>Original title (nl)</u> : Democratie blijft een zaak van onze vertegenwoordigers

<u>Original content (nl)</u> :

Ik hoor in de media elke keer opnieuw dat een referendum pas een echte democratie zou opleveren. En theoretisch is dat ook zo.  
Sterker nog, ik heb ooit het domein internetkamer.nl en derdekamer.nl geregistreerd (gehad).  
  
Echter, twee belangrijke zaken maken dit beeld (mijn toenmalige idealistische beeld) zo ongelovelijk naief:  
1. elke beslissing waar we over kunnen stemmen heeft zoveel consequenties dat een gemiddelde Nederlander dit niet kan overzien. Dus het is erg moeilijk om als niet expert hier stelling in te nemen en kan eenvoudig leiden tot niet bedoelde 'colleteral damage'; wij vaardigen niet voor niets onze beste mensen om voor ons te kiezen!  
2. de media is niet meer objectief en sterker nog, social media is niet in handen van een neutrale Nederlandse (Europese) partij. We maken geen schijn van kans als de social media magnaten iets willen.
