## 901. Stand for your values, share them with everyone(!) and don't hide away in your own channel

Volt has decided to leave X.  
  
I am struggling immensely with this X decision...  
  
Initially: "Yes, boycott X!"  
  
It has become a bizarre platform and Facebook is going after it.....  
  
At the same time,  
  
a. do we really want everyone to retreat to their own platform to only hear what they want?  
  
b. who will offer a dissenting voice then? A different perspective on the matter for the millions who do stick around?  
  
c. MM's framing/observation now is that the left-wing elite really doesn't understand what is going on among ordinary citizens.. retreating to one's own platform confirms that image and makes understanding each other even harder (a bit like 'American conditions' with 2 opposing parties)  
  
d. we Volters, as true democrats, pride ourselves on freedom of speech. So why be critical of a platform that facilitates that?  
  
e. not fact-checking: is that bad? I think so, but/however..... who checks the fact-checker? State media agents? 'Independent' (unknown?) journalists/experts? Who then?  
  
So I am unsure what is better.  
  
In any case, even though my heart supports leaving X, my head tells me that this promotes polarization, reduces dissenting voices, and will widen the divides.  
  
Moreover, the reach of new Volt messages has SIGNIFICANTLY decreased (meaning fewer potential new members) and it focuses mainly on kindred spirits whom we no longer need to bring along towards our vision for the world anyway!

<u>Original title (nl)</u> : Sta voor je waarden, deel deze met iedereen(!) en duik niet weg in je eigen kanaal

<u>Original content (nl)</u> :

Volt heeft besloten om van X af te gaan.  
  
Ik worstel enorm met deze X beslissing...  
In eerste instantie: "Yes boycotten dat X!"  
Het is een bizar platform geworden en Facebook gaat er achter aan.....  
  
  
Tegelijkertijd,    
a. willen we echt dat iedereen zich terugtrekt op zijn eigen platform om alleen nog de gewenste dingen te horen?   
b. wie geeft er dan nog tegen geluid?  Een ander inzicht op de materie voor de miljoenen die wel blijven hangen?   
c. de framing/ observatie van MM is nu dat de linkse elite echt niet begrijpt wat er onder normale burgers speelt.. op een eigen platform terugtrekken bevestigd dat beeld en maakt elkaar begrijpen nog lastiger (beetje 'Amerikaanse toestanden' met 2 tegenovergestelde partijen)   
d. wij Volters, als echte democraten, gaan prat op vrijheid van meningsuiting. Dus waarom kritisch zijn op een platform die dat faciliteert?  
e. niet fact checken: is dat slecht? Ik vind van wel maar/ echter..... wie checkt de fact checker? Staatsmedia agenten?  'Onafhankelijke' (onbekende? ) journalisten/experts? Wie dan?    
Dus ik twijfel wat beter is.    
  
  
Hoe dan ook,  ook al sta ik in mijn hart achter het vertrek uit X, mijn hoofd zegt dat dit de polarisatie bevorderd, tegengeluid verminderd en de verschillen gaat vergroten.    
Bovendien is het bereik van nieuwe Volt  berichten SIGNIFICANT verkleind (dus minder potentiële nieuwe leden)  en richt het zich vnl op zielsgeliiken die we toch al niet meer hoeven mee te nemen richting onze visie voor de wereld!

## 908. Faith in care given

A friend of mine broke his finger, was helped in the hospital at the 1st aid and was send home with a cast.   
The staff requested him to get pictures made and double check with the specialist.  
A few weeks later, because everything takes a long time to arrange yourself, he had an appointment with a specialist who told him they should have operated immediately, because now he can't do anything anymore about the loss of motion in the finger.  
This is not an isolated incident, I also had a friend with torn achilles tendon and he was send home without help although he came in ambulance. That he had to come back following day to check how it was going, didn't really make sense that day, so he went to the hospital across the border on work insurance.  
I don't mind paying for healthcare, the most important thing is that you want to be sure you're taking care of in a moment that you can't manage the situation yourself.

## 914. We are in a Hybrid World War #HyWOWa

I am Italian live in Brussels and am a 2nd generation Eurocrat, being a eurofederalist for the last 45 years.  
My grandmother was a Polish aristocrat and she fell in love with my socialist grandfather when they met in the expat community in Paris - in the 1920s.  
She was born in what is now Bielorussia and I have cousins living in Poland and Lithuania.  
I have worked all my life to maintain peace in Europe, seeing the Commission where I work as "The institution which maintains ideals alive " (Jean Monnet, in his memoirs)  and was completely taken by surprise by Putin's aggression to Ukraine. On 24/2/24 I was in the heart of Europe, where I organised on Rond-Point Schuman, in front of the Berlaymont a demonstration with hundreds of Commission colleagues. The following day 20.000 Belgians demonstrated in Brussels.  
Three years later I am working to "widen the Overton window" so that Belgians first, EUropeans then understand and prepare for sending troop in Ukraine to defend the ceasefire that, I hope, will come soon. Joining VOlt Belgium ant taking its leadership as a member of the Board, is part of this "Experience", which is also a mission.

## 918. Europa first

Last week, I walked through Dubai for work and saw so much money and business activity in a country that doesn't care about the climate or the rights of low-paid workers. Trump had just started his tariff war, and I thought to myself: Our Western European welfare state is doomed unless we do something NOW. If the rest of the world promotes tax evasion and denies environmental damage, we as Europe must act to preserve our prosperity, otherwise we will perish. We must regulate less, innovate more, and invest more in companies and our armies. Let the environment take its course for a while if the rest of the world does the same. If the rest of the world isn't participating, we shouldn't destroy ourselves by placing too much emphasis on it.

## 919. The EU needs to better understand that the Netherlands cannot currently comply with all climate rules. The EU must impose fewer rules.

Dutch society has become hardened and uncertain over the last 20 years. Specifically for entrepreneurs, there are major and almost insurmountable challenges. The market is not the problem, because it does exist, certainly when looking at the EU. However, locally in the Netherlands, many factors are working against entrepreneurs: 1: the poor availability of space to expand; 2: the uncertain and currently negative position of the energy supply (network), which often makes expansion impossible; 3: the constantly changing government policy regarding the energy transition, which prevents entrepreneurs from daring to take action; 4: the incredibly large bureaucracy, despite the fact that many cabinets have been claiming for 20 years that they will reduce this pressure; 5: the fact that the Netherlands must adhere to the same emission and energy transition rules as the entire EU, knowing that our country is much more densely populated than any other country within the EU. As a result, many companies are unable to operate or can only do so with great difficulty. This situation has arisen primarily because the Netherlands, despite the endless EU regulatory zeal, has always wanted to serve as a role model. Entrepreneurs are suffering under this.

<u>Original content (nl)</u> :

De Nederlandse samenleving is de laatste 20 jaar verhard en onzeker geworden.  Specifiek voor ondernemers zijn er grote en bijna onhaalbare uitdagingen. Niet de markt is het probleem, want die is er wel, zeker als je naar de EU kijkt. Maar lokaal in Nederland spelen veel tegenwerkende zaken voor ondernemers  1: de slechte verkrijgbaarheid van ruimte om uit te breiden, 2: de onzekere en op dit moment negatieve positie van de energieleverantie ( netwerk) waardoor expansie vaak niet mogelijk is, 3: de steeds wisselende policy van de overheid als het gaat om de energietransitie waardoor ondernemers geen maatregelen durven te nemen 4: de ongelofelijk grote bureaucratie ondanks dat vele kabinetten al 20 jaar lang roepen dat men die druk gaat verminderen 5: Het feit dat Nederland zich aan de zelfde uitstoot- en energietransitieregels moet houden als heel de EU , wetend dat ons land veel drukker bevolkt is dan welk ander land binnen de EU.  Hierdoor kunnen veel bedrijven niet of heel moeilijk werken. De situatie is hoofdzakelijk ontstaan omdat Nederland ondanks de eindeloze EU regeldrift toch altijd een voorbeeldfunctie heeft willen bekleden.   Ondernemers lijden hieronder.

## 920. Why is it so difficult to tell the story of progressive politics

It's not an experience as such, but an obeservation. Throughout the world, and in Europe, we see a rise to power of right-wing populist parties. The opinions and views they represent often are extremist, anti-democratic, anti-environment and anti-inclusivity. But somehow these populist and anti-democratic voices are more easy heard, and accepted by, what seems to be, a growing number of people. And how come this is not being met with a strong response by the left wing, or more progressive and inclusive parties? Why does the idea take place that the sound of the future is dominated by the shouting of the right wing populist? I think that parties (like Volt) miss the translation of making their voice and message be heard and felt on the streets. We (as Volt memnber) need to maximise our effort to reacht the people in the street, and make our message clear and relevant to everyone. One of the key insights from a local right wing politician I read in the newspaper; is that this person is approachable, talks to the people in the streets, drives around in a car with his phone numer written on it, and he actually pick up the phone and listens! In order to win the vote, we need to break down the 'Europe for all' idealogy and make it super tangible and utterly relevant to the people in the local community. A collaborative Europe starts in your street, niot in Brussels.

## 921. Less "economies of scale" means more "social justice".

Having fled the city shortly after my retirement, I took refuge in a rural area. Six thousand liters of rainwater irrigate my toilets and my land when drought strikes. Photovoltaic panels stand proudly on the roofs.  
I let my small garden plots lie wild and reintroduce native plant species from my region. I buy my dairy products from a nearby farm. I have local produce delivered.  
Throughout my life, I've seen large retailers kill, step by step, local businesses, the kind that built community. Today, they're playing the victim card to consumers who are tired of their mantra: "economies of scale." They're starting to mimic the neighborhood grocery store they banished decades ago. It's a sham. Only one religion prevails: profit. Price has become the sole selling point, to the detriment of quality, sustainability, and health. Producers are being squeezed dry.  
  
I'm doing my part, but it seems insignificant compared to what needs to be done to return to a minimum of humanity and social cohesion.  
Europe must be united or risk being crushed. But it must be united around more regionally focused projects. Social cohesion moves mountains. The neoliberalism driving globalization is destroying the bond and the very essence of humanity.  
Volt interests me because of its cross-border aspect, and I also appreciate hearing that you have an approach that respects regional specificities.  
People who have lost their identity and see the far right as an escape route frighten me. To what level of deprivation of freedoms, of cultural mortification, are they capable of embracing it? The duty to remember is no longer enough. We must address all the human rights abuses that accompany dictatorships. The USA shows us the path not to follow... Have we failed? Are our children no longer being raised in the spirit of the Enlightenment? Is it the digital revolution that is destroying the very engine of our democracies: critical thinking?  
Is it possible to rediscover values ​​other than the sole pursuit of profit? Have we, to such an extent, forgotten that we are mortal and that the accumulation of goods is futile once we can house, feed, clothe, and heat ourselves?  
Can we still rely on the political world to halt climate change? Citizen mobilization seems more convincing today. If we can no longer influence decision-makers, we must act at the Achilles' heel: consumption, which fuels the power of those who acquire ever-increasing monopolies. We want to revitalize the economy? How can favoring large corporations and monopolies encourage entrepreneurship? Does creating startups prevent them from being sold off to large corporations that absorb them to become even more powerful?  
  
I grew up with the mantra: "The economy self-regulates thanks to the principle of supply and demand"... That's no longer really the case. If we let a company become a behemoth that takes up all the market share, where is the self-regulation? More SMEs competing with each other—isn't that what boosting the economy is all about?  
  


<u>Original title (fr)</u> : Moins d' "économie d'échelle", c'est plus de "justice sociale".

<u>Original content (fr)</u> :

Ayant fui la ville peu après ma retraite, je me suis réfugié dans un coin de campagne. 6000 litres d'eau de pluie irriguent mes chasses d'eau et mon terrain quand vient la sécheresse. Des panneaux photovoltaiques trônent sur les toits.   
Je laisse mes quelques ares de jardin en friche et y réintroduis des espèces végétales indigènes de ma région. J'achète mes produits laitiers à une ferme toute proche. Je me fais livrer des produits du terroir.   
J'ai vu au cours de ma vie les grands distributeurs tuer, pied à pied, le commerce local, celui qui faisait société. Aujourd'hui, ils jouent du violon aux oreilles des consommateurs qui sont fatigués de leur credo: "l'économie d'échelle". Ils se mettent à mimer l'épicerie de quartier qu'ils avaient bannie quelques décennies plus tôt. C'est un leurre. Une seule religion prévaut: le profit. Le prix est devenu l'unique argument de vente au détriment de la qualité, de la durabilité, de la santé. Les producteurs sont étranglés.  
Je fais ma part, mais ça me paraît infime à côté de ce qu'il y a à faire pour retourner à un minimum d'humanité et de lien social.  
L'Europe doit être unie sous peine de se faire écraser. Mais elle doit doit être unie autour de projets plus régionalisés. On déplace des montagnes avec de la cohésion sociale. Le néolibéralisme qui conduit la mondialisation détruit le lien et l'essence-même de l'humanité.  
Volt m'intéresse par l'aspect transfrontalier et j'aime aussi entendre que vous avez une approche qui respecte les spécificités régionales.   
Les gens en perte d'identité qui voient en l'extrême-droite une porte de sortie m'effraient. A quel niveau de privation de libertés, de mortifications de la culture  sont-ils capables d'adhérer? Le devoir de mémoire ne suffit plus. Il faut relever toutes les atteintes aux droits de l'homme qui vont avec les dictatures. Les USA nous montrent la voie à ne pas suivre... Avons-nous failli? Nos enfants ne sont-ils plus élevés dans l'esprit des lumières? Est-ce le ras-de-marée digital qui est en train de détruire le moteur-même de nos démocraties: l'analyse contradictoire?   
Est-il possible de retrouver d'autres valeurs que la seule recherche de profit? Avons-nous, à ce point, oublié que nous sommes mortels et que l'accumulation de biens est vaine dès lors que nous pouvons nous loger, nous nourrir, nous vêtir, nous chauffer.  
Peut-on encore compter sur le monde politique pour enrayer le dérèglement climatique? La mobilisation citoyenne semble aujourd’hui plus convaincante. Si on ne peut plus influencer les décideurs, il faut agir au niveau du tendon d'Achille: la consommation qui nourrit la puissance de ceux qui acquièrent de plus en plus de monopoles. On veut dynamiser une économie? En quoi favoriser les grosses entreprises et les monopoles peut-il encourager à entreprendre? Créer des start-up empêche-t-il qu'elles finissent revendues à des gros groupes qui les phagocytent pour devenir toujours plus puissants?  
J'ai grandi avec le mantra: "l'économie s'autorégule grâce au principe de l'offre et de la demande"... Ce n'est plus trop d'actualité. Si on laisse une entreprise devenir un mastodonte qui prend toutes les parts de marché, où est l'autorégulation. Plus de PME qui se concurrencent, n'est-ce pas cela, dynamiser l'économie?

## 922. Star Wars in the polder (and beyond)

I joined Volt after the Dutch elections because I was angry and disturbed. Since the American elections and the results thereof, I have been even angrier and more disturbed, and I will not be the only one. An acute need has arisen for very concrete ideas, an action plan, for what to do to erect a dam against fascism. I am adjusting my consumption habits accordingly. No more Twitter and Facebook (Meta has to go completely, but getting rid of WhatsApp isn't that simple, work-wise, etc.), and no more Amazon, and I have to de-Google (also not that simple, work-wise, etc.). Besides the difficulties involved in erecting a dam against fascism due to the (almost traditional) internal divisions of everything to the left of Attila the Hun, it is further complicated by the fact that we are increasingly failing to maintain a shared reality. I have a cousin in America, a born-again Christian, who lives not only in another country, on another continent, but in a completely different, parallel universe. That is where things are heading in the Netherlands too. And before I start blaming De Telegraaf, Voetbal Inside, and voters for far-right parties for that, I would actually like to know from you what a strategy might be to counter this. To regain momentum.  
  
NB: Actually, I am looking for a map of the Death Star with an X on it indicating its weak spot(s) -;)

<u>Original title (nl)</u> : Star Wars in de polder (en daarbuiten)

<u>Original content (nl)</u> :

Ik ben na de Nederlandse verkiezingen lid geworden van Volt omdat ik kwaad was en verontrust. Ik ben sinds de Amerikaanse verkiezingen, de uitslag daarvan, nog kwader en nog verontruster en ik zal de enige niet zijn. Er is een acute behoefte ontstaan aan hele concrete ideeen, een actieplan, wat te doen om een dam op te werpen tegen fascisme. Ik ben mijn consumptiegedrag erop aan het aanpassen. Geen Twitter en Facebook meer (Meta moet helemaal de deur uit maar van WhatsApp afkomen is nog niet zo eenvoudig, qua werk etc.), en geen Amazon meer en ik moet de-Googlen (ook nog niet zo eenvoudig, want qua werk etc.). Naast de moeilijkheden die het opwerpen van een dam tegen fascisme ondervindt door de (bijna traditionele) onderlinge verdeeldheid van alles wat er zich ter linkerzijde van Atilla de Hun bevindt, wordt het extra bemoeilijkt door het feit dat we er steeds minder een gedeelde realiteit op nahouden. Ik heb een nicht in Amerika, een born again Christian, die niet alleen in een ander land, op ander continent, maar in een volstrekt ander, parallel, universum woont. Daar gaat het in NL ook naartoe. En voordat ik daar de De Telegraaf, Voetbal Inside en de kiezers op extreem-rechtse partijen de schuld van ga geven, zou ik eigenlijk van jullie willen weten wat een strategie kan zijn om dit tegen te gaan. Om momentum terug te pakken.  
  
NB: Eigenlijk ben ik op zoek naar een kaart van de Death Star met daarop een X die de zwakke plek(ken) ervan aangeeft -;)

## 923. What do you do if someone on the street asks you for money?

I was at Rotterdam station recently when I was approached by a man in his mid-twenties. He needed money to renew his ID, as it had broken. He told me that he was under guardianship and therefore couldn't afford it. He was very friendly. I found the story a bit strange and asked some follow-up questions (but I don't remember the exact details). I then decided to give him the loose change I happened to have with me, but not the 20-euro note; I thought that was too much. In hindsight, I wonder if it was a nonsense story and I gave him 'too much' money, or if I should have given him the 20-euro note instead.

<u>Original title (nl)</u> : Wat doe je als iemand op straat je om geld vraagt?

<u>Original content (nl)</u> :

Ik was laatst op het station van Rotterdam en toen werd ik aangesproken door een man van halverwege de 20. Hij had geld nodig om zijn identiteitsbewijs te vernieuwen. Deze was stuk gegaan. Hij vertelde dat hij onder bewind stond en dit daarom niet kon betalen. Hij was heel vriendelijk. Ik vond het een beetje vreemd verhaal en heb wat doorgevraagd (maar weet de details niet meer precies). Toen heb ik ervoor gekozen om hem het losse geld te geven dat ik toevallig bij me had, maar niet het briefje van 20, dat vond ik teveel. Achteraf vraag ik me af, was het een onzin-verhaal en heb ik hem 'teveel' geld gegeven of had ik hem juist het briefje van 20 moeten geven.

## 924. Neighbour's grass

Years ago, I regularly traveled by train without assistance (in a wheelchair), and back then the Netherlands was still a nightmare, with Italy and Spain leading the way. Now things are better throughout Europe, but high-speed travel, ICE, TGV, etc., really needs to happen, with dedicated compartments and toilets for wheelchair users or people with disabilities in general, just like on the Shinkansen.  
  
Having lived with my disability for a long time, I suffered a brain hemorrhage in Croatia, where I was living at the time. Although no one ever thought so, the treatment there was amazing, truly top-notch. But I heard later that this would never have worked so well for the Croatians back then. Mind you, I was still a Dutch resident. There needs to be one travel and health insurance scheme for ALL OF Europe; there should be no difference regarding health, unlike in the US and its states.  
  
Because I know the Balkans very well, I have met many people there over the past 10 years. But as early as 1999, oh my first trip, I already heard from taxi drivers that they expected to fall under the Russian yoke again someday, and 10 years later they still thought that, even with NATO membership. Crimea, Donbas, they saw it coming. We, as the other EU countries, need to listen much more to the East; they know "the Russian" through and through.  
  
I once became a Volt member precisely for the reasons mentioned above. If we are safe, the economy is safe too; that is why more EU regulations need to be harmonized to make a stand against China and the US. We must eventually be able to function without the US within NATO as well; that is why I am a member.

<u>Original title (nl)</u> : Neighbour's grass

<u>Original content (nl)</u> :

Jaren geleden reisde ik geregeld per trein zonder assistentie, (rolstoel) en toen was NL nog een drama en Italië en Spanje stonden voorop, nu gaat het beter door heel Europa, maar HSL reizen, ICE, TGV etc. moet er echt komen, met net als in de Shinkansen eigen coupés en toiletten voor rolstoelgebruikers of mensen met beperking in het algemeen.  
  
Met al lange tijd met mijn beperking, kreeg ik een hersenbloeding in Kroatië waar ik toen woonde. Hoewel men dit nooit dacht was de behandeling daar geweldig, echt top. Maar hoorde ik later, voor de Kroaten had dit toen nooit zo goed gewerkt. Let wel, ik was nog steeds NL ingezetene. Er moet één reis en ziektekostenverzekering komen voor HÉÉL Europa, er mag op vlak van gezondheid geen verschil zijn zoals in de VS en haar staten.  
  
Omdat ik de Balkan zeer goed ken, veel mensen leren kennen in 10 jaar aldaar. Maar al in 19999, o mijn eerste trip, hoorde ik al van taxichauffeurs dat zij verwachtten ooit weer on Russisch juk te komen, en 10 jaar later dachten ze dat nog steeds ook met NATO lidmaatschap. Krim, Donbas, zij zagen het aankomen. Wij als overige EU landen moeten veel meer naar het Oosten luisteren, zij kennen "de Rus" door en door.   
  
Ooit werd ik Volt lid juist om de bovenstaande zaken. Als we veilig zijn is de economie dat ook, daarom moet er meer EU regelgeving gelijk getrokken worden om een vuist tegen China en VS te maken. We moeten binnen Nato ook zonder VS kunnen uiteindelijk, daarom ben ik lid.

## 926. Give EU citizens their full democratic rights when settling in another EU country.

As an EU citizen with Dutch citizenship, I have been working and living in Sweden since the autumn of 1979. During all these years, I have, together with my Dutch wife, paid my taxes and participated in Swedish society. Every 3 years I have been able to vote in municipal and county council/regional elections but ...... never in the parliamentary elections! I consider this to be a major shortcoming in today's EU, which, among other things, gives us EU citizens the right to reside and work in another EU country. When we moved, we were therefore unable to bring our democratic rights and thus were unable to elect politicians who could present our case in the political body that decides, among other things, how our tax money is used. As an EU citizen, you should not have to become (in our case) a Swedish citizen and thereby (in our case) renounce your Dutch citizenship in order to fully participate in all democratic elections in the EU country where you live, work and pay taxes.  
  


<u>Original title (sv)</u> : Ge EU medborgare sina fulla demokratiska rättigheter vid bosättning i annan EU land.

<u>Original content (sv)</u> :

Som EU medborgare med nederländskt medborgarskap har jag sedan hösten 1979 arbete och varit bosatt i Sverige. Under alla dessa år har jag, tillsammans med min nederländska fru, betalat mina skatter och deltagit i det svenska samhällslivet. Var 3e år har jag kunnat rösta i kommun resp landsting/regionval men ...... aldrig i riksdagsvalet ! Jag anser detta vara en stor brist i dagens EU som bl a ges oss EUR medborgare rätt till att vistas och arbeta i ett annat EU land. När vi flyttade har vi alltså inte kunnat ta med våra demokratiska rättigheter och därmed inte kunnat välja politiker som skulle kunna föra vår talan i den politiska instans som bestämmer över bla hur våra skattepengar används. Man skall som EU medborgare inte behöva bli (i vårt fall) svensk medborgare och därmed (i vårt fall) avsäga sitt nederländska medborgarskap för att fullt ut kunna delta i alla demokratiska val i det EU land där man bor, arbetar och betalar skatt.

## 931. The financial and human dimension of a care situation against the backdrop of the current federal election campaign

I care for my 85-year-old father. He lives in a nursing home and has dementia. He doesn't remember events that happened more than five minutes ago. He's a difficult case because he refuses to communicate with caregivers and other residents. Most of the caregivers are not of German origin, but they do their jobs very well. They are friendly and kind.  
  
What must the foreign caregivers think when they hear about the current political debate on immigration and migration? The CDU/CSU is deliberately conducting it in a very one-sided manner. This power-hungry and inhumane style of politics infuriates me.  
  
And then there are the nursing home costs. They've almost doubled in the last four years to €4,800. I don't understand it; wages haven't doubled. Given this, I find the CDU's approach incredibly stupid!

<u>Original title (de)</u> : Die finanzielle und menschliche Dimension eines Pflegefalls vor dem Hintergrund der aktuellen Bundestagswahlkampfes

<u>Original content (de)</u> :

Ich betreue meinen 85 jährigen Vater. Er lebt im Pflegeheim und ist dement. Ereignisse, die länger als 5 Minuten vergangen sind weis er nicht mehr. Er ist ein schwieriger Fall, weil er die Kommunikation mit Pflegekräften und Heimbewohnern ablehnt  Die Pflegekräfte sind zum großen Teil nicht deutscher Herkunft, sie machen Ihren Job sehr gut. Sie sind freundlich und nett.   
  
Was denken wohl die ausländischen Pflegekräfte, wenn sie die aktuelle politische Diskussion zum Thema Einwanderung und Migration mitbekommen? Von der Union wird sie absichtlich sehr einseitig geführt. Mich nervt dieser machtgeile und menschenverachtende Politikstil.  
  
Und dann sind da noch die Pflegeheimkosten. Sie haben sich in den letzten vier Jahren fast verdoppelt auf 4800 Euro. Ich verstehe das nicht, die Löhne haben sich nicht verdoppelt. Vor diesem Hintergrund finde ich die Vorgehensweise der CDU saudumm!

## 933. Outside the bubble

A conversation with a sewer cleaner, a nice young man (30) who has been here before. A brief conversation developed about house prices and scarcity, and from there it moved on to more general political topics. We ended up discussing agriculture and livestock farming, and he said, "but yes, a farm is basically just nature." To which I replied that that might have been true in the beginning, but it hasn't been for a long time now due to scaling up, artificial fertilizer, artificially optimized animal feed, manure emissions, and of course nitrogen (which has caused, among other things, the housing shortage to increase due to a problem with permit issuance). "That is actually true," he said, just before getting back into his van.  
  
I thought: a lot of explanation is needed for people who do not have the right understanding of various matters in society. Now their voice is determined by poor information, often not by unwillingness.

<u>Original title (nl)</u> : Buiten de bubbel

<u>Original content (nl)</u> :

Een gesprek met een rioolontstopper, een aardige jonge man (30) die al eerder is geweest. Er ontstond een gesprekje over huizenprijzen, schaarste en vandaar ging het naar algemenere politieke onderwerpen. We belandden bij landbouw en veeteelt, en hij zei "maar ja, een boerderij is in feite gewoon natuur". Waarna ik zei dat dat in de oorsprong wellicht waar is geweest maar nu allang niet vanwege schaalvergroting, kunstmest, kunstmatig geoptimaliseerd veevoer, mestuitstoot en natuurlijk stikstof (waardoor oa de woningnood toe is genomen vanwege een probleem met vergunningverlening). "Dat is ook wel weer waar" zei hij, vlak voor dat hij weer in zijn busje stapte.   
Ik dacht: er is heel veel uitleg nodig aan mensen die niet het juiste beeld hebben bij allerlei zaken in de samenleving. Nu wordt hun stem bepaald door slechte informatie, vaak niet door onwil.

## 940. Cultural segregation in the Netherlands

I recently attended a concert by Ahmed Aslan, a Turkish/Kurdish singer, in Amsterdam. I was approached by a Turkish boy who was surprised to see me (a white Dutchman) there. When I mentioned that I was traveling to Istanbul soon, he thought he had the solution: "Your wife must be Turkish!" I had to disappoint him. The venue was indeed filled mostly with people of Turkish/Kurdish descent, softly humming along to Alsan's melancholic songs. Through this experience, I realized just how incredibly culturally segregated our (Dutch) society actually is. We live in one country with people from many different cultures, yet we do nothing to get to know each other. Like 'ships that pass in the night'. Europe is an immigration continent. And that is fine. But we really need to do much more to get along well with one another.

<u>Original title (nl)</u> : Culturele segregatie in Nederland

<u>Original content (nl)</u> :

Ik was pas bij een concert van Ahmed Aslan, een Turks/Koerdische zanger in Amsterdam. Ik werd aangesproken door een Turkse jongen die verbaasd was mij (een witte Nederlander) hier te zien. Toen ik zei binnenkort naar Istanbul te reizen dacht hij de oplossing te hebben: Je vrouw is zeker Turks! Ik moest hem teleurstellen. De zaal was inderdaad vooral gevuld met mensen van Turks/Koerdische komaf, die zachtjes meeneurieden met de melancholieke liedjes van Alsan. Door deze ervaring realiseerde ik mij hoe ongelofelijk cultureel gesegregeerd onze (Nederlandse) samenleving eigenlijk is. We leven in één land met mensen uit vele verschillende culturen, maar doen eigenlijk niets om elkaar te leren kennen. Als 'ships that pass in the night'. Europa is een immigratie continent. En dat is prima. Maar we zullen echt veel meer moeten doen om het gezellig met elkaar te hebben.

## 943. Local patriotism is insurmountable.

Some time ago, I became aware of an illegal landfill in a somewhat remote location near my home (southern Greece). It was clearly professionally constructed, with a specially constructed concrete loading ramp. A friend and I tried to get some information from the local council. We were met with a wall of silence: "We know nothing about it." An article in the newspaper only prompted comments along the lines of: What's that foreigner doing here? Even a complaint to the EU in Brussels was fruitless: "We've asked the relevant authorities to take care of it..." There were no attempts from any side to remove these hundreds of tons of garbage, which also threaten a beach during heavy rain. "No money."  
  
Then there was another citizens' initiative: a protest against a planned wind farm in the mountains. In a nature reserve (where, incidentally, the landfill is also located). Suddenly, a petition against it garnered thousands of signatures to prevent the "destruction of the environment."  
  
My conclusion: When it comes to something where someone in the local area might be financially affected... Then everyone falls silent. If someone from the outside comes along who wants to push through a profitable project here, then everyone is loudly opposed.

<u>Original title (de)</u> : Lokalpatriotismus ist unüberwindbar

<u>Original content (de)</u> :

Vor einiger Zeit bin ich auf eine wilde, also illegale Mülldeponie  in etwas abgelegener Lage in meiner Umgebung (Süd Griechenland) aufmerksam geworden. Sie wurde ganz klar professionell angelegt, mit extra betonnierter Laderampe. Mit einem Freund habe ich versucht, von der Gemeinde Aufklärung darüber zu bekommen. Eine Wand des Schweigens: "Wir wissen darüber nichts". Ein Artikel in der Zeitung führte nur zu Kommentaren  nach dem Tenor: Was will der Ausländer hier? Auch eine Beschwerde bei der EU in Brüssel brachte nichts: "Wir haben die zuständigen Behörden gebeten, sich darum zu kümmern..."Es gab von keiner Seite Versuche, diese hunderte Tonnen Müll, die zudem bei Starkregen einen Strand bedrohen, zu beseitigen. "Kein Geld".  
Dann gab es eine andere Bürgeraktion: Protest gegen eine geplante Windfarm in den Bergen. In einem Naturschutzgebiet (in dem übrigens auch die Mülldeponie gelegen ist) Plötzlich konnte eine Unterschriftensammlung tausende Unterschriften dagegen bekommen, um die "Zerstörung der Umwelt" zu verhindern.  
Fazit für mich: Wenn es um etwas geht, bei dem jemand vor Ort womöglich finanziell betroffen sein könnte. dann schweigen alle. Wenn von außen jemand kommt, der hier ein profitables Projekt durchziehen möchte, dannsind alle lautstark dagegen.

## 949. 1 billion trees???? Please no!

A concern that has been troubling me ever since I read VOLT's platform for the federal elections. As a conservationist, I am appalled. A mere "tree number target" is no guarantee of ecological benefit – and, formulated so undifferentiatedly as it is here, can lead to immense environmental damage if extensively managed areas, such as dry grasslands and extensive habitats, are to be reforested. Instead of blindly planting large quantities, an integrated approach with renaturation, protection of existing ecosystems, and sustainable land use would be far more sensible. This point might sound great to laypeople, but it's very poorly thought out. I still support VOLT, but they really need to take this further.

<u>Original title (de)</u> : 1 Millarde Bäume???? Bitte nicht

<u>Original content (de)</u> :

Eine Sorge, die mich umtreibt, seit ich das Programm von VOLT für die Bundestagswahl gelesen habe. Als Naturschützer bin ich jetzt entsetzt. Ein reines "Baumzahl-Ziel" ist kein Garant für ökologischen Nutzen – kann, so undifferenziert, wie es hier formuliert ist, größte Naturschäden nach sich ziehen, wenn extensiv bewirtschafte Flächen, wie Magerrasen, extensive Habitate aufgeforstet werden sollen. Statt blind große Mengen zu pflanzen, wäre ein integrierter Ansatz mit Renaturierung, Schutz bestehender Ökosysteme und nachhaltiger Landnutzung deutlich sinnvoller. Dieser Punkt klingt für Laien vielleicht großartig, aber das ist sehr wenig durchdacht. ich bin immer noch auf der Seite von VOLT, aber hier muss echt nachgelegt werden.

## 951. The Netherlands is not full, but it is overbooked. You cannot admit students, expats, and economic refugees if you do not have decent housing for them.

My fifteen-year-old daughter was harassed during her first running training session in a wood behind the house. The wood is located next to Duinrel, where refugees are forced to stay for too long because there are no homes for them. Upon inquiry, it turned out that the girls are better off not using that wood.  
  
We, a single-parent family, receive one or two anonymous threatening letters every year. For example: ‘You pathetic single woman, if you want help with suicide, contact me.’  
  
In my son’s room, one housemate said to the other, ‘I am going to kill you in your sleep.’  
  
In short, we no longer feel so safe.

<u>Original title (nl)</u> : Nederland is niet vol, maar wel overbooked. Je kunt geen studenten, expats, en economische vluchtelingen toelaten als je geen fatsoenlijke woningen voor ze hebt.

<u>Original content (nl)</u> :

Mijn vijftienjarige dochter op haar eerste hardlooptraining in een bos achter het huis lastig gevallen. Het bos ligt naast Duinrel, waar vluchtelingen te lang moeten verblijven omdat er geen woningen voor ze zijn. Bij navraag is bekend gebleken dat de meiden beter geen gebruik van dat bos kunnen maken.   
We, eenouder gezin, krijgen iedere jaar wel één of twee anonieme dreigbrieven. Bijvoorbeeld: ‘jij zielige single vrouw, als je hulp wilt bij zelfdoding, neem dan contact met mij op’.  
Bij mijn zoon op kamer zei de ene huisgenoot tegen de andere ‘I am going to kill you in your sleep’.  
Kortom, we voelen ons niet meer zo veilig.

## 952. Polarization at the checkout

Here is a rephrasing of the text in proper Dutch:  
  
At the checkout, a young woman asked an older lady if she could keep her dog close to her so that he could not sniff her. The dachshund was busy inspecting the younger woman's shoes.  
  
After a brief conversation about the reason for the request and the older woman's remark that "my dog ​​is clean; he even sleeps in my bed," she started a sentence with "you." Unfortunately, I can no longer remember the rest of that sentence. I asked the older woman what exactly she meant by "you." The younger woman was wearing a long, chic coat and a headscarf.  
  
The younger woman thanked me and asked if her request to keep the dog at a distance was wrong. I replied that this was not the case. Afterward, she left the store, while the older woman grumbled as she paid for her purchases and walked away.  
  
I walked away too, but now regret not having taken a clearer stance on the use of "you," as if "we" were superior.  
  


<u>Original title (nl)</u> : Polarisatie aan de kassa

<u>Original content (nl)</u> :

Bij de kassa vroeg een jonge vrouw aan een oudere dame of ze haar hond bij zich kon houden, zodat hij niet aan haar kon snuffelen. De teckel was druk bezig met het inspecteren van de schoenen van de jongere vrouw.  
  
Na een kort gesprek over de reden van het verzoek en de opmerking van de oudere vrouw dat "mijn hond is schoon; hij slaapt zelfs in mijn bed," begon ze een zin met "jullie." Helaas kan ik me de rest van die zin niet meer herinneren. Ik vroeg de oudere vrouw wat ze precies met "jullie" bedoelde. De jongere vrouw droeg een lange chique jas en had een hoofddoek op.  
  
De jongere vrouw bedankte me en vroeg of haar verzoek om de hond op afstand te houden verkeerd was. Ik antwoordde dat dit niet het geval was. Daarna verliet ze de winkel, terwijl de oudere vrouw mopperend haar aankopen betaalde en wegging.  
  
Ik liep ook weg, maar heb nu spijt dat ik niet duidelijker stelling had genomen over het gebruik van "jullie," alsof "we" superieur zouden zijn.

## 955. Policies and communication responding to real life problems

End last year, local elections where I live and the big fear was that the flemish ultra right wing party would win up to 30% of the votes. A scary outlook.  
  
I discussed with many people, those that are political active, or simply aware, and those of the large majority who have real world daily problems that they describe quite bluntly.  
  
It struck me that none of the classic parties cater for that majority, they play only for their own small constituenty except for that ultra right wing party, that manages to speak the language of the people and talk about daily problems (a real drug problem in the streets of our small town, a huge crime raise... ) and about the measures they would take to... behave like Trump   
  
It is very difficult to convince a member of the majority whose 18 year old daughter is harassed on the street by "immigrants" that the ultra right is not the answer, certainly while normal parties are deaf and blind for his fear and anger, even refuse to mention it or listen to him...  
  
Please don't make that mistake. address the real problems, also and certainly when these are inconvenient.

## 956. More inclusive schooling

My daughter has developmental delays in cognitive and physical abilities due to a congenital brain malformation. She is currently in the first grade of a mainstream school. There, she is one of many children with special educational needs. In our view, this inclusive schooling is the best solution for our daughter, as it gives her the opportunity to reach her full potential, which is always difficult to assess in children with special educational needs (especially those with intellectual disabilities). Many children with intellectual disabilities therefore attend special education centers and are taught separately from typically developing children. This means that some of the potential of these children is never developed and they remain consistently unchallenged, which reduces their future prospects. Furthermore, it reinforces the German practice of placing a disproportionately high number of children in special schools.  
  
In our daughter's case, however, getting her into our preferred school was a major challenge, as various agencies influence the school placement process: the school board, the youth welfare office, the schools themselves, and potentially special education centers or assessment agencies, etc. As always, it ultimately comes down to suitability and availability. Unfortunately, this is where the real problem lies: too few schools have the necessary staffing, infrastructure, and experience to accommodate students with special needs. Demand far exceeds supply. I advocate for more special education teacher positions in schools, along with more teaching assistants. I also believe schools should have easier access to implement or commission measures to create barrier-free access (see building regulations).

<u>Original title (de)</u> : Mehr inklusive Beschulung

<u>Original content (de)</u> :

Meine Tochter ist aufgrund einer angeborenen Hirnfehlbildung entwicklungsverzögert in Bezug auf kognitive und physische Leistungsfähigkeit. Sie geht aktuell in die 1. Klasse einer Regelschule. Dort ist sie eines von zahlreichen Kindern mit Förderschwerpunkt. Diese inklusive Beschulung ist aus unserer Sicht für unsere Tochter die beste Lösung, da sie ihr die Möglichkeit gibt, ihr volle Potenzial auszuschöpfen, was bei Kindern mit Förderschwerpunkt (besonders bei „GE“-Kindern = geistige Entwicklung) immer schwer zu ermitteln ist. Viele GE Kinder gehen daher in ein Förderzentrum und werden getrennt von gesunden Kindern beschult. Das sorgt zum einen dafür, dass manche Potentiale betroffener Kinder niemals gefördert werden und sie stets unterfordert bleiben, was ihre Zukunftschancen mindert. Zum Anderen verfestigt es die deutsche Praxis, überdurchschnittlich viele Kinder in Sonderschulen zu betreuen.   
Im Falle unserer Tochter war der Weg jedoch in unsere Wunschschule eine große Herausforderung, da es verschiedene Stellen gibt, die die Schulplatzvergabe mit beeinflussen: Schulamt, Jugendamt, Schulen, ggf. SPZs bzw. begutachtende Stellen usw.   
Wie immer kommt es am Ende auf Geeignetheit und Verfügbarkeit an. Hier liegt leider das eigentliche Problem: zu wenige Schulen haben entsprechende personelle und infrastrukturelle Ausstattungen sowie die notwendige Erfahrung Schülerinnen und Schüler aufzunehmen. Hier ist aber die Nachfrage viel größer als das Angebot. Mein Plädoyer für mehr Stellen für Sonderpädagoginnen/-Pädagogen in den Schulen in Verbindung mit mehr Schulhelfern. Auch einfachere Möglichkeiten für Schulen, Maßnahmen zur Schaffung von Barrierefreiheit durchzuführen bzw. zu beauftragen (siehe Bauordnung).

## 960. Housing crisis

Within the family there are a couple of nephews in their twenties who are having and extremely hard time finding somewhere to live. They have literally been looking and waiting for years to find something. One has recently found a small studio to rent for around 1000 euros per month!! The other has just been able to buy a house with his partner. This house was built in the 1970's and is nothing special and not in any of the big cities, but cost them around 450.000 euros. To be so young and have such a high mortgage to start seems so unreasonable. This not only the story of my family, but is the case for most young people in the Netherlands. There is not enough reasonably priced accommodation to go around. This is the basis of a lot of resentment that results in certain political choices (read right wing populism).

## 962. Boulonnais: Autonomous within EU and France.

I haven’t a recent experience of me in our society, unless personal ideas development, retractions from politics due to lack of will and power concentration from elected officers, far right French MP and many people in the Boulogne-sur-Mer area. Being candidate for Regional in 2021 wasn’t easy at all, facing how citizens were pretty disgusted. Too many critics or pretexts about our community places for poor results from them. Boulogne, a town dead. That’s all they’re able to say without reconsider our potential and open their minds to the world we are building.  
  
Boulogne-sur-Mer area is underrated, concentrated to fish industry and Nausicaá whilst it has the potential to be a better and powerful place between London and Brussels.  The town and its areas suffered from wars, the French State and local officers have no will to make it richer and rethink its attractiveness. I’m really concerned about the place I live as personal and as visitor. When I travel elsewhere in Europe and the UK, It feels like you’ve find your way back to the world of civilization after being lost in the forest.   
  
Since always, Europe makes sense for a lot of things and although the National Rally (Antoine Golliot and Christine Engrand) won Boulonnais constituencies in 2024, Europe is important for the prosperity and the well-being of the Boulonnais people.   
  
Under the French centralism rule, our territory cannot express itself with its lack of emancipation because it’s considered as a territory in the North of Paris rather than in the heart of Europe.  
  
To make our territory “Great Again” in a better way than our lil’bro USA, it needs to be more autonomous, sharing a special status within France and the EU at the same time, based on examples such as Åland, an associated-state with Finland. The main idea is to make the Boulonnais an European Laboratory for experiencing both EU and French public policies, close to the UK Post-Brexit.   
  
Thanks to the Autonomy, and the ability to have a wide and full competencies, with legislative bodies, we’ll be able to help our people and inspire others that EU works by having power to legislate, handle refugees crisis with more humanity, responds to floods, diversifying our economies through AI or decarbonization researches and develop Free trade zone to enhance our bound with Britain and Benelux, better transportation system with our neigbors, recognize Boulonnais/Picard , Dutch, English and French at the same level and not only French as sole language and Boulonnais/Picard as wrong French... Why not having an extended welfare system and more democracy, flex security inspired by other european countries.  
  
That idea came a long time ago with aim to make Boulogne and the Boulonnais a better place to live in the 21st century, respond to crisis with neighbors, EU and State and set one step further to the foundation of the United States of Europe and perhaps, the Boulonnais will not become member, but just European State.

## 967. Connectivity through Europe

## 977. recycling ?

Returning home, I was once again struck by the filth: for the past few years, garbage containers (yellow bins or otherwise) have been brought out of the basements onto the access road behind the buildings, waiting for the trucks to come. Roma people come and rummage through their contents, taking various items. But everything that falls from the containers isn't collected and is blown away by the wind, littering the fences, the base and branches of some trees, the path, and the gutter. This dispersal is deteriorating the entire area and transforming the green spaces into...a dirty neighborhood?

## 984. Desertification

I went to the post office, just five minutes from my house, to mail a letter, only to find it was closed. So, I had to travel two kilometers round trip to mail it.  
I can only imagine how difficult this must be for elderly people or those with mobility issues, and that's not even mentioning rural areas where people sometimes have to travel over 20 kilometers. It's a shame there isn't an intermediate solution (like an ATM, for example, for simple needs such as sending a letter).

<u>Original title (fr)</u> : Désertification

<u>Original content (fr)</u> :

Parti pour poster un courrier au bureau de poste à 5 minutes du domicile, je me suis aperçu qu'il avait été fermé. Du coup 2 kilomètres A/R à faire pour aller poster mon courrier.   
J'imagine ce que ce doit être pour des personnes âgées ou ayant des difficultés à se déplacer et on ne parle pas en région où l'on doit faire parfois plus de 20 kilomètres. Dommage qu’il n’y ait pas de solution intermédiaire (guichet automatique par exemple, pour des besoins simples, comme l’envoi d’une simple lettre).

## 986. For the people by the people

Yesterday, I attended a book presentation at a welcoming meeting place in Huizen. The evening was organized by a lady associated with the meeting place. Some time ago, she received help from the author in overcoming a fear of dogs. When it turned out that this gentleman had written a nice book about dogs and their owners, she decided to organize an evening where the person in question would be interviewed, people could ask questions, and possibly buy the book.  
  
Characteristic of the event was the "coziness" (in a positive sense). Chairs scattered haphazardly. A sound system that wasn't quite properly adjusted. Coffee/tea for a euro, served from pitchers into all sorts of different cups.  
  
Unlike a super-commercial evening organized by a publisher with the goal of selling as many books as possible, I can genuinely enjoy these kinds of authentic moments where connection is the main focus (from which the purchase of the book then flows).

<u>Original title (nl)</u> : For the people by the people

<u>Original content (nl)</u> :

Gister was ik aanwezig bij een boekpresentatie in een gastvrije ontmoetingsplek in Huizen. De avond was georganiseerd door een dame die verbonden is aan de ontmoetingsplek. Zij heeft enige tijd geleden hulp gehad van de auteur bij het overwinnen van een angst voor honden. Toen bleek dat deze meneer een leuk boek geschreven had over honden en baasjes besloot zij een avond te organiseren waarbij de bewuste persoon geïnterviewd zou worden, mensen vragen konden stellen en eventueel het boek konden kopen.   
  
Kenmerkend was de "kneuterigheid" (in positieve zin). Stoelen die kraskras door elkaar stonden. Een geluidsinstallatie die niet helemaal goed stond afgesteld. koffie/thee voor een euro, geschonken uit kannen in allerlei verschillende kopjes.   
  
In tegenstelling tot een super commerciële avond die georganiseerd wordt door een uitgever met als doel zoveel mogelijk boeken te verkopen, kan ik oprecht geniet van dit soort authentieke momenten waarbij de verbinding vooral centraal staat (waaruit het kopen van het boek dan voortvloeit).

## 992. Inequality of opportunity begins in primary school

I conducted a study, somewhat by chance, of nearly 1,800 primary school teachers in France, and the results are appalling. 98.6% of them have to pay out of pocket to equip their classrooms with teaching resources. The Ministry spends €7,000 per student, but we can't seem to find the €30-35 per student per year needed to address this. The Ministry and the regional education authorities remain passive and pass the buck to the local municipalities. The municipalities are not adequately fulfilling their legal obligation to cover the operating costs of schools. This is completely unfair to the children, and we're just standing by and watching the world go by. Too bad for the kids, and too bad for equal opportunity.

<u>Original title (fr)</u> : l'inégalité des chances commence au primaire

<u>Original content (fr)</u> :

J'ai mené un peu par hasard une étude auprès de presque 1800 enseignants de primaire en France et les résultats sont déplorables. Ils sont 98,6% à devoir dépenser de leur poche pour équiper leur classe en ressources pédagogiques. Le ministère dépense 7000€ par élève, mais on est infoutus de trouver les 30/35€ par élève et par an qu'il faudrait pour remédier à cela. Le ministère et les académies restent passives et se défaussent sur les communes. Les communes ne remplissent pas suffisamment leur obligation légale de subvenir aux dépenses de fonctionnement des écoles. C'est complètement inégalitaire pour les enfants et on se contente de regarder les trains passer. Tant pis pour les gosses et tant pis pour l'égalité des chances.

<u>Question</u> : Given the successive PISA and TIMSS studies that show the decline in French academic standards over the years, at what point do we decide we need to solve the problem? (Not just take ineffective action to say, "I did something and spent money," but actually solve the problem.)

## 994. Democracy is not a right you have, you have to earn it, you have to fight for it!

I was active within Volt for over three years, starting in 2020, but I stopped in 2024. Not because I no longer believe in or stand for what Volt is built upon. In the beginning, it was very simple: Justice, Equality, Sustainability, and Solidarity; you cannot achieve that alone, so at least at the European level. It started so beautifully, and by now we are represented at all levels. The reason I stopped is simple: by now, the very behavior I so strongly condemn has simply become acceptable within Volt. The way the departure of Nilufer was handled, the way we blindly follow parties in municipalities where we participate that systematically exclude others, and the way we abuse democratic rights to justify behavior that cannot be justified. How we want to elevate exceptions to the rule. Democracy is not a right; you have to earn it and, unfortunately, sometimes even fight for it. Claiming rights while failing to uphold the rights of those who think differently does not foster tolerance, but rather the further division of people. Don't get me wrong, I still stand behind the pillars upon which Volt is built, but we are taking the wrong turn. I see Volt increasingly diving into treating symptoms instead of discussing the causes. A positive exception is the stance on defense; unfortunately, a powerful military apparatus is necessary. But if you want to do something about the climate, you have to tackle the root cause: 120 million people in China living in poverty, or look at child poverty in general. While our well-educated children are sitting on the highway, according to UNICEF, 300 million children are still living in extreme poverty. What argument should I use to deny these people the chance to try to escape that poverty? And then there is the women's quota; I would love nothing more than to see more women in politics, but in the current world, driven by social media and big data and ruled by men who care little about equality, you see the opposite. Driven by what the algorithms deliver, women are becoming more left-wing and men more right-wing. So do not limit yourself by ideals. If there are men who are willing and capable of contributing what we need women in politics for, then make use of them; do not confuse ends and means. Men and women are not equal, and that is precisely the beauty of it. Not everyone feels comfortable in a male or female box, and that is okay, but we are not all equal, and that is precisely what makes it so beautiful. And what about equality? That, too, is very simple: you are only equal if you accept others as equals. Equality does not mean that everyone must think or feel what you feel.

<u>Original title (nl)</u> : Democracy is not a right you have, you have to earn it, you have to fight for it!

<u>Original content (nl)</u> :

Vanaf 2020 ben ik ruim drie jaar actief geweest binnen Volt, maar in 2024 ben ik ermee gestopt. Niet omdat ik niet meer geloof of sta voor waar Volt op gebouwd is. In het begin was het heel simpel; Rechtvaardigheid, Gelijkwaardigheid, Duurzaamheid en Solidariteit, en dat kun je niet alleen, dus minimaal op Europees niveau. Het begon zo mooi, en inmiddels zijn we op alle niveaus vertegenwoordigd. De reden dat ik gestopt ben is simpel, inmiddels is hetzelfde gedrag dat ik zo veroordeel gewoon goed geworden binnen Volt. De manier waarop er omgegaan is met het vertrek van Nilufer, de manier waarop we in Gemeenten waar we meedoen klakkeloos partijen volgen die stelselmatig anderen uitsluiten en de manier waarop we democratische rechten misbruiken om gedrag te rechtvaardigen dat niet te rechtvaardigen is. Hoe we uitzonderingen tot regel willen verheffen. Democratie is geen recht, dat moet je verdienen en helaas soms zelfs voor vechten. Wel aanspraak maken maar zelf niet staan voor het recht van andersdenkenden zorgt niet voor verdraagzaamheid maar voor het verder uiteendrijven van mensen. Begrijp me niet verkeerd, ik sta nog steeds achter de pilaren waarop Volt gebouwd is, maar we nemen de verkeerde afslag. Ik zie Volt steeds vaker in de symptoombestrijding duiken ipv het te hebben over de oorzaken. Een positieve uitzondering is de opstelling rondom defensie, helaas is een krachtig militair apparaat noodzakelijk. Maar als je iets aan het klimaat wilt doen dan moet je de oorzaak aanpakken, 120 miljoen mensen in China die in armoede leven of kijken naar kinderarmoede in het algemeen. Terwijl onze goed opgeleide kinderen op de snelweg gaan zitten, leven er volgens Unicef nog steeds 300 miljoen kinderen in extreme armoede. Welk argument zou ik moeten gebruiken om deze mensen de kans te ontnemen om te proberen die armoede te ontvluchten? En dan het vrouwen quota, ik zou niets liever zien dan meer vrouwen in de politiek, maar in de huidige wereld, gedreven door social media en big data en geregeerd door mannen die weinig hebben met gelijkheid zie je het omgekeerde. Gedreven door wat de algoritmes brengen worden vrouwen linkser en mannen rechtser. Dus beperk jezelf niet door idealen, Als er mannen zijn die willen, en die in staat zijn om datgene waarvoor we de vrouwen in de politiek nodig hebben ook in te brengen maak daar dan gebruik van, haal niet doel en middel door elkaar.  Mannen en vrouwen zijn niet gelijk en dat is nu juist het mooie, en niet iedereen voelt zich thuis in een hokje man of vrouw en dat is oké, maar we zijn niet allemaal gelijk en dat is nu juist zo mooi. En gelijkwaardigheid dan? Ook die is heel simpel gelijkwaardig ben je alleen als je en ander ook als gelijkwaardige accepteert, gelijkwaardig Heid betekend niet dat iedereen moet vinden of voelen wat jij voelt.

## 995. More unity, more strength, concerted action

Politically speaking, Germany will only survive and remain strong if we reform the EU according to the motto: "Europe first, national only when useful." This requires classifications within the member structures, so that, for example, unwilling or obstructive countries are downgraded or at least disadvantaged in certain areas or receive fewer benefits. Mr. Macron once expressed a similar idea.  
  
And above all, we need a strong voice in foreign policy as a TRUE AND UNITED EUROPEAN UNION, as the name should actually suggest.  
  
Due to my frequent stays abroad, I constantly hear the aforementioned demand, especially directed at us Germans.

## 997. The traffic

The traffic.   
  
Cyprus is supposedly a small island thus the destination to A to B should not take a long time. Instead it might take someone a usual 10-minute ride even an hour, especially when it comes to peak-hours.   
  
For example, from Aglantzia to go to Stavrou, around 17:00, it took up to 40 minutes. It's not just the ride itself, or the lack of public transport option, it's also the fact that Cyprus cities are not built for walking either, which is always another good &amp; healthy option to have as an individual.

## 998. The castle

I had a Kafkaesque experience with the "self-governing bodies"—especially the Association of Statutory Health Insurance Physicians. The case workers are incompetent, yet they wield a power that prevented me from freely practicing medicine. I wanted to work in a private practice instead of a hospital, which was denied to me. This was due to the case workers' ignorance and bureaucracy. Therefore, I demand a reduction in bureaucracy and flexible, well-trained case workers.  
  
This experience shook me so deeply that I considered giving up medicine temporarily.

<u>Original title (de)</u> : Das Schloss

<u>Original content (de)</u> :

Ich hatte ein kafkaeskes Erlebnis im Zusammenhang mit den "Selbstverwaltungsorganen" - allem voran der Kassenärztlichen Vereinigung. Die Sachbearbeiter sind inkompetent, verfügen aber über eine Macht, die es mir verwehrte meinen Beruf als Arzt frei auszuüben. Ich wollte statt in einer Klinik in einer Praxis arbeiten, was mir verwehrt wurde. Aus Unwissenheit der Sachbearbeiter und Bürokratie. In dem Zusammenhang fordere ich Bürokratieabbau, flexible und gut geschulte Sachbearbeiter.   
Diese Erfahrung hat mich so erschüttert, dass ich den Beruf zeitweise aufgeben wollte.

I will try to bring friends and family along on this journey in a pragmatic way.

## 1004. Missing male turtles

Due to climate change, the soil temperature has risen. However, the temperature in a turtle's nest determines whether the hatchlings will be male or female. This increased temperature means that almost only female turtles are hatching, and some species have already become extinct. (As an aside: I participated in a turtle conservation program in Malaysia, tagged the mother turtles, and dug up the eggs to bury them on the project grounds. The sand there can be kept wet and therefore cold.)

Die erhöhte Temparatur führt dazu, dass fast nurnoch weibliche Schildkröten schlüpfen und einige Arten bereits ausgestorben sind. (Betug zu mir: Ich war in Malaysia bei einem Schildkrötenschutzprogramm dabei, habe die Muttertiere markiert und die Eier ausgebuddelt, um sie auf dem Gelände des Projektes zu verbuddeln. Dort kann der Sand nass und damit kalt gehalten werden)

## 1009. The family

The compatibility of family and career is not sufficiently valued in Germany: Compared to my parents' generation (Boomers), where it was socially normal and more feasible for one parent (usually the mother) to stay home or work part-time, this has changed drastically. For both parents to work full-time is virtually impossible without support from family (especially grandparents). It's frustrating to look at neighboring countries where this is much easier to reconcile (from our personal circle of friends, especially Denmark, the Netherlands, Finland, but also France).

Dass beide Elternteile Vollzeit arbeiten, ist ohne Unterstützung seitens der Familie (insbes. Großeltern) so gut wie unmöglich. Hier frustriert ein Blick auf Nachbarländer, in denen dies deutlich besser vereinbar ist (aus unserem persönlichen Freundeskreis insbes. Dänemark, Niederlande, Finnland, aber auch Frankreich).

## 1010. untapped societal potential

I am 65 years old and have spent more than 40 years in healthcare: after studying medicine, I completed alternative service at an institute for people with intellectual disabilities. After that, I specialized as a rehabilitation physician and worked in that capacity for more than 30 years, working with patients and rehabilitation teams, as a trainer and researcher, mostly in private practice. I recently retired.  
  
I am happy and healthy. "All my basic needs are fulfilled," such as housing, family, hobbies, et cetera. A good retirement. "What more could you want?" Almost everyone calls out to me: "Enjoy life now!" Sure; it is well-intentioned, and I enjoy doing that, but still...: I don't need a camper with bicycles on the back. I am not going to go on a world tour. I hope to live a few more years and am now "available" to others in a new way. For example, I teach. And I take care of my grandchildren. My repertoire as an amateur pianist is growing steadily. However: how do we make good (preferably optimal, of course) use in our society of the potential of people who are not (or no longer) active in their original profession (in my case, that of a practicing physician)? Especially now that there are so many shortages, it is regrettable that there is a "hard cut" between working and not working.  
  
I will find my way, but in general, there is little organization in this area. (If I see it correctly, haha.)  
  
Experience: the process of retirement.

<u>Original title (nl)</u> : onbenut maatschappelijk potentieel

<u>Original content (nl)</u> :

Ik ben 65 jaar en heb meer dan 40 jaar in de gezondheidszorg doorgebracht: na mijn studie geneeskunde heb ik vervangende dienstplicht vervuld in een instituut voor mensen met een verstandelijke beperking. Daarna heb ik me gespecialiseerd tot revalidatiearts en in die functie heb ik meer dan 30 gewerkt, werkend met patiënten en revalidatieteams, als opleider en als onderzoeker, meestentijds in de praktijk. Recent ben ik met pensioen gegaan.  
  
Ik ben gelukkig en gezond. "All my basic needs are fulfilled", zoals wonen, familie, hobby's, et cetera. Goed pensioen. "Wat wil je ng meer?" Bijna iedereen roept me toe: "nu genieten!" Tuurlijk; goed bedoeld ook en ik doe dat graag, maar toch...: ik hoef geen camper met fietsen achterop. Ik ga geen wereldreis maken. Ik hoop nog wat jaren te leven en ben nu op een nieuwe manier "beschikbaar" voor anderen. Zo geef ik bijvoorbeeld les. En zorg ik voor kleinkinderen. Mijn reportoire als amateur-pianist groeit gestaag.  
  
Echter: hoe maken we in onze maatschappij goed (liefst optimaal natuurlijk) gebruik van het potentieel van de mensen, die niet (of niet meer) actief zijn in hun oorspronkelijke vak (in mijn geval dat van praktiserend arts)? Zeker nu er zoveel tekorten zijn, is het betreurenswaardig, dat er een "harde knip" bestaat tussen werken en niet-werkend.  
Ik ga mijn weg wel vinden, maar in het algemeen is er weinig georganiseerd op dit vlak. (Als ik het goed zie, haha.)  
  
Ervaring: proces van pensionering.

## 1012. 70 Years of Europe: An Imperfect Paradigm Shift

Born in France in the 1950s, I heard about the wars from my family and friends, the scars of which I could still see on the buildings. In my childhood games, these relics of the past lived on as if they were normal.  
  
As a schoolboy and student, I learned languages ​​from other European countries, including Germany.  
  
As an adult, I lived and worked in Germany.  
  
As an older person, I see how many young people study across borders within the EU, how they communicate without boundaries.  
  
I think that the nation-states of my childhood still exist within the EU, only partially and sensibly united, even though they no longer provide the right political framework for young adults and those of tomorrow. These young people growing up in a European context are not yet aware of their political power and the value of their experience. It's good that VOLT exists to give them a voice.  
  


<u>Original title (de)</u> : 70 Jahre Europa: unvollkommener Paradigmenwechsel

<u>Original content (de)</u> :

Geboren in den 50er Jahren in Frankreich, ich hörte von Familie und Umgebung von den Kriegen, deren Spuren ich noch an den Gebäuden sah. In meinen Kinderspielen lebten diese Vergangenheitszeugnisse weiter wie eine Normalität.  
Schüler und Student lernte ich Sprachen von anderen europäischen Ländern, darunter Deutschland.  
Erwachsener, lebte und arbeitete ich in Deutschland.  
Älterer Mensch, ich sehe wieviel Jugendliche quer durch die Grenzen innerhalb der EU studieren, wie sie grenzenlos kommunizieren.  
Ich denke, dass die nationalen Staaten aus meiner Kindheit in der EU noch weiterleben, nur teilweise vernünftig vereint, obwohl sie für die jungen Erwachsenen und die von morgen gar nicht mehr die richtigen politischen Rahmen bilden. Diese europäisch wachsenden jungen Menschen sind sich ihrer politischen Macht und des Werts ihrer Erfahrung noch nicht bewusst. Gut, dass es VOLT gibt, um ihnen eine Stimme zu geben.

## 1014. Extraordinary weather events

A few years ago, there was severe flooding in the Ahr Valley. The heavy rainfall was quite predictable. Nevertheless, there was no adequate automatic warning system.  
  
Many people there lost their homes or large parts of them.  
  
My step-aunt was also affected.  
  
The water even reached the front door of the house where I lived as a child.  
  
These extreme weather events are occurring with increasing frequency.  
  
Currently, we are also experiencing recurring periods of drought, which are then interrupted by monsoon-like downpours.  
  
This is increasingly leading to reduced yields for farmers.  
  


<u>Original title (de)</u> : Außergewöhnliche Wettereignisse

<u>Original content (de)</u> :

Vor ein paar Jahren gab es im Ahrtal ein gravierendes Hochwasser. Die Regenmassen waren im Vorfeld durchaus vorherzusehen. Dennoch gab es kein hinreichendes automatisches Alarmsystem.  
Viele haben dort ihr Haus bzw. Große Teile davon verloren.  
Auch meine Stief-Tante war davon betroffen.  
Das Wasser stand auch bis zur Haustüre des Hauses, in dem ich in meiner Kindheit gewohnt habe.  
Diese außergewöhnlichen Wetter Ereignisse treten immer regelmäßiger auf.  
Auch aktuell erleben wir wiederkehrende trockenphasen, welche dann von monsunartigen Regengüssen unterbrochen werden.  
Dies führt bei Landwirten verstärkt zu minder Erträgen.

## 1020. My partner's Bday...

My partner is turning 65, and I would loive to throw a party, but he hates parties, especially surprise parties. Yet, friends in the valley are asking me about will happen this weekend. You have to know my partner is doing a lot for the people. ## 1030. Torn apart

I feel increasingly trapped and unable to act and live according to my own values ​​and convictions. Climate and nature conservation, sustainability and poverty reduction, equal opportunities and conditions for all (including outside Europe), as well as consideration and humanity are extremely important to me. However, I am confronted daily with the following decisions: Do I actively restrict and limit myself—by not buying certain things, not using the car to travel somewhere, but instead using a bicycle, or by critically examining myself and my actions—and thus become more and more of an outsider in this society? OR do I simply accept that I cannot change anything this way and that the real leverage doesn't lie with me, and despair at this realization?

<u>Original title (de)</u> : Zerissenheit

<u>Original content (de)</u> :

Ich fühle mich zunehmend gefangen und unfähig nach meinen eigenen Werten und Überzeugungen zu handeln und zu leben. Für mich sind der Klima- und Naturschutz, Nachhaltigkeit und Abbau der Armut, gleiche Chancen und Voraussetzungen für alle (auch außerhalb Europas), sowie Rücksicht und Menschlichkeit extrem wichtig. Jedoch sehe ich mich täglich mit folgenden Entscheidungen konfrontiert: Beschränke und begrenze ich mich aktiv selbst - indem ich gewisse Dinge nicht kaufe, nicht das Auto nutze um irgendwohin zu fahren, sondern das Fahrrad oder mich selbst und meine Handlungen kritisch hinterfrage - und werde so immer mehr zur Außenseiterin in dieser Gesellschaft ODER akzeptiere ich einfach, dass ich damit nichts ändern kann und die wahren Hebel nicht bei mir liegen und verzweifle an dieser Erkenntnis?

## 1032. Disappointing experience with local politician

At the local elections in my city I talked to the major about the heavy truck traffic in our street. The street leads to a processing company and every day many semi-trailer trucks drive along it. The street is quite narrow and it is difficult to pass them. In my opinion is not only annoying but also posing a danger to the locals living in and close to the street. There is a street bypassing the whole city which would divert the traffic from our street but unfortunately it is not finished. Only about 200m are missing, but they are on the private ground of the factory and the factory does not want to pay for completing it. I asked the major if she could do something so that the missing part of the street, but she said that the factory is very important for the city as tax payer and employer of 200 persons. But there are also over 200 residents in our street who suffer from the traffic. She said she cannot do anything. This was very disapointing.

## 1056. Suspending the impulse!

I find it astonishing how many triggers people have these days, especially in forums and groups. I'm not even talking about unfiltered social media forums, but perfectly normal groups about a shared Qi Gong practice or natural gardening. In the latter, all it takes is for someone to harmlessly post a picture, perhaps of a non-native bush, and a shitstorm erupts, usually ending with everyone attacking the "perpetrator," comparing them to truly evil groups, and them leaving the group completely bewildered—or getting kicked out. The same thing happens in the other forum: something is brought up, and then the shitstorm begins. All superficial triggers without a long fuse, without reflection or awareness. We seem to have forgotten how to communicate with each other and to accept different perspectives. Or how to take a breath and not give in to the impulse to know better than others or to react immediately.

<u>Original title (de)</u> : Suspending the impulse!

<u>Original content (de)</u> :

Ich finde es erstaunlich, wie viele Trigger heutzutage bei Leuten da sind, insbesondere in Foren und Gruppen. Ich rede noch nicht mal über ungepufferte social Media Foren, sondern ganz normale Gruppen über ein gemeinsames Qi Gong Training oder über Naturgärten. Im letzten braucht nur jemand harmlos irgendein Bild zu posten, wo z.B. ein Busch drauf ist, der nicht eiheimisch ist, und schon erfolgt ein Shitstorm, der meist damit endet, dass alle über den "Täter" herfallen, ihn mit wirklich bösen Bevölkerungsgruppen vergleichen, und er oder sie völlig konsterniert die Gruppe verlässt - oder rausgeschmissen wird. Auch beim anderen Forum wird was angesprochen, und dann erfolgt der Shitstorm. Alles oberflächige Trigger ohne lange Lunte, ohne Reflektion oder Bewusstheit. Wir scheinen verlernt zu haben, mit einander zu kommunzieren und andere Perspektiven gelten zu lassen. Oder mal durch zu atmen und dem Impuls, was besser zu wissen als die anderen oder zu reagieren mal nicht zu folgen.

## 1058. A shift in global values

I work in EU policymaking, and following a huge rightward shift after the EU elections last year, we are seeing some of the most important legislation (the European Green Deal) being subjected to "death by a thousand cuts". The European Commission, who is not supposed to be a politically motivated actor, is giving in to political and lobby pressure in the name of "simplification" and "competitiveness". Despite previous assurances that simplification would not lead to deregulation and that the EU’s sustainability goals would remain intact, they are introducing significant changes that constitute a major setback for transparency, accountability, sustainable finance, not to mention our climate and environmental goals. They are even starting to attack NGOs' involvement in the policymaking process, which would be an enormous blow to our democratic participation. It feels like the vultures are circling and we are trying our best to do as much damage control as we can, but we are heading for a massive deregulation. The global political context, in particular everything that is happening in the USA, seems to have uprooted the goalposts. Peoples' values have changed, and I no longer feel like I am aligned with the majority of society in terms of wanting a better future for everyone. People seem to only care about the financial bottom line. It's really depressing.
