## 1059. The crisis of cooperation

For some time now, I've been discussing the "network of networks" with a few people—that is, a level at which all relevant groups and actors become visible and, above all, effective across regions. At a recent conference, I experienced firsthand where this idea falls short. Firstly, most people are firmly embedded in roles and structures and consciously position themselves according to "their" task, "their" concern, and "their" goal. It is either impossible for them or doesn't seem logical to them to consider their own project systemically—even when they are acting in the interest of the common good. Here, a performance-oriented mindset may still be at play, dictating that we "achieve" something "on our own" and "alone," and certainly not share the glory and honor with others. Secondly, it is indeed difficult to become capable of speaking for an abstract system or to be tasked with doing so. The mere act of being asked to advocate for cooperation in the interest of systemic change often triggers strong defensive reactions and, above all, questions about one's legitimacy. Based on these experiences, I unfortunately do not yet believe that we as a human society are capable of systemic cooperation.

<u>Original title (de)</u> : Die Krise der Kooperation

<u>Original content (de)</u> :

Mit einigen Menschen spreche ich seit einer Weile über das "Netz der Netze" - also über eine Ebene, auf der alle relevanten Gruppen und Akteure überregional sichtbar, vor allem aber wirksam werden. Auf einer Fachtagung habe ich kürzlich wieder eindrücklich erlebt, woran diese Idee scheitert. Zum einen sind die meisten Menschen fest in Rollen und Strukturen eingebunden und verorten sich bewusst für "ihre" Aufgabe, "ihr" Anliegen und "ihr" Ziel. Es ist ihnen nicht möglich oder erscheint für sie nicht schlüssig, das eigene Vorhaben auch systemisch zu betrachten - selbst wenn sie im Sinne des Allgemeinwohls aktiv werden. Hier greift möglicherweise immer noch ein Leistungsverständnis, welches uns diktiert, "selbst" und "allein" etwas "zu schaffen" und keinesfalls Ruhm und Ehre mit anderen zu teilen. Zum anderen ist es tatsächlich schwierig, für ein abstraktes System sprechfähig zu werden oder sich damit zu beauftragen. Allein die Beauftragung, für eine Kooperation im Sinne des Systemwandels zu sprechen, löst häufig starke Abwehrreaktionen und vor allem die Frage nach der Berechtigung aus. Ich halte uns als menschliche Gesellschaft auf Basis dieser Erlebnisse leider noch nicht für systemisch kooperationsfähig.

## 1060. Perceived truths and supposed rights

For three decades, cars have been parking on the grassy areas on either side of my street, areas that—due to their long use as parking spaces—actually look like parking spaces. Then, seemingly overnight, this "sidewalk and grassy parking" on this very long street was penalized with a €55 fine. In the first round, 240 vehicle owners were fined, and in just a few weeks, fines totaling approximately €50,000 were collected. My initial reaction was relief that action was finally being taken. Then I realized that it wasn't as straightforward for everyone as it was for me (I have a parking space, but no car). Then the discussion began (press, local council, WhatsApp group). Overall, the tone is still friendly, but the car-owner bubble is really intense. Here, arguments are quickly based on a perceived right to free parking in public spaces, and the elderly, disabled woman or the single mother with seven children are constantly cited as examples. Anyone who advocates for alternative uses of public space is labeled "green," "out of touch with reality," and "ideologically deranged."

<u>Original title (de)</u> : Gefühlte Wahrheiten und vermeintliches Anrecht

<u>Original content (de)</u> :

In meiner Straße parken seit 3 Jahrzehnten die Autos auf den Grünflächen, die links und rechts vom Gehweg angelegt sind und - aufgrund der langen Nutzung als Parkplatz - auch wie Parkplätze aussehen. Von einem Tag auf den anderen wurde das "Gehweg- und Grünflächenparken" auf dieser sehr langen Straße mit einem Bußgeld von 55 € geahndet. In der ersten Runde wurden 240 Halter mit Bußgeld belegt, insgesamt wurden in wenigen Wochen Bußgelder i.H.v. ca. 50.000 € erhoben. Im ersten Moment habe ich mich gefreut, dass hier endlich durchgegriffen wird. Dann habe ich verstanden, dass das nicht für alle so einfach ist, wie für mich (ich habe einen Stellplatz, aber kein Auto). Dann ging die Diskussion los (Presse, Ortsbeirat, WhatsApp-Gruppe). Insgesamt ist der Ton noch freundlich, aber die Autofahrer-Bubble ist schon echt krass. Hier wird recht schnell mit einem gefühlten Anrecht auf einen kostenfreien Stellplatz im öffentlichen Raum argumentiert und ständig wird die alte, gehbehinderte Dame oder die alleinerziehende Mama mit 7 Kindern als Argument herangezogen. Wer sich für eine anderweitige Nutzung des öffentlichen Raums ausspricht, wird als "grün", "realitätsfern" und "ideologisch verstrahlt" bezeichnet.

## 1066. To intervene or not to intervene.

I'm standing by a train platform in the evening after a long day at work. A young man and a woman walk past me. The woman tells the man to "piss off." I perk up and think: Maybe this man is harassing the woman. I look more closely to see if I should intervene. Then it turns out that the woman apparently has a photo of the man, which he's demanding be deleted. I think: Okay, if she deletes it now, they'll probably be able to sort things out, and he'll leave her alone. I'm relieved that I didn't have to intervene. Two minutes later, however, the two of them walk past me again, and now it looks like the man is harassing the woman again. I consider intervening again, but they both walk past me extremely quickly and are gone before I can do anything. I'm unsure whether I acted wrongly. It seemed as if the man thought he had the right to control the woman.

<u>Original title (de)</u> : Eingreifen oder nicht?

<u>Original content (de)</u> :

Ich stehe am Abend eines anstrengenden Arbeitstags an einem Bahngleis. Neben mir kommen ein junger Mann und eine Frau. Die Frau sagt zu dem Mann „verpiss dich mal“. Ich horche auf und denke: Vielleicht bedrängt dieser Mann die Frau. Ich schaue genauer hin, ob ich nicht eingreifen muss. Dann stellt sich heraus, dass die Frau offenbar ein Foto von dem Mann hat, dessen Löschung er fordert. Ich denke: Ok, wenn sie es jetzt löscht, schaffen sie es wahrscheinlich klar zu kommen, und er lässt sie in Ruhe. Ich bin beruhigt, dass ich nicht einschreiten musste. Zwei Minuten später kommen die beiden aber wieder an mir vorbei, und jetzt sieht es wieder so aus, als würde der Mann die Frau bedrängen. Ich überlege wieder, ob ich eingreifen soll, aber die beiden laufen extrem schnell an mir vorbei und sind schon wieder weg, bevor ich etwas tun kann. Ich bin mir unsicher, ob ich falsch gehandelt habe. Es wirkte so, als ob der Mann meinte, er müsse über die Frau verfügen können.

## 1071. The sociologue and the theatre

I attended a presentation by a sociologist who is working with the local theatre to engage villagers in giving the theatre a meaningful place in the community. It was very interesting and showed the problem of housing. I never knew that 40% of the houses in this village are secondary homes. Young people have trouble finding a place locally. Mind you, there is also not kuch economic activity, and many young people choose to live in cities these days. There was one person that I found interesting, because he thinks systemically about issues. He was talking about the commons in a way that I hadn't heard before. Many people benefit from the area, it's a great nature tourism place, but all we get back is the money they spend locally. Our thinking is so dominated by money and teh economy. We have to change the way we think about ourselves, our environment, the way we live, the solutions we can find together. The concept of the commons may be brought back to life. What if we manage to renovate the old textile buildings that are now empty, for housing of young people? One person has space to make an apprtment in her house, but she is not doing it, because too many rules and morms will make it costly, and then the rights of the tenants are soo strong, you can never get people out anymore. Hmm, who knows what we could do if we just tried to come together? A seed had been planted...

## 1075. AI helps shape care, but can also 'hallucinate'

I currently use AI in healthcare (working as a practitioner and team leader in mental healthcare). It helps me enormously to create summaries of vision documents and research reports for my teams. It also assists in writing a substantive article or chapter; I always ask AI to create an outline regarding a specific theme and then check if I have forgotten anything that AI suggests to me. Occasionally, I use AI to record a conversation, transcribe it, and convert it into a report. This does not yet have the desired final quality; it also sometimes fills in information with things that were not quite said ('hallucinates'), and it is not entirely clear what my input and that of the client was regarding important decisions and how informed consent was established. In all these matters, it is not clear to me whether I can be certain that my input is not being shared with others without my permission. I lack appropriate government policy on this. It feels as if the field has to figure it out for itself.

<u>Original title (nl)</u> : AI helpt om zorg vorm te geven, maar kan ook 'hallucineren'

<u>Original content (nl)</u> :

Ik gebruik AI momenteel in de zorg (werk als behandelaar en teamleider in de ggz). Het helpt me enorm om samenvatting van visiedocumenten en onderzoeksrapporten te maken voor mijn teams. Het helpt ook bij het schrijven van een inhoudelijk artikel of hoofdstuk, ik vraag AI dan altijd om een opzet te maken over een bepaald thema en check dan of ik zaken vergeten ben die AI me aanreikt. Een enkele keer gebruik ik AI om een gesprek op te nemen, te transcriberen en om te zetten in een verslag. Dit heeft nog niet de gewenste eindkwaliteit, ook vult het soms informatie in met dingen die net niet gezegd zijn ('hallucineert'), en er wordt niet helemaal duidelijk wat mijn input en die van de client was op belangrijke beslissingen en hoe de informed consent tot stand kwam.   
Bij al deze zaken is me niet helder of ik er zeker van kan zijn dat mijn input niet gedeeld wordt met anderen zonder mijn toestemming. Ik mis passend beleid van de overheid hierop. Het voelt alsof het veld het zelf uit moet vinden.

## 1078. New England Town Meetings &amp; the Interstate Highway Expansion

Growing up in the northeastern United States, my town (like many in New England at the time) operated hyper-democratically with an annual Town Meeting. All of the town's citizens gathered each year to act as the town's legislative body, debating and making policy decisions.  
  
One of my earliest memories of our Town Meeting had us debating the extension of a regional highway system through our town. I was young, so my perceptions of it at the time were of lots of very opinionated adults being very loud and the discussion being very boring. Now though, a few decades later, it's rather impactful in that day's decisions continues to shape the regional transportation infrastructure... We decided not to allow the highway to pass through the town, and so the highway (Route 25) exists only from the coast through the nearest city, where it abruptly ends and forces you to take local roads until connecting with the next highway a few towns later.  
  
It's impactful to me in the level of long-term power and impact given to a very citizen-level process, while also (again in retrospect) demonstrating some challenges to regional cooperation in a democratic framework.

## 1087. the risks of renting property by elderly individuals

I have an apartment for rent in an old building in the heart of a medieval village, preferably to a single man, as it's on the ground floor and relatively dark, suitable for someone who works and only returns home in the evening. The apartment meets all health and safety standards, however, and the rent is reasonable. It has been managed for a long time by an agency that I was very satisfied with, especially thanks to its secretary. She has since left, and one of the owner's children has been assigned to find a new tenant. There were many applications, yet the rental failed three times. The first time, the selected candidate didn't have the security deposit when moving in. The second time, the candidate's son advised her against finalizing the lease, saying the apartment was too small. Finally, the third candidate, upon moving in, decided to repaint everything and destroyed all the work we had done to prepare the apartment after the previous tenant left. He removed and threw away the kitchen cabinets, which I had agreed to help replace. I then learned that he was in a relationship and wanted to have a child in this apartment, which was completely unsuitable for that purpose. The agency ignored my recommendations, and we terminated the lease. I don't have the energy to redo the work, and the agency informed me that they are no longer marketing or managing the property.

j'ai un appartement à louer dans un immeuble ancien au cœur d'un village médiéval, de préférence à un homme seul car en rez de rue et relativement sombre, convient à quelqu'un qui travaille et ne rentre que le soir. le logement est cependant conforme aux critères de salubrité, et son loyer est intéressant. il est géré depuis longtemps par une agence qui me donnait toute satisfaction surtout grâce à sa secrétaire. celle ci est partie, un des enfants du patron a été désigné pour trouver un nouveau locataire. il y avait beaucoup de demandes, pourtant la location a échoué 3 fois. une première fois le candidat retenu n'avait pas l'argent de la caution au moment de prendre possession du logement, la deuxième fois, le fils de la candidate lui a déconseillé de finaliser considérant que l'appartement était trop petit, et enfin  le troisième candidat, entré dans les murs à décidé de tout repeindre et a détruit tout le travail que nous avions fait pour  mettre en état après le départ du locataire précèdent, enlevé et jeté les meubles de cuisine dont j'avais accepté de participer au remplacement et finalement j'ai appris qu'il était en couple et désirait avoir un enfant dans cet appartement absolument pas approprié pour cet usage. l'agence n'a pas tenu compte de mes recommandations et nous avons résilié le bail. je n'ai pas le courage de refaire le travail et l'agence m'informé qu'elle renonçait à commercialiser et gérer ce bien

## 1097. Loneliness and stress due to overpopulation

I have lived in the same house for sixty years on a quiet lane where Eurosense also has a branch. Occasionally, there would be a construction site... Now, for several years, I have been living right in the middle of a construction site. New construction is going upwards, and renovations of older buildings are creating more living spaces in the same location.  
The neighborhood is full of anonymous company cars (especially in the evenings and on weekends), so residents or their visitors can no longer find a parking spot. All that residential activity and traffic brings with it noise pollution from people, animals, cars, and roaring motor vehicles. The noise pollution from airplanes pales in comparison.

<u>Original title (nl)</u> : Eenzaamheid en stress door overbevolking

<u>Original content (nl)</u> :

Ik woon al zestig jaar in hetzelfde huis in een rustige laan waar ook Eurosense een vestiging heeft. Af en toe eens een bouwwerf.... Nu leef ik al enkele jaren middenin een bouwwerf. De nieuwbouw gaat de hoogte in en de renovaties van oudere gebouwen creëren meer woongelegenheden op dezelfde plaats.  
De wijk staat vol met anonieme bedrijfswagens (vooral s'avonds en in de weekends zodat de bewoners of hun bezoek hun auto niet meer kwijtraken. Al die bewoning en verkeer brengt geluidsoverlast mee van mensen, dieren, auto's, knetterende motorvoertuigen. De geluidsoverlast van vliegtuigen is daartegen niets.

## 1100. Preaching for your parish

I attended Guillaume Merry's lecture at the "L'odyssée de l'eau" exhibition and was struck by a quote he made about where to start to address the planet's current issues. He is particularly sensitive to the extermination of living beings by humans.  
I empathize with his passion, but I'm skeptical of the idea that we need to start creating real marine reserves, because the impact is immediately visible, while other actions, like reducing plastic use, take much longer. He's aware that these statements might suggest he's busy with other actions, but he stands by his own opinion. I'm surprised he'd prioritize one idea over another.

Lui é particolarmente sensibile allo sterminio degli  esseri viventi da parte degli umani.  
Sento empatia per lla sua passione ma sono dubbiosa riguardo all 'idea che bisogna cominciare a fare delle vere riserve marine prché l'impatto é visibile subito mentre altre azioni come ridurre l'uso della plastice prendono molto piu tempo. Lui é cosciente che queste affermazioni poossinocolpire che  é impegnato iltre azioni, ma mantiene la propia idea. Sono sorpresa dal fatto di voler dare piu priorità a un'idea piuttosto che un'altra.

## 1107. Can I really trust ChatGPT?

My experience relates to ChatGPT, and particularly its reliability. I use ChatGPT very regularly, but I still frequently discover errors and instances where things are being fabricated. You notice that circular reasoning is sometimes used from which you cannot really "escape"; as a result, individuals or organizations surface more quickly as answers to questions. Probably because these experiences also match best on the internet. It is unfortunate and concerning that unusual suspects sometimes do not surface.

## 1109. Bad experiences with a party called VOLT.

Following the recent local elections, I was once again bitter and disappointed that I hadn't noticed anything from a political party. Just as in the European and National Council elections, the party was virtually invisible. I had originally hoped that this party would make it clear to people—not only in Austria, but throughout Europe—that a strong, free, and democratic, a united Europe is necessary to guarantee prosperity and freedom. I supported this party, namely VOLT, in the European elections by submitting a corresponding declaration to the district office. Afterwards, I wondered what the point was, since I heard nothing back. There are several other points of criticism, but—forgive me for repeating myself—what was the point?

Hatte ich ursprünglich die Hoffnung, dass diese Partei den Menschen - nicht nur in Österreich, sondern in ganz Europa - klarmachen würde bzw. zumindest könnte, dass es ein starkes, freies und demokratisches, ein gemeinsames Europa braucht, um den Wohlstand und die Freiheit sicherstellen zu können. ## 1114. Algorithms that create political polarization sow discord in families and communities.

Part of the family has become radicalized by right-wing populism and part by left-wing populism. Each brings arguments from their social and informational bubbles. ## 1116. Public transport in the border region

I live on a European internal border (Germany/Netherlands) and therefore use public transport on both sides. Thanks to an EU project, a train now crosses the border here, but the connection is very unreliable because the two systems are not compatible, meaning that the respective sections of the route are always operated by a local team. Particularly on the German part of the route, there are extremely frequent cancellations due to staff shortages. Furthermore, I need a separate app and account for each transport provider. There is usually no compatibility, especially across the border, which I find very regrettable. For climate protection reasons, it is extremely important to me to use public transport, even if it sometimes takes considerably longer.  
  
Nevertheless, I greatly appreciate being able to visit neighboring towns without having to exchange currency, etc. I am convinced that better cross-border connections will make Europe grow closer together. Especially here at the border, the Union already feels like a reality, even if there are still major hurdles to overcome.

<u>Original title (de)</u> : ÖPNV im Grenzland

<u>Original content (de)</u> :

Ich lebe an einer europäischen Binnengrenze (De/NL) und bin entsprechend auf beiden Seiten mit dem ÖPNV unterwegs. Dank eines EU-Projekts fährt inzwischen ein Zug hier über die Grenze, allerdings ist die Verbindung sehr unzuverlässig, da die beiden Systeme nicht kompatibel sind und daher die jeweiligen Streckenabschnitte immer von einer lokalen Mannschaft gefahren werden. Besonders auf dem deutschen Teil der Strecke kommt es dabei extrem oft zu Ausfällen aufgrund von Personalmangel. Außerdem benötige ich für jeden Mobilitätsanbieter eine eigene App mit eigenem Konto. Besonders über die Grenze hinweg gibt es meist keine Kompatibilität, was ich sehr bedauere. Aus Klimaschutzgründen ist es mir ausgesprochen wichtig, den ÖPNV/ ÖSPV zu nutzen, auch wenn dies teils erheblich länger dauert.  
Dennoch genieße ich die Möglichkeit sehr, die Nachbarstädte besuchen zu können, ohne Währung etc. wechseln zu müssen. Ich bin überzeugt davon, dass eine bessere Verbindung über die Grenzen hinweg Europa stärker zusammenwachsen lässt. Besonders bei uns an der Grenze ist die Union gefühlt längst Realität, auch wenn noch große Hürden zu bewältigen sind.

<u>Unique identifier</u> : eurosense

<u>Europe is like</u> : my home

## 1117. Individual interest in public transportation

I commute by train. This week, as I was outside on the platform waiting for everyone to disembark so I could get on the train, a conductor was deploying an aid for disabled people to bridge the gap between train and platform. There were still other people inside, waiting for the deployment to finish so they too could leave. One person stepped onto that bridge as it deployed, several times so. The deployment was delayed massively and as she was reprimanded several times, she yelled "but I gotta catch my connecting train". It's pretty typical for people to block the door trying to enter instead of letting people disembark first, but this was a rare situation for me even as a seasoned commuter.

## 1120. Is it still "right" to procreate?

There would be many thoughts to describe but I will dissolve this.  
I think the overpopulation has reached its highest point, causing a good part of the world’s population to be deprived of their basic rights.  
Closing in brief my thought, I think that we should start to procreate less, thinking instead of the option of being able to adopt children.  
I know that maybe having a child is a fundamental right, but in my opinion it is necessary to start making a balance, which I see day after day, especially nowadays, increasingly negative.  
There are children who are in serious difficulties, especially in countries with more political and economic problems, but also from a human rights point of view.  
I don t want to be the one who saves children from "poorer countries", don’t see it in this way, but I think there is only that gain from this situation for all, in my opinion it could be a first step to rebalance a world that is in total ruin.

## 1141. Infrastructure in the Netherlands

Recently in the Netherlands, the whole country went basically on lock-down due to bad weather. The train system shut down, our main airport became dysfunctional and supply chains started shutting down. What does this say about the Netherlands? When they self-proclaim themselves to be one of the more developed countries in the world but the infrastructure cannot handle three days of snow. I believe this experience has shown to never rely on best case scenario, the Netherlands has invested in the belief that global warming will make our climate warmer and not just more extreme. In a world where we need to adapt to risks, the Netherlands ' divesting from infrastructure is a grave mistake. What will happen when the next crisis comes along, both man-made or from nature?

[fooday](https://www.fooday.it/too-good-to-go-nel-2025-una-crescita-in-doppia-cifra-solo-negli-ultimi-due-anni-duplicati-i-risultati-dei-cinque-precedenti.html)  
  
At the same time, I am really struck by following the debate on the return of nuclear power in Italy: for someone like me, who believes we need stable sources to replace fossil fuels, finally seeing a more open discussion – even amid controversy and resistance – is one of the few things that makes me feel there is at least a minimal long‑term vision in our society. ## 1155. Everything is actually there, but we downplay our abilities.

Germany is at the heart of Europe: safe, prosperous, and scenically beautiful. Together with France, it forms the core of Europe. Europe offers its people military protection (security), healthy food, good education, and has all the prerequisites to remain a livable continent in the 21st century.  
  
At the same time, the public debate has shifted. Negative, fearful, and destructive narratives dominate. War, migration, and economic problems frighten citizens, and democracy is under attack in every Western country.  
  
Personal dialogue with family, friends, and colleagues is becoming increasingly difficult—listening openly and exchanging ideas is becoming a rare art. Discourses are often highly polarized (filter bubbles), and we are less frequently able to reach understanding or agreement.  
  
Some parts of society strike me as tired, resigned, cynical, or even hateful.  
  
I miss positive messages, successes we can celebrate together, progressive change, and the hope that we can do better together in the future.

<u>Original title (de)</u> : Eigentlich ist alles da, aber wir reden uns klein

<u>Original content (de)</u> :

Deutschland ist im Zentrum Europas: sicher, wohlhabend und landschaftlich schön. Zusammen mit Frankreich bildet es des Kern Europas. Europa bietet den Völkern militärischen Schutz (Sicherheit), gesunde Nahrung, gute Bildung und hat alle Voraussetzung, um im 21. Jahrhundert ein lebenswerter Kontinent zu bleiben.    
  
Die öffentliche Debatte ist gleichzeitig verrutscht. Es dominieren negative, ängstliche und destruktive Erzählungen. Krieg, Migration und Wirtschaftsprobleme machen den Bürgern Angst und die Demokratie wird in jedem westlichen Land angegriffen.   
  
Der persönliche Dialog mit der Familie, Freunden und Kollegen wird immer schwieriger — sich offen zu zuhören und auszutauschen wird zu einer Kunst, die immer seltener wird. Diskurse sind oftmals stark polarisiert (Filterblasen) und wir schaffen es weniger oft Verständnis oder Übereinkunft zu erreichen.   
   
Machen Teile der Gesellschaft wirken auf mich müde, resignierend, zynisch oder teilweise auch hasserfüllt.   
  
Mir fehlt es an frohen Botschaften, Erfolgen, die wir zusammen feiern, progressivem Wandel und der Hoffnung, dass wir es zusammen in Zukunft besser machen können.

## 1172. A fence does not solve the drug problem

Yesterday I did a short cycling trip with my partner. Afterwards, we went to a great Falafel place to grab lunch. The place is close to a local park that is known for the drug abuse happening there. It was the first weekend of spring, quote sunny and not freezing cold anymore. Outside the park there were a lot of dealers hanging around. And then we passed a place where there were many people consuming. I haven't seen an open drug scene such as this before. I know there park and I regularly see people, marked by drug abuse and sleeping rough, asking for money which I often give them. But this scene was quite shocking to me - there were children and families lounging in the sun and playing inside the park while outside really broken people were struggling with the consquences of addiction. Local government has built a fence around the park and they're closing it at night to keep out the drug scene. But I think this is not a security but rather a social issue. These people won't go away just because they're being locked out. They will go somewhere else.

## 1176. bad management

I had an experience where my role was cut from the budget, and I was notified that very day that it would therefore be my last day. To be clear this was a part time gig, with irregular hours. But to be cut off immediately and lose access to internal systems - without a chance to communicate with colleagues with whom I'd already scheduled appointments - felt unprofessional, and damaging to my professional reputation. The manager wished to send an email saying the role had been cut from budget to those people, but only at my request, and would not allow me to do it because he wanted to control the message. There was no professional courtesy or trust, and the suddenness created a sense of self-doubt, and that there was something more to it. It will service mostly to raise more questions than answers. It was a bad experience in the society I'm now in, as they then gave me paperwork to say I can't say anything negative about the organisation or this process, if I want my tiny severance. ## 1188. AI and the Return of Interdisciplinary Thinking

As a child, if my grandfather couldn’t answer a question I asked, he would take an encyclopedia off the shelf. “You don’t have to know everything. You just have to know where to look it up,” he always said.  
I still think that way today. The internet and Wikipedia were a huge step forward. But now we have AI. That is another order of magnitude entirely.  
I run a small business and use AI, for example, to help me draft difficult customer emails or to troubleshoot software problems. At the same time, I have been writing a speculative novel for several months. I discuss ideas and background research with AI, even at two in the morning. The topics range from sodium-ion battery storage and global medical care to architecture, Inuit storytelling traditions, or a swarm of solar reflectors at Lagrange Point 1 between Earth and the Sun. I also use it to explore and develop the psychological profiles of my characters.  
Before AI, this kind of research would hardly have been possible for me. Gene Roddenberry, for example, had an entire network of experts for Star Trek: physicists, engineers, doctors, linguists, even military advisers. I have AI. Scientific knowledge today is often highly specialized and wrapped in technical jargon, which makes it difficult for non-experts to access. This problem also exists across disciplines. Much of our knowledge is organized in what one might call Aristotelian drawers. In practice, universal scholars hardly exist anymore, and this is where AI can help.  
If you use AI as a discussion partner, it can function like a cognitive interface between scientific fields and different worlds of thought. It helps to think more systemically, to recognize connections, and to develop ideas that emerge when knowledge from different areas comes together.

<u>Original title (de)</u> : AI and the Return of Interdisciplinary Thinking

## 1192. Occupational discrimination against people with neurodivergence

As a neurodivergent person with autism and ADHD, I frequently experience discrimination in the workplace. Out of fear of not getting the job, I conceal my condition during the application process, which also means I receive no support. Consequently, I can never address problems related to my neurodivergence in the workplace. Three years ago, I voluntarily resigned after bullying from my supervisor brought me to the brink of burnout. There is no established framework for dealing with neurodivergence in the job market, and therefore no guidelines for employers.

<u>Original title (de)</u> : Berufliche Diskriminierung von Personen mit Neurodivergenz

<u>Original content (de)</u> :

Als neurodivergente Person mit Autismus und ADHS erlebe ich häufige Diskrimierung in beruflichen Zusammenhängen. Aus Angst, die Stelle nicht zu bekommen, verschweige ich die Problematik in Bewerbungsprozessen, erhalte so jedoch auch keine Unterstützung. Probleme, die im Zusammenhang mit meiner Neurodivergenz auftreten, kann ich deshalb im Arbeitsumfeld nie ansprechen. Vor drei Jahren kündigte ich eine Stelle freiwillig, nachdem mich Mobbing meines Vorgesetzten an den Rand eines Burnout getrieben hatte. Es gibt keinen geregelten Umgang mit Neurodivergenz auf dem Arbeitsmarkt und daher auch keine Vorgaben für Arbeitgeber.

## 1205. Climate shelter -  missed opportunity

I live in a quiet street with lots of trees in a busy area of Barcelona with two traffic heavy roads around me. My street has two small pavements, two lanes occupied by car parking spaces, and two lanes for traffic (there is barely any traffic, just destination traffic). The street was approved to be peatonalised in 2024 however no budget has been allocated since so the works have not started. There is a lot of talk in Barcelona about to  have more "climate shelters" and my street is exactly that. Because of the trees it is notably cooler in summer but the street cannot be utilised for that purpose at the moment as the pavements are narrow and there are no benches to sit down on. It would be an ideal place for people to sit down, rest, walk. I recently tried to get more information from the city council about a status update on when the works will start but that was not easy at all. I received standard responses that were frankly not very helpful for a somebody not familiar with the ins and outs of the town council´s working. I am frustrated by the fact budget has not been allocated and that there is such a disconnect between a project being approved and budget allocated. I don´t know how to get this project moving as it seems stuck in some bureaucratic loop I don´t fully understand.

## 1208. Tipping point

I live in a large EU city and have a dog. When I meet with other dog owners, and we always talk about restaurants or weather, keeping the conversation  light and superficial, to be polite, to not delve into religious, political or moral controversy, while our dogs run around. No one really pays attention to how people are being treated in my country, only how my country interacts on the world stage and if it affects EU politics, but I felt that it was important to raise that people are being persecuted, that human rights and federal laws are being challenged, as ultimately, in a democracy (any democracy,including those in EU) it is the people that are going to need to speak up for change.   
  
After this, the next times we met, I saw that people in the group were more aware and concerned about my country and me and perhaps more conscious of the impact a local slide of human rights in one country could have on them, as well, in their country. I felt a non-partisan, non political shift towards more concern, more unity, more desire to be a player in protecting all of our rights in this little local community group.

## 1209. The missing track

Where I live has been without a railway for 50 years. It was suspended for reconstruction and then moved elsewhere. In the meantime, the entire area has grown exponentially: the population has doubled, the number of buildings has increased, and no new roads have been built, so its absence has been greatly felt (today we all travel by car, and buses aren't enough).  
20 years ago, they thought about building a tram that would lead to the subway: they built the road and raised the funds. Everything was going well until the new Province was elected, the municipalities changed mayors, and the regional representatives began arguing over where to put it. The result was that the funding was lost, and the tram was never built. Even today, you either have a car or walk, because buses aren't enough.

<u>Original title (it)</u> : Il binario che manca

Nel posto dove abito manca da 50 anni una ferrovia. Fu sospesa per rifarla e poi fu spostata altrove. Nel frattempo tutta la zona è cresciuta oltremodo, è raddoppiata la popolazione, sono aumentati i palazzi, non sono state fatte nuove strade e quindi la sua mancanza si è fatta sentire molto (oggi ci muoviamo tutti con l'auto e gli autobus non bastano).  
20 anni fa pensarono di fare un tram che portasse alla metropolitana: costruirono la strada e reperirono i fondi. Tutto stava andando bene fino a quando non fu eletta la nuova Provincia, i comuni cambiarono i sindaci e i rappresentanti regionali iniziarono a litigare su dove farla arrivare. Il risultato è che furono persi i fondi e non è stato più fatto il tram. Ancora oggi o hai un'auto o vai a piedi, perché gli autobus non bastano.

## 1214. Can AI automate consumer research? and what would happen then?

Over the past couple of years I've been doing freelance projects for a startup that uses AI to do consumer interviews.   
  
Two years ago the tool was cool, but made a lot of mistakes - and in general I could question whether it actually added any value over doing it without AI (other than the fact that you could do the interviews much faster). Besides, it still required a lot of manual work, so I did not feel at all like it would replace my role in running the consumer interview studies.  
  
Nowadays the tool has improved a lot - and a lot of the manual work I used to have to do is gettign automated effectively. So I am starting to think about whether it coulkd eventually fully replace my work. And also whether if AI can do cosnume rresearch autonomosly that would enable it to automatically aalsocome up with new product ideas for consumers and use that to generate revenue it cna then use for other goals (a scenario contemplated in some doomer AI scenarios)

## 1217. abolish preferential medication

I have had a negative experience with the pharmacy. More and more medication is preferred, which means that the health insurer determines which drug I can use and from which manufacturer. They assume that all drugs containing the same substance, from any manufacturer, work the same way. This is not the case. This has long been scientifically proven, but the health insurance, and therefore government policy, determines this, not the doctor anymore. Now there is a way out, and that is for the GP or specialist to indicate a medical necessity on the prescription. But if the GP does this too often, he and the pharmacist face a financial penalty: a discount on their rates. The GP is therefore indicating that they are only willing to do it if it is life-threatening. Becoming nauseous from a drug is not life-threatening, so too bad for the patient. So I can get the right drug, but it is not reimbursed (even though it is also cheaper than the drug they recommend). I think the government should intervene here. The same applies to the free choice of doctor, which they want to abolish in the coming years, meaning people will no longer be able to choose who their doctor is. As if it is unimportant who the doctor is, just as unimportant as whether you get sick from a medication. The only solution is to pay for it yourself, because that is actually the only reason they make these choices this way.

<u>Original title (nl)</u> : afschaffen preferente medicatie

<u>Original content (nl)</u> :

Ik heb een negatieve ervaring met de apotheek. Steeds meer medicatie is preferent, dit wil zeggen dat de zorgverzekeraar bepaalt welk middel ik kan gebruiken en van welke fabrikant. Ze gaan ervan uit dat alle middelen die dezelfde stof bevatten, van elke fabrikant, hetzelfde werken. Dit is niet zo. Dit is al veel langer wetenschappelijk aangetoond, maar de zorgverzekering en dus het beleid van de overheid bepalen en niet meer de arts. Nu is er een uitweg en dat is dat de huisarts of de specialist een medische noodzaak zet op het recept. Maar als de huisarts dit te vaak doet krijgt hij en de apotheker financiele straf, een korting op hun tarief. Huisarts geeft dus aan dat ze het alleen willen doen als het levensbedreigend is. Misselijk worden van een middel is niet levensbedreigend dus jammer dan voor de patiënt. Ik kan dus het juiste middel wel krijgen maar het wordt dan niet vergoed (terwijl het ook nog goedkoper is dat het middel dat zij adviseren). Ik denk dat de overheid hier kan ingrijpen.  
  
Ditzelfde geldt bij de vrije artsen keuze, die willen ze gaan afschaffen komende jaren, waardoor mensen ook niet meer kunnen kiezen wie hun arts wordt. Alsof het onbelangrijk is wie de arts is, net zo onbelangrijk als of je ziek wordt van een middel. De enige oplossing is zelf betalen want is eigenlijk de enige reden dat ze deze keuzes zo maken.

## 1218. Moment of simplicity

This afternoon, returning home, I had a wonderfully simple experience, one that gave me a profound sense of well-being. After leaving the chaos of Florence and navigating my usual public transportation journey (amidst sudden arguments and tensions now ignored by general indifference), I finally arrived at my station. Despite the rain, I didn't even open my umbrella; I got in my car and headed toward the reserve where I live. Upon arriving, I felt like I was entering paradise: flowers, greenery everywhere, and no sound except the patter of rain on the leaves and the birds singing. Since I didn't have my keys and no one was home, I waited outside for half an hour: it was a moment of unexpected pleasure.

<u>Original title (it)</u> : Momento di semplicità

<u>Original content (it)</u> :

Oggi pomeriggio, rientrando a casa, ho vissuto un'esperienza splendida nella sua semplicità, capace di regalarmi un profondo senso di benessere. Dopo aver lasciato il caos di Firenze e aver affrontato il consueto tragitto sui mezzi pubblici ( tra liti improvvise e tensioni ormai ignorate dall'indifferenza generale ) sono finalmente arrivato alla mia stazione. Nonostante la pioggia, non ho nemmeno aperto l'ombrello; sono salito in auto e mi sono diretto verso la riserva in cui vivo. Al mio arrivo, mi è sembrato di entrare in paradiso: fiori, verde ovunque e nessun rumore, se non il picchiettio della pioggia sulle foglie e il canto degli uccelli. Poiché non avevo le chiavi e in casa non c'era nessuno, ho aspettato mezz'ora all'aperto: è stato un momento di una piacevolezza inaspettata.

## 1222. The hope of a passage

In the final years of my working life, I drove 50 km every day to get to the office where I worked as a sales executive for a company specializing in telecommunications systems and business consulting.  
I had the habit of stopping at the bar for breakfast before arriving at the office after this long, about 60-minute journey.  
One morning, I arrived earlier than usual at this only bar in the CIS (Central Information and Communications Center) in Nola. At the door, I met a friend's sister. I had noticed her because she was nervous and worried about being late. She told me that every day she traveled from Naples to her job at CIS by public transportation, which took about two hours. The bus stopped at the bar, and from there she had to wait for a colleague or someone else who kindly offered her a ride. That day, I happened to be on her way, and after having a coffee together, I accompanied her to her office, which was not far from the company headquarters where I also went every day.  
Of course, from then on, I looked for her every morning and occasionally ran into her.

<u>Original title (it)</u> : La speranza di un passaggio

<u>Original content (it)</u> :

Nell'ultimo periodo della mia vita lavorativa, tutti i giorni percorrevo 50 km in auto per raggiungere l'ufficio dove svolgevo la mia attività di funzionario commerciale in una società che si interessava della realizzazione di impianti di telecomunicazioni e consulenza aziendale.  
Avevo l'abitudine, prima di arrivare in ufficio dopo questo lungo viaggio di circa 60 minuti, di fermarmi al bar per fare colazione.  
Una mattina arrivo prima del solito in questo unico bar del CIS di Nola, sull'uscio incontro la sorella di una mia amica, l'avevo notata inquanto era agitata e preoccupata per il ritardo che aveva, mi racconta che tutti i giorni raggiungeva da Napoli il suo posto di lavoro al CIS con i mezzi pubblici impiegando circa due ore, che la fermavano fino al bar e da lì doveva sperare in un passaggio di un collega o qualche altra persona che gentilmente le offriva un passaggio. Quel giorno mi trovai io sulla sua strada e ,dopo avere consumato un caffè insieme, l'accompagnai al suo ufficio che che si trovava poco distante dalla sede dell'azienda dove anche io tutti i giorni mi recavo.  
Ovviamente da quel momento tutte le mattine la cercavo e qualche volta mi capitava di incontrarla.

## 1231. University for students, not students for university.

My student life is very difficult to describe in black and white. Not that there's anything positive or negative in general; it's more of a gray area, a mix.  
  
I've certainly developed a critical approach to scientific disciplines, I've developed a scientific reasoning method, and I've certainly felt enriched both personally and culturally, BUT very little professionally.  
  
My expectations of university and the Italian education model were dashed. I expected an approach to learning and teaching that would connect with students, that would make them experience learning almost as if it were a hobby to be cultivated, allowing them to USE the knowledge and concepts acquired in their everyday lives.  
  
Unfortunately, I instead observed an extremely theoretical teaching model (too theoretical, in my opinion) that veers into mere factuality. To quote a quote I read on Quora from an Erasmus student in Italy: "Italian students must be memory athletes." It seems that rote learning is at the heart of education, but this choice has caused me deep pain because it's a learning method I reject.  
  
Even on the negative side, it must be said that these forced choices have allowed me to grow, mature, and develop my skills.  
More than experiencing university, I'd say surviving it.  
  
I've received a lot of support from my friends and colleagues throughout my education; humanity and emotional support have certainly been a fundamental factor in allowing me to move forward despite the many pressures of society.  
Every time they ask you how many exams you have left, how long it takes you, or if you're "behind" the average, it's a stab in the back, a wound inflicted, sometimes unconsciously and without malice. However, there are those who do it with malicious intent, and very often they are those with whom I share the same ship.  
  
Personally, I know that a human being cannot be judged by a grade or their performance in exams. Knowledge is a journey, logic is a path that must be traveled at each student's own pace. In this sense, the university doesn't approach the student; rather, the student must struggle to approach the university, almost as if he or she were chasing it.  
As an aspiring engineer, I know that measuring a physical quantity with absolute precision is pure fantasy, pure idealism.  
For this, I must thank some of my professors who distinguished themselves by adopting an alternative teaching approach that I recognized myself in.

<u>Original title (it)</u> : Università per gli studenti, non gli studenti per l'università.

<u>Original content (it)</u> :

La mia vita da studente è un qualcosa molto difficile da descrivere in termini di bianco e nero. Non che ci sia qualcosa di positivo o negativo in generale, diciamo che è più un grigio, un miscuglio.  
  
Ho sviluppato sicuramente un approccio critico alle discipline scientifiche, ho sviluppato un metodo di ragionamento scientifico, e mi sono sentito sicuramente formato sia a livello personale che a livello culturale, MA molto poco a livello professionale.   
  
Le mie aspettative su cosa sia l'università e il modello di istruzione italiano sono state infrante, mi aspettavo un approccio all'apprendimento e alla didattica che si avvicinasse agli studenti, che gli facesse vivere l'apprendimento quasi come se fosse un hobby da coltivare facendo UTILIZZARE le conoscenze e le nozioni acquisite anche nella sfera del quotidiano.  
  
Purtroppo ho potuto osservare invece un modello di didattica estremamente teorico (per me eccessivamente teorico) che sfocia nel nozionismo fine a se stesso, citando una frase che ho letto su quora di uno studente Erasmus in Italia : "gli studenti italiani devono essere atleti della memoria". Sembra che l'apprendimento mnemonico sia al centro dell' istruzione, questa scelta mi ha fatto soffrire nel profondo poiché è un metodo di apprendimento che rifiuto.  
  
Anche nel negativo però c'è da dire che queste forzature mi hanno permesso di crescere, di maturare e di sviluppare le mie capacità.  
Più che vivere l'università, direi più sopravvivere l'università.  
  
Ho ricevuto tanto supporto dai miei amici e dai miei colleghi nel mio percorso formativo, sicuramente l'umanità ed il supporto emotivo è stato un fattore fondamentale che mi ha permesso di andare avanti nonostante le molte pressioni della società.  
Ogni volta che ti chiedono quanti esami ti mancano, quanto ci metti o se sei in "ritardo" rispetto la media è una coltellata, una ferita inferta a volte anche inconsciamente e senza malizia. C'è pero chi lo fa con cattivo intento e molto molto spesso sono coloro con cui condivido la stessa nave.  
  
Personalmente so' che un essere umano non può essere giudicato da un voto o dalla sua performance agli esami. La conoscenza è un percorso, la logica è un itinerario che va percorso ognuno con i suoi tempi. È in tal senso che l'università non si avvicina allo studente ma è lo studente che deve avvicinarsi a fatica all'università, quasi che debba rincorrerla.  
Da aspirante ingegnere so' che misurare esattamente una grandezza fisica nella sua più totale esattezza è un puro vaneggiamento, pura idealità.  
In quanto a questo devo ringraziare alcuni miei professori che si sono distinti per usare un approccio didattico alternativo in cui mi sono riconosciuto.

## 1232. Story of a student who dropped out of school in Naples

University student life in Naples is ambivalent, at least in my case as a student who hasn't completed their course of study: there's no stigma attached to being one, but there are many small, indirect things, especially financially, that make you feel uncomfortable.  
University fees, first and foremost, require a certain level of academic achievement that isn't easy to achieve, if only because it's set at a value unattainable by taking a full number of exams: either you take x and stay below that number, or you take x+1 and go way above the threshold. The result is that for some time now, despite being in a tax-free area, I've been paying a fair amount of money that theoretically, by definition, I couldn't afford.  
Even services like the cafeteria become paid for as a student who hasn't completed their course of study; and as long as it's a one-time thing, it's feasible (especially compared to the cost of a full meal without cafeteria), but for a student who wants to attend regularly, the cost can be significant.  
Regarding transportation, our region offers very discounted passes for students, but they also depend on age. Wouldn't it be better to make them depend solely on enrollment and ISEE (Equivalent Economic Situation Indicator)? Is it wrong to be a student after a certain age?  
  
Regarding the university as an institution, here too we're dealing with ambivalent relationships: over the years, I've seen excellent professors, capable of inspiring you to be passionate about the subject and even understanding you (last year, for the first time in my life, I heard a professor say he perfectly understood the difficulties of studying); but also terrible professors, who habitually mock students, even casting doubt on their careers, passing this off as "candor" and "sincerity."  
Regarding the courses, a direct extension of the professors, here too we're dealing with some very stimulating courses, and others truly poorly managed.  
Finally, exams come at the price of a certain amount of freedom in their organization: if an overly rigid organization would limit their purpose (I took an experimental exam last year that allowed me to demonstrate my knowledge infinitely better than all the other theoretical and practical exams I'd taken in previous years), today we're faced with a slew of possible formats, from multiple-choice tests to mini-theses.  
Furthermore, I had the misfortune of enrolling during a period in which, shortly thereafter, the Study Plan was changed, thus canceling several courses that I would now have to take as exams, and at a time when mandatory prerequisites were still blocking university careers, which forces me down certain challenging paths.  
  
When it comes to attendance, the problem is related to the origins of those attending the faculties: it's certainly not possible to have a faculty in every municipality of every country, but on the other hand, there's no efficient transportation system. It's very difficult, and sometimes even expensive, to attend university to study together, thus preventing the group study that would be an important part of learning.  
In my specific case, moreover, not only was I unfortunate enough to see my study group disintegrate shortly thereafter, with several changing faculties, but the change in the Study Plans facilitated the diaspora of those who were in my year and who, perhaps, are still studying at university today, preventing us from grouping together.  
  
Finally, universities, as buildings, require a partial reevaluation of their spaces: some are being renovated, while others have remained in pitiful condition for thirty years; and there's a lot of filth. In particular, in the study rooms there is an ancestral shortage of chairs still in good condition: among dirty, broken, and legless chairs, rather than sitting at a desk we simply camp out.

## 1240. Research: precarious progress

I'm a PhD student at Federico II University.  
The research center where I work has nothing to envy; we're packed with tools. But there's another side to the story: the staff is always in precarious employment. This is due to how research works: the university doesn't fund it directly; research funding is requested in the form of grants (a call for proposals that allocates funds from third parties). This creates a problem: a portion of the money goes toward tools, resources, and staff, but projects have deadlines. So, once the years are up, you have the tools, but you have to lay off the staff. Thus, PIs (personal investigators) prefer to buy equipment with those funds and constantly rotate researchers, creating precarious employment. Thus, you squeeze the PhD student and postdoc as much as possible, while the newly hired researcher hopes to be legally established at the end of the project.  
In my research group, we have all the tools we need and trained staff; this fosters healthy competition in research, but for other groups, this isn't the case. Some find themselves traveling long distances to use a tool another lab has, and always being available to work beyond their scheduled hours.  


<u>Original title (it)</u> : Ricerca: progresso precario

<u>Original content (it)</u> :

Sono un dottorando all'università Federico II.  
Nel centro di ricerca dove lavoro non abbiamo nulla da invidiare, siamo pieni di strumenti. Però c'è l'altra faccia della medaglia; il personale si trova sempre in condizione di precariato. Questo è dovuto a come funziona la ricerca: ovvero l'università non finanzia direttamente, i fondi di ricerca li chiedi sottoforma di Grant (un bando di ricerca che assegna i fondi provenienti da parti terze). Questo crea un problema, una quota dei soldi va in strumenti, elementi e personale, ma i progetti sono a scadenza. Perciò finiti gli anni, gli strumenti li hai, ma il personale lo devi licenziare. Così succede che i PI (personal investigator) preferiscono comprare attrezzatura con quei fondi e fare un cambio continuo dei ricercatori creando un precariato. Così succede che il dottorando e il post-doc lo spremi fino a che possibile, mentre il ricercatore appena assunto spera di essere messo in regola a fine del progetto.  
Nel mio gruppo di ricerca abbiamo tutti gli strumenti che ci servono e personale preparato, questo spinge ad avere una sana competizione nella ricerca, ma per altri gruppi non è così. Alcuni si trovano a fare lunghi spostamenti per utilizzare uno strumento che un altro laboratorio ha, e ad essere sempre disponibili a lavorare anche oltre lo stabilito.

## 1241. Is AI an indispensable tool for surviving university?

I'm a PhD student at the 1st University of Campania.  
I never had any problems studying or passing exams during my degree, but I've always noticed many of my colleagues having serious difficulties. It's been two years since I graduated. Now I'm a researcher and I also share a teaching position with a professor at the university. As a teacher, I'm now beginning to understand the difficulties students face. They're truly under pressure, forced to study enormous amounts of theoretical knowledge. It's true that I never had any problems as a student, but I can't help but consider that since I was a child, I've always had an unusually great memory and reasoning ability that I've rarely seen in other people. Therefore, I think my lack of difficulty in graduating is more of an exception.  
The course I take focuses primarily on the practical application of the theory students study with the other professor, and when I have free time after my lecture, I offer to help them with anything they didn't understand from the previous theory lecture.  
Something happened recently that got me thinking about this.  
After class, lunchtime had begun, and I saw the students in my class rushing together to solve a problem on a theoretical proof that the theory professor had assigned them as practice for the exam. I tried to solve it quickly, but to no avail.  
Amidst the general distrust, one student tried several times to solve the problem with AI, and by the fifth time, she had succeeded.  
I read the solution the AI ​​provided, and it was, indeed, surprisingly correct.  
Curious, I asked them how often they use AI to study.  
They replied that they use it very often, especially after theory classes, where, unfortunately, the professor isn't very good at explaining the topics well during the two hours of daily class.  
This really shocked me. Is it possible that our university curricula are so full that, in the end, a machine is more efficient than a teacher at optimally explaining a topic?  
Perhaps they should be redesigned to make them more effective for the average human being, rather than just for people with higher-than-average cognitive abilities. And perhaps AI could help with this by improving the quality and comprehensibility of lessons, and possibly streamlining them.

<u>Original title (it)</u> : L'IA strumento indispensabile per sopravvivere all'università?

<u>Original content (it)</u> :

Sono una dottoranda della 1° università della Campania.  
Non ho mai avuto problemi nello studiare ed a superare gli esami durante il mio corso di laurea, ma ho sempre notato tantissimi dei miei colleghi avere grandi difficoltà. Sono passati 2 anni dalla mia laurea. Adesso sono ricercatrice e condivido anche una cattedra con una professoressa dell'università. Da docente adesso inizio a comprendere le difficoltà che hanno gli studenti. Sono veramente messi sottopressione, obbligati a studiare gigantesche quantità di nozioni teoriche. È vero che non ho mai avuto problemi quando ero studente, ma non posso non considerare che fin da bambina ho sempre avuto una inusuale grande capacità di memoria e ragionamento che raramente ho riscontrato anche in altre persone. Perciò penso che il mio non aver avuto difficoltà nel laurearmi sia più un eccezione.  
Il corso che seguo è principalmente sull'applicazione pratica di ciò che gli studenti studiano di Teoria con l'altra professoressa, e quando c'è tempo libero dopo la mia lezione mi offro nel dare loro una mano su ciò che non hanno capito della lezione precedente di teoria.  
Ultimamente è capitato qualcosa che mi ha fatto riflettere a riguardo.  
Finito di fare lezione, era scattata l'ora di pausa pranzo e ho visto gli studenti del mio corso aggregarsi di fretta tutti assieme per risolvere un quesito su una dimostrazione teorica che la professoressa di Teoria ha assegnato loro come allenamento per ciò che uscirà all'esame. Ho cercato di risolverlo velocemente ma senza successo.  
Nella sfiducia generale una studentessa ha provato più volte a risolvere il quesito con l'IA e alla quinta volta ci era riuscita.  
Lessi la risoluzione fatta dall'IA ed era, in effetti, sorprendentemente corretta.  
Incuriosita chiesi loro quante volte capita che usino l'IA per studiare.  
Mi risposero che la usano molto spesso, soprattutto dopo le lezioni di teoria dove purtroppo la professoressa non è molto capace nello spiegare bene gli argomenti nelle 2 ore di lezione giornaliere.   
Questo mi ha scosso molto. Possibile che i nostri piani di studi universitari sono così pieni che alla fine è più efficiente una macchina rispetto ad un docente nello spiegare in maniera ottimale un argomento?  
Forse sarebbero da rifare per renderli più efficaci per un essere umano medio invece di per sole persone con capacità cognitive più spiccate della norma. E in questo forse l'IA potrebbe aiutare migliorando la qualità e la comprensibilità delle lezioni, e se possibile snellirle.

## 1250. Volt can only thrive if we also take an active role within civil society

My thoughts after our meeting:  
  
Volt Europa aims to unite, mobilize, support, and empower people who share the same European dream in order to make that dream a reality. Part of this dream is democratic cooperation. This should be one of the pillars of Volt Europe.  
  
At the same time, the question is how we can unite and mobilize people who share this European dream. My answer is: it does not really matter how we do it, as long as we do it (provided it is ethically responsible). This can happen through politics, businesses, supporting grassroots initiatives, but also through civil society organizations.  
  
During the last municipal elections, I noticed that the success of local parties was largely driven by civil society. In fact, local political parties themselves emerged from civil society organizations. They are especially successful because of their high degree of organization and their extensive networks (including business networks) — something that generally cannot be said about grassroots movements.  
  
My philosophy is that Volt can grow and create more impact if its members start taking on relevant positions within civil society, while at the same time remaining actively involved in politics and grassroots initiatives.

## 1254. Disintermediation and participation

Put shortly, disintermediation. The EU Commission and many MEPs keep talking about speed. We need to make decisions faster. We need to get rid of veto. We need to take this decision now. We need the United States of Europe. But how do we make decision-making faster without sacrificing participation? Honestly, I didn't have time (and taste) to read more than a few comments on the EUPP and I didn't find time to read candidate's answers. I also don't know whether a limit to veto instead of abolishing it has been considered? A veto without consequences is a power that corrupts. I'm not sure no veto is the solution. The EU Commission has sped up its "competitivness" packages - Omnibuses, by getting rid of real public participation and copying industry proposals. We need to slow down. We stand for participation so we should fight for it even when it makes things messier and longer.

## 1255. Volt needs to become the model of the democractic space we want for Europe

I joined Volt because it's building a Europe-wide movement that seeks to engage citizens in European politics. I have worked the past 25 years on strengthening local governments to become more inclusive, more responsive locally, and more influential (inter)nationally, so in a way Volt has been made for me.  
I love the community organisng methods used by Volt in it's early days. I love the possibility of local action where government fails, of activism to bring attention to causes that are overlooked. I love the idea of bringing experience and best practices from one country to the next.  
However, more recently I have noted, from speaking with new Volters. that this love for Volt is note a shared story anymore. It pouzzles me. We started out almost 10 years agoto do politics differently: to be collaborative over competitive, to be connected with citizens, not distant, to come together, net "exit".  
I tried building connections with European civil society, with European media, wiht start-ups who make happen what we stand for, but such partnerships are often frowned upon. We facilitate coalitions with likeminded local parties, and some accuse us of "diluting Volt's identity".  
Sometimes I don't recognise the Volt I joined 8 years ago. We have become a reflection of our polarised society, not the model for European collaboration.  
We have shine 29, our strategy, but i miss us coming together around shared European projects that can be influential and impactful because they unite us in all our diversity. Everything turns around winning elections, but how can we win elections without Volters? We need more Volters, not just voters. I'm afraid we will just become like any other european party, with the only difference being that we have one program. We are not rooted enough in our societies. Where is the European democratice space we aimed to create?

This young guy was running within an independent list. He has is own personal website, he has been active quite a while in promoting young people careers in his region. Seemed aligned with Volt’s values, but….  
I checked and rechecked his website and Facebook page…. No mention of Volt anywhere. How is that possible? Why I had not heard about him before? this is an example of lack of transparency all round.

## 1264. Dancing in the dark

Why do we even need a new way of doing politics?  
I am a volunteer in an European team that is supposed to be providing services to many stakeholders in our movement,. Until recently I felt I did not know these stakeholders, never met them, do not know their names, what they do, what their daily priorities are, and what they expect from our team.  
I am working to gather these info through contacts with people who provide similar services in the national chapters or other team leaders - there is always a way if one takes the initiative - but it shouldn't be like that.  
  
Before this EU experience, I was working within a Volt Chapter for a mayoral election campaign in a big city, and Volt Europe was totally absent, both ideologically and practically.   
  
I feel there should be a much more natural, organic integration between EUR and chapters, the EUR service providing teams should be in close, unintermediated contact with our stakeholders and clients and vice versa.  
What we already have: competence and passion. What we need: a slimmer, simpler EUR structure, easy integration mechanisms between EUR and chapters. Where do I see myself in this process: as part of a strong, empowered team plugged in to our stakeholders' needs.

## 1265. Partner with civil society and knowledge organisations

To day I attended the European and national community leads call. The partnerships team was presenting their approach to doing politics differently.  
  
first they map a topic using a mindmap. It's great because you can update as your topic evolves. Some European communities also have a mindpad like this. One starts with the EP policy mission, and develops areas of work from there.   
  
The next step would then be to identify organisations working on these topics already. Make a network map and get connected, ideally via people already known to Volters in your community. Look into the organisations carefully, go step by step, start with small activities, and when things get serious: do due dilligence! the partnerships team can help.  
  
proceed with understanding the dynamics in the network - who is influential? Who do theyu work with? Considering the network, what can really be strategic partners for Volt?  
  
The "explorer's guide to Volt's Way of doing politics" - in Volt has more practical tips.

## 1267. How We Block Ourselves from Better Outcomes

Recently, I noticed how often our society operates on a kind of zero-sum logic: for someone to gain, someone else must lose. I experienced this in a situation where collaboration could have created value for everyone, but instead people defaulted to protecting their own position, leading to inefficiency and missed opportunities.  
  
What struck me is that this mindset seems deeply embedded—not just in economics, but in how we think, communicate and organize ourselves. It makes systems feel unnecessarily rigid and sometimes even counterproductive, while the potential for more cooperative and mutually beneficial outcomes is clearly there.  
  
Regarding question 1.2: it relates to almost everything.  
  
Regarding question 3: those aren't actual binaries, related to this matter.

## 1271. The challenge of Individuality

My partner and I were arguing about something. It got pretty heated. Eventually everything was said and we went quiet.   
  
After some time things normalized again.   
  
The challenge here is to be able to express once opinion without the hazard of loosing a relationship.   
  
Our society claims to be democratic but as soon as it comes to deviating points of view, especially in friend- or partnership people can react very irritated and quickly consider ending the connection. I think in many cases we are too judgemental to be real democrats.   
Just because an opinion doesn't fit within the typical modern canon shouldn't make us cut connection. For as long as we are able to air our points of view, stand for what we feel is right we have won. If our view prevails is subject to the democratic process. Especially within the party.   
Nobody looses if their opinion doesn't prevail.   
You only loose if you didn't get the chance to express it.
